title: Senior UI Designer
description:
We are currently looking for a highly skilled UI Designer to join our team and help enhance the visual appeal and user-friendliness of our interfaces. At Jisr, we strive to deliver exceptional user experiences, and as a UI Designer, you will play a crucial role in achieving this goal. Working closely with our Product Designers, UX Researchers and Frontend Engineers, you will have the opportunity to contribute to the development of a cutting-edge user interface that sets us apart from the competition.

In this role, you will have the responsibility of maintaining and enhancing our existing design system, micro-interactions and the interface overall, ensuring that our products are consistent and of the highest quality. We are looking for a creative and detail-oriented individual who is passionate about creating innovative and intuitive designs.

• Collaborate with Product Designers, UX Researchers to understand user needs and translate them into innovative and visually appealing designs

• Create wireframes, mockups, and prototypes to communicate design direction and interactions to stakeholders

• Conduct usability testing and gather user feedback to refine and improve designs

• Collaborate with the development team to ensure the successful implementation of the designs

• Maintain and enhance the design system, including UI components, style guides, and patterns

• Ensure consistency and quality across all products and platforms

• Proven experience as a UI Designer with a strong portfolio showcasing your work.

• Proficiency in design tools such as Figma, or Principle.

• Familiarity with design systems and atomic design principles.

• Understanding of responsive design principles.

• Excellent communication skills and ability to articulate design decisions.

At Jisr, you’ll enjoy a welcoming and casual environment, company retreats, and the ability to interact with and learn from a growing Startup. We work hard and care about our most prized asset - our people.

We aim to make people management faster, efficient, and simpler, in order to allow organizations to invest employees' time on what matters, and focus on growing the business. Our vision is to become the MENA region's leading People Management Platform.

We’re data driven and never stop iterating. If you’d like to work in a supportive, entrepreneurial environment, are interested in building something meaningful and having fun while doing it, we’d love to hear from you.

title: 3D Environment Artist & Level Designer
description:
3D Environment Artist & Level Designer
ScapeWorld Entertainment · Remote

•
Level: Senior to lead

•
Location: Remote, CET overlap

•
Contract: Full time, long term

About us

We are ScapeWorld Entertainment, a fully remote Swedish game studio of just over 20 people. We are building Scape, a platform of multiplayer games where a player’s identity carries across all of them. We have just launched our first game within Scape. Our senior team has shipped and run live games at studios including Arrowhead (Helldivers 2), Avalanche Studios and Ubisoft.

The project

Our next game is a cleaning and restoration sim set in a shared neighbourhood. Every player has a place of their own that starts buried in junk and grime, and puts it in order in full view of neighbours who are doing the same.

Cleaning games are usually played alone or in short co-op sessions. We want to make one set in a neighbourhood that players share and keep coming back to, and we want to do it well. We have a working prototype and are refining the loop now. If you play games like this and have views on what makes them satisfying, you will enjoy this.

About the role

We are looking for a senior to lead 3D environment artist who is also a level designer.

You will be the only level designer on the project. You own the game’s spaces, from first layout through to dressed and lit, and you are responsible for delivering them.

The role is split roughly evenly between environment art, mostly props and other environment 3D assets, and level design, which includes some gameplay design. On the design side you work with our Creative Director and engineering, and you bring your level and gameplay design experience into those discussions. On the art side you work with the rest of the art team.

You report to the Art Director.

What you will do

Environment art

•
Model and texture props and other environment 3D assets. Most of what we use is made in-house, and we also work with asset packs where they fit.

•
Work to our polygon, texture and material standards. Assets used in large numbers, such as foliage, are kept low poly. Most props use standard poly counts.

•
Build modular kits that can be reused across levels.

•
Dress and light levels in Unity, following the Art Director’s visual direction.

Level design

•
Design the layout of rooms and plots: how the player moves through them, what they notice first, and the order in which the space is revealed as it is cleared.

•
Greybox levels and take them through to final, checking scale, pathing and collision in engine.

•
Test levels in engine and in playtests, and make changes based on the results.

•
Help shape how spaces support the game loop and its features, and give input on pacing and progression.

•
Document your work: layout plans, kit guides and dressing guidelines.

What we are looking for

•
Senior to lead level, with several years of professional experience in game development.

•
Experience as both an environment artist and a level designer. You have done each on at least one project, shipped or not, and you have owned a game’s spaces or levels from start to finish.

•
Some gameplay design experience, for example working on game loops, features or mechanics alongside level layouts.

•
A portfolio that shows both sides: real-time environments and 3D assets you made, and levels you designed, from greybox to final.

•
Good working knowledge of Unity, including building and lighting levels. Our level tools are built inside Unity.

•
Comfortable using Blender. It is part of our production pipeline, and we have built an add-on for it.

•
Comfortable using the Substance suite for texturing and materials.

•
Comfortable giving your view in design discussions and explaining your reasoning.

•
Able to work independently from a brief, and to work closely with a small team.

•
Comfortable working in English every day, in meetings (mostly on camera) and in writing. It does not need to be perfect.

Nice to have

•
3D character or gameplay animation.

•
3D character modelling.

•
Technical art or VFX.

•
Experience with GitHub or Fork.

•
Experience with player-built levels, or tools for game creators.

•
Experience in a small team where you covered more than one role.

What we offer

•
A fully remote team with flexible working.

•
Trust to manage your own time. We do not use timesheets.

•
Ownership of the game’s spaces, from first layout to final.

•
A small team where people help each other.

Working setup

•
Fully remote. Your working day needs to overlap with CET.

•
Full time, on a long-term contract. It is business to business.

•
We would like you to start as soon as you are available.

What this role is not

•
Not a lead game designer role. Our Creative Director sets the direction of the game.

•
Not an art-only or design-only role. You will do both.

How to apply

Apply through the link; a few short questions are part of the application form. If we shortlist you, the next step is interviews, and for final candidates an unpaid planning task of about two hours at an agreed time, with no modelling or texturing. We reply to everyone at every step.

Disclosure

This application will be evaluated with the help of an AI tool that checks your CV and application against the criteria for this role. A human recruiter always makes the final decision. The AI does not reject or accept anyone on its own. If your application isn’t taken forward, you can ask us for an explanation of how the AI was used in that decision. Our big, hairy, audacious goal? Help bring 150 life-changing medical innovations to patients who need them by 2034. And everyone on our team is deeply committed to the cause with team tenure ranging from four years to eleven years!

Projects frequently involve translating technical concepts, clinical data, and product information into clear and engaging visual storytelling.

Responsibilities include designing and animating motion graphics sequences, building data visualizations, developing typography-driven animations, and adapting graphics to align with client brand systems.

You’ll work closely with producers, editors, and clients to explore visual approaches that are clear, elegant, and strategically aligned with client messaging. Many of our projects require balancing strict brand guidelines with creative problem solving, and we value artists who can push design forward while maintaining brand integrity.

Because we are a small, specialized team, your contributions will have a direct impact on the quality and clarity of our storytelling.

Job Description:

Seize your opportunity to make a personal impact supporting the Case Management Modernization (CMM) Program. The CMM program is an initiative to support the Administrative Office of the US Courts (AO) in developing a modern cloud-based solution to support all 204+ federal courts across the United States.

GDIT is your place to make meaningful contributions to challenging projects and grow a rewarding career. The UI/UX Human Centered Design Specialist ensures dashboards, reporting tools, predictive analytics screens, and AI/ML interfaces are intuitive, accessible, and aligned with Judiciary user workflows, supporting the CMM Data Modernization and Governance team in delivering data-driven decision-support tools in alignment with strict federal compliance requirements.

This role supports the Reporting, Analytics, and Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML) deliverables by shaping user-centered visual designs for the Reporting & Analytics Capability and the Measurement Definitions and Decision-Support Package. By applying human-centered design (HCD) best practices to visualizations, navigation patterns, and decision-support experiences, this role enhances adoption and interpretability while ensuring designs meet Section 508, WCAG 2.1 AA, and federal digital service standards for accessibility, performance, and security.

The UI/UX Human Centered Design Specialist will execute the following responsibilities:

Reporting & Analytics

• Design intuitive, accessible dashboards, self-service reporting interfaces, and predictive analytics screens for the CMM Reporting & Analytics Capability, applying Human-Centered Design (HCD) and usability best practices.

• Translate UX research, personas, and journey maps into high-fidelity prototypes, wireframes, and interface design specifications for development teams.

• Partner with BI Architects, data engineers, product owners, and developers to align visual designs with data models, KPIs, and reporting requirements.

• Conduct usability testing, including heuristic evaluations, card sorting, and A/B testing, on dashboards and visualizations, and apply findings to refine designs each sprint.

• Define and maintain visualization, navigation, and interaction design standards to ensure reports and dashboards are consistent, interpretable, and support adoption.

• Design the user experience for the Measurement Definitions and Decision-Support Package, ensuring metrics and KPIs are presented in a clear, decision-ready format.

• Evaluate designs for Section 508 and WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility compliance across all reporting and analytics interfaces.

• Support rapid prototyping and iterative validation of dashboard and reporting designs within Agile sprint cycles.

• Drive user adoption of dashboards and reporting tools by aligning navigation patterns and visual hierarchy with Judiciary user workflows.

• Contribute standardized UI components and templates to the shared CMM design system for reuse across reporting products.

AI/ML Capabilities

• Design intuitive, explainable interfaces for AI/ML-driven predictive analytics and decision-support features, ensuring model outputs are interpretable to end users.

• Apply HCD principles to the presentation of AI/ML model outputs, confidence indicators, and recommendations to support responsible AI adoption.

• Collaborate with AI/ML and data science teams to translate model capabilities into user-facing workflows aligned with federal responsible-AI requirements for transparency, fairness, and risk mitigation.

• Conduct usability evaluations of AI/ML interfaces and incorporate feedback into iterative design refinements.

QUALIFICATIONS

• MA/MS degree, or Bachelor's/Master's degree in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), Design, or a related field, with 10+ years of general experience in information systems and 8+ years of specialized experience in UI/UX design, including 5+ years in a Human-Centered Design (HCD) role supporting enterprise or government applications.

• Experience may be considered in lieu of degree as follows: HS (16+ years), AA/AS (14+ years), BA/BS (12+ years), Doctorate Degree/Ph.D. (9+ years).

• Expertise in usability testing methodologies, such as heuristic evaluations, card sorting, and A/B testing, and proficiency in design and prototyping tools (Figma, Sketch, Axure, Storybook, or similar).

• Strong understanding of Agile/SAFe delivery, iterative design integration, and DesignOps/UX governance practices.

• Familiarity with HTML5, CSS3, and responsive UI behavior to collaborate effectively with front-end developers.

• Experience designing for federal systems, with practical knowledge of Section 508 and WCAG 2.1 AA compliance.

COMMUNICATION & ORGANIZATIONAL

• Excellent presentation and communication (oral and written) skills.

• Consultant mindset with the ability to work with high level customer stakeholders and build excellent customer relationships.

• Experience identifying and applying industry tools, solutions, methods best practices, and emerging technologies.

• Strong analytical skills and problem-solving skills with the ability to formulate and communicate recommendations for improvement.

• Demonstrated ability to work effectively, independently, and as part of a team.

CERTIFICATIONS (Preferred)

• Certified Usability Analyst (CUA) or Certified HCD Professional

• SAFe Agile Practitioner (SPC or SSM)

• Section 508 Trusted Tester Certification

• UX Design or HCD Certification (NN/g, IDEO, or HFI)

The Role

The Associate Creative Director (ACD) role marks transition from senior individual contribution into holistic creative leadership. It reflects a high level of trust, ownership, and influence—both within our internal teams and across our global client accounts. As an ACD, you remain a practitioner at heart, staying deeply involved in the craft while taking command of creative direction, high-stakes client stewardship, and team mentorship.

Beyond project execution, this role requires a shift in mindset toward representing Active Theory as a future leader. You are expected to champion the studio’s vision and values, acting as an ambassador for our both internally to the team and externally to the broader industry.

Core Responsibilities

Creative Ownership

•
Take creative ownership of one or more core client accounts, ensuring consistency, quality, and clarity across engagements.

•
Set and maintain creative direction across projects — from early concept through execution.

•
Be accountable for the overall creative health of the work, not just individual deliverables.

Craft Champion

•
Be practiced in core creative competency – you should be intimately familiar with creative execution at the highest level

•
As needed, be hands-on with conceptual and delivery phases of the creative process

•
Understand the possibilities, limitations and potential within 2D/3D motion design

Partnership Leadership

•
Act as a creative point of continuity for assigned client accounts.

•
Build trust through taste, follow-through, and thoughtful decision-making.

•
Collaborate closely with Production and Tech to shape approaches that balance ambition, feasibility, and craft.

New Business & Growth

•
Step into a creative lead role on pitches and new client opportunities articulating our unique perspective. Help shape concepts, narratives, and presentations that reflect Active Theory’s point of view.

•
Contribute to how we position our creative capabilities externally.

•
Act as a primary ambassador for Active Theory starting to build a public-facing leadership profile (e.g., through industry events or thought leadership).

Team & Studio Leadership

•
Lead by example through craft, communication, and collaboration.

•
Demonstrate being AI native and generally interested in AI

•
Provide direction and feedback that helps elevate designers and strengthen the work.

•
Contribute to creative standards, systems, and ways of working that scale across the studio.

•
Foster a design culture and support in department process and initiatives

What Success Looks Like

Summary

•
The work feels cohesive, intentional, and confidently directed.

•
Partners experience clarity, consistency, and trust in creative leadership.

•
Designers feel supported, challenged, and elevated.

•
Creative leadership is proactive — identifying opportunities, not just responding to briefs.

Growth Path (ACD → CD)

•
As an Associate Creative Director, you’re building toward full Creative Director scope by:

•
Continued demonstration of high craft and quality

•
Build taste and sense of innovation within the department and cross functionally

•
Expanding ownership across multiple partnerships

•
Increasing influence on studio-wide creative direction

•
Leading larger pitches and long-term strategic narratives

•
Developing others into leaders, not just strong contributors

•
Demonstrating moving from 'leading the work' to 'shaping the future of the studio' through strategic public representation and studio-wide influence.

• Good communication and collaboration skills

• Experience using AI tools to accelerate design work and improve workflows

Nice to have

• Experience with design audits and design-to-code workflows

• AEC/BIM domain experience

• Motion design and micro-interactions

• Basic understanding of HTML/CSS

Where You Will Make the Difference

• Contribute to the evolution and maintenance of the design system, including components, patterns, tokens, and documentation

• Own and improve assigned design system components and patterns throughout their lifecycle

• Support design system adoption and consistency across product teams, working to the adoption approach set by the design system lead

• Participate in Design QA and design reviews to identify visual inconsistencies, incorrect component usage, and gaps between design and implementation, then log, triage and follow those issues through to a fix with engineering

• Identify and help reduce design debt and UI inconsistencies across the product

title: Senior Motion & Graphic Designer
description:
Silverback Strategies is a performance marketing agency built to help marketers grow and capitalize on change. Ad Age, Inc Magazine, The Washington Post, The Washingtonian, and The Washington Business Journal have recognized Silverback as one of the best places to work.

We hire the best and help them get better. Silverbackers are supported, challenged and inspired by their peers. Regardless of title or tenure, every Silverbacker plays a role in helping our agency get better. This is a place where you can make a difference.
What you will do:

• Translate strategy into visuals: partner closely with our Creative Strategist to take research, hooks, and loose creative briefs and turn them into concrete visual concepts, storyboards, and finished assets
• Produce both statics and video: design and build static ad creative and edit/produce short-form video and motion content for paid social at a consistently high craft level
• Interpret brand guidance at any altitude: work from anything ranging from a thin one-pager to a comprehensive brand system, and reliably produce creative that's unmistakably on-brand either way
• Navigate regulated-industry review cycles: produce creative that anticipates compliance and legal scrutiny, minimizing revision rounds and rejection risk without watering down creative quality
• Push brands into new creative territory: identify opportunities to evolve a brand's creative expression to unlock scale and new-market growth, while staying inside brand-safety guardrails
• Select and edit raw footage/imagery: review raw photography and video footage from shoots and select, crop, cut, and edit the strongest material into finished assets — no on-set creative direction required
• Own asset quality and turnaround: deliver polished, client-ready work with minimal internal revision cycles so assets aren't burning days internally before they even reach the client
• Maintain visual consistency at scale: keep creative consistent and on-brand across a high volume of ad variations, formats, and platform

What we are looking for:

Core Experience
• 5+ years in a hands-on creative production role — Art Director, Senior Designer, Creative Producer, or similar —with dedicated performance/paid social experience
• A portfolio that shows range across both static design and video/motion editing, ideally for paid social specifically
• Experience working within brand guidelines of varying depth and translating them into new creative applications
• Experience in regulated or highly regulated industries (healthcare, finance, insurance, legal, or similar) is a strong plus, given our client base
• Experience working in matrixed organizations with multiple stakeholders and layered approval processes

Craft & Technical Skills
• Expert-level proficiency in Figma (or similar) for static design and layout
• Strong proficiency in After Effects (or similar) for motion graphics and video editing
• Comfortable editing raw video/photo footage into finished assets: selects, cuts, pacing, captions/graphics overlays
• Working knowledge of Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator) as needed
• Understands platform-specific creative specs and best practices across Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Pinterest, and other paid social channels

Creative & Strategic Judgment

• A strong eye for what "good" looks like in modern performance advertising — thumb-stopping, polished, and effective, not just pretty
• Understands performance/paid-social fundamentals (hooks, pacing, hierarchy, CTAs) well enough to make smart creative calls independently, without needing to run the strategy
• Can take a loose brief or visual direction and fill in the gaps with sound creative judgment
• High attention to detail — typos, brand misapplications, and spec errors don't make it to client review
• Comfortable giving and receiving fast, iterative feedback in a deadline-driven environment

Working Style
• Thrives on speed without sacrificing polish — this role owns production timelines that need to move fast to offset long approval cycles
• Collaborative by nature; sees the Creative Strategist as a partner, not a hand-off point
• Self-sufficient in production; doesn't need heavy oversight to get from brief to finished asset

What success looks like:

• Assets consistently reach client/compliance review in 1–2 internal revision rounds or fewer
• Creative reliably passes compliance and legal review with minimal rework
• Output balances brand safety with creative freshness — clients see growth and new territory, not just "more of the same"
• The Strategist and Senior Performance Creative function as a true two-person creative engine, each covering what the other doesn't

What This Role Is Not:

• Not a photo/video shoot creative director — you won't be expected to run or direct live shoots, just to select and edit from what's captured
• Not a pure strategist — research, testing frameworks, and reporting live with the Creative Strategist, not this role

Make an impact: We’re a small agency. Everybody has the opportunity to drive change and impact

We’re early, funded and moving fast. Joining Entity at this stage is a rare opportunity to help shape our company and our mission. We are an AI-native business; embracing the latest technologies and tools is essential to being successful with us.

About the role

This is a hands-on senior role with real ownership of your work. You'll be the core designer on the Entity brand, evolving it and keeping it consistent as the team grows. You'll design the visual creative for our 2027 launch, across player campaigns, social content, brand idents and motion. You'll also design marketing for the developers and publishers we work with, from pitch decks and case studies to a partner toolkit, and show their games in a way that keeps Entity recognisable. Beyond digital, you'll create booth graphics, print and merchandise for industry events.

Where it genuinely helps, you'll use AI to support and enhance our creative workflows, always thoughtfully and with care, and help shape how Entity approaches AI in its creative work. For us, AI is a tool that supports human creativity, never a replacement for it. As an early member of the team, you'll own projects end to end, build things from scratch and help define what Entity becomes.

You'll report to the Art Director, who sets overall creative direction and signs off major brand decisions.

Key responsibilities

• Brand: Evolve the Entity brand (logo use, colour, type, imagery and tone) and maintain the guidelines that keep it consistent as more people use it.

• Launch: Design the visual creative for our 2027 launch across player and partner campaigns, and brief and coordinate external studios and freelancers when needed.

• What makes Entity different: Find visual ways to show full-scale games that start in seconds in the browser, with no downloads or installs. This is the heart of our story, and you'll help tell it.

• Brand idents: Create animated logo stings, intro and outro cards, and video title and end slates.

• Player campaigns and social: Design player campaigns and promotions (seasonal sales, featured collections, platform events) and always-on social content, with templates that keep recurring posts quick and on brand.

• Partner games: Showcase partner games inside Entity-branded promotions, combining assets that developers supply with our own look so the platform stays recognisable.

• Developer and publisher marketing: Design marketing for partners, from pitch decks and case studies to a partner toolkit with "Play on Entity" badges and co-marketing templates.

• Events and merchandise: Design booth graphics, decks, printed material, t-shirts, hoodies and giveaways, with print-ready files for suppliers.

• AI-assisted design: Use AI thoughtfully to support your workflow, for example to explore early concepts, build mood boards or speed up repetitive tasks like resizing and format variants, while the core creative stays yours.

• Measurement: Review how campaigns perform and use what you learn in the next round.

Requirements

• 5+ years of graphic or visual design experience, in-house or agency, focused on brand and marketing work for both consumer (B2C) and business (B2B) audiences.

• A design degree or equivalent practical experience; your portfolio matters more than your qualifications.

• A portfolio showing strong ideas and clean execution across social, digital, print and motion, with a sharp eye for typography, hierarchy, colour and layout.

• Strong motion design and video editing skills for short-form content, promos and brand idents, using After Effects, Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve or similar.

• Expert use of Adobe Creative Cloud (Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign) and Figma.

• Experience developing or maintaining brand guidelines and keeping work consistent across many channels and contributors.

• Working knowledge of social and paid platforms: formats, specs, safe zones and what performs on each.

• Hands-on experience using AI tools thoughtfully in your workflow, with the judgement to know where they help, where they don't, and how to keep output on brand.

• Cultural and aesthetic awareness: you follow design and visual culture closely and can explain why current trends work.

• Comfort working in an early-stage company: you own projects end to end, manage your own workload, juggle fixed deadlines and build things from scratch.

• Clear communication: you can present and defend your work, and give and take feedback well.

Nice to have

• Experience in the games industry, or a genuine interest in games and the communities around them.

• Experience branding a platform, marketplace or app, especially one serving two audiences.

• Experience launching a new brand or product from scratch.

• Experience creating co-marketing or partner toolkits that other companies use.

• Performance creative experience: designing ad variants and learning from test results.

• Deeper experience with generative image, video and motion tools (e.g. Adobe Firefly, Runway), or building repeatable AI-assisted production workflows.

• Illustration or 3D skills (Blender, Cinema 4D).

• Experience guiding or mentoring junior designers.

Working Conditions

Entity is remote-first, but this role is only open to candidates based in the UK or Ireland, with a suitable home-working setup. We value autonomy, clear ownership, and outcome-driven work. Some flexibility in working hours is expected to support collaboration across the team. Occasional travel may be required for team sessions, industry events, or visits with development partners.

title: Digital Product Design Lead
description:
About Bobbie

Bobbie makes European-style organic infant formula manufactured end-to-end in the U.S., because we believe every parent deserves to feed their baby with confidence, without judgment and without compromise. No mystery ingredients. No shortcuts. Just clean, thoughtfully made formula that parents can trust.

But Bobbie has never been just a formula company. When the 2022 national infant formula shortage left parents across the country unable to feed their babies, we closed our storefront to new customers rather than leave a single existing family without formula. We went to Washington. We got loud. And we opened our Heath, Ohio manufacturing facility to make sure something like that could never happen again.

That's who we are, and that's what you'd be joining.

Bobbie for Change

Our advocacy arm, Bobbie for Change, exists because making great formula isn't enough if the systems around parenthood are still broken. We fight for paid federal parental leave, push for legislation to prevent future formula shortages, advocate for feeding equity, and support families navigating impossible situations, including donating formula to parents impacted by breast and gynecologic cancers through the Bobbie Breasties program.

We're a company that genuinely believes becoming a parent makes you an activist. The people who work here feel that too.

The Role

We’re looking for the person who wakes up every day thinking about how to make the Bobbie experience better, and who partners closely with Product, Lifecycle, Creative and Development to make it happen.

You’re obsessed with our customers and driven by insight. You’ll be the voice of parents in every design decision. You’ll spend as much time understanding them (what confuses them, what worries them, what makes them stay or leave) as you spend in Figma, and you’ll turn that understanding into clear problem statements, sharp prioritization and well-crafted experiences.

You’re proactive. You don’t wait for a brief. You spot friction in the data, in support tickets or in a usability session, and you bring the problem, plus a point of view on how to solve it, to the table before anyone asks.

You’ll lead and rebuild our in-house UX/UI function, setting the standards, workflows and design culture the rest of the team builds on. You’ll own our design system and Figma hygiene end to end, starting with a new foundation, and bring personalization into the subscriber journey.

What You’ll Do

Lead the in-house UX/UI function

• Act as Bobbie’s in-house UX/UI lead. Set the design vision, quality bar and ways of working as we rebuild the function.

• Establish and evangelize UX/UI best practices, accessibility standards (WCAG) and design workflows across the product organization, staying current with industry trends and emerging tools.

• Direct our ongoing UX/UI agency partner: set priorities, give clear creative and quality feedback, and raise the bar on their work.

• Mentor designers and contractors, and be the go-to design partner for leadership.

Design across the subscriber journey

• Design wireframes, prototypes and user flows to communicate ideas. Identify and fix UX/UI issues across the conversion funnel: homepage, product, cart and checkout pages.

• Partner with Product Managers and Lifecycle Marketing to shape the subscriber journey, designing key moments across it: signup, plan management, billing, feeding-stage transitions, save flows, cancellation and winback.

• Bring design and customer insight to personalization, working with Product and Lifecycle on experiences that adapt to each family’s stage and needs, onsite and throughout the subscription.

Build and own the design system

• Own Bobbie’s design system end to end. Start by auditing it and rebuilding its foundation so the team can move faster without losing quality.

• Develop and maintain design systems, style guides and UI patterns for consistency across mobile and web, with a mobile-first approach to visual design.

• Own Figma file hygiene and design system integrity (components, tokens, documentation and naming conventions) so the system stays scalable and easy for any collaborator to pick up.

Research and validation

• Plan and run qualitative and quantitative research (usability testing, subscriber interviews, funnel and behavioral analysis) to validate design decisions and improve conversion, retention and satisfaction across the subscription funnel.

• Turn what you learn into clear problem statements and bring them to Product as opportunities, not just design requests.

• Run competitor analysis, gather user feedback and use A/B testing to keep improving design and usability. Always look for new ways to remove friction from our UX.

• Keep Bobbie’s parent community at the core of the UX, designing the subscription journey around their needs, feedback and voice.

Cross-functional collaboration

• Creative: Partner hand in hand to align user experience, visual identity and brand voice, translating brand direction into interfaces that feel unmistakably Bobbie.

• Platform: Work with designers, Product Managers and Engineers early and often to validate technical feasibility, scope tradeoffs and make sure designs ship with fidelity across mobile and web.

• Lifecycle: Design cohesive experiences across owned channels (email, SMS, web) that reduce churn, increase reactivation and support parents through every stage of their subscription.

• Brand and Product Marketing: Partner with Brand on brand and commercial strategy, and with Product Marketing so the subscription experience supports go-to-market priorities and stays true to Bobbie’s positioning.

Project and process leadership

• Clearly explain and justify design decisions, breaking features down into MVPs that deliver immediate value.

• Set clear timelines for UX/UI deliverables, managing dependencies and blockers while leading projects through the design phase.

What You Bring

•
Customer obsession you can show. A portfolio where you can point to the customer insight behind each decision and what you learned after launch, not just the final screens.

•
Proactive problem-solving. Examples of problems you spotted and pushed forward yourself, and the outcome they drove.

•
Strategic rigor. You frame problems clearly, weigh tradeoffs against business goals like conversion and retention, and hold your own in roadmap conversations with Product and leadership.

•
Experience leading a design function. You’ve built or led an in-house UX/UI practice: setting standards and workflows, directing agencies or contractors, and mentoring designers.

•
Senior craft. Deep UX and UI skills across web and mobile, expert Figma skills, and experience building scalable design systems.

•
Personalized, data-driven design. Experience designing personalized or data-driven experiences, and using data to shape decisions and measure results.

•
Relevant experience. Significant product design experience, ideally in DTC subscription, membership or other recurring-revenue products. Mobile-first design experience is strongly preferred.

•
Clear communication. You can tell the story behind a design decision to any audience.

While Also Being

• Passionate — about what we are doing.

• Proactive — can take initiative to get things done.

• Curious — love learning and staying on top of emerging trends.

• Excited about working at an early-stage startup — where you may end up doing all kinds of things!

Bonus points

• Health, baby/parenting, or CPG/ecommerce experience

• Familiarity with Recharge, Shopify, Klaviyo

Why This Role Matters

At Bobbie, design isn't decoration — it's the thing standing between a parent and their baby's next meal. Every flow you design determines whether a subscriber gets their formula on time, understands their options during a stressful moment, or feels supported through a feeding-stage change. This role sits at the center of Creative, Platform, and Lifecycle because the subscription experience only works when all three tell one consistent story.

You’re inspired by our core values:

• Be Radical - We are change makers, rule breakers and stigma shakers. We are unapologetically bold and use our megaphone for good.

• Nurture the Tension - Parenthood is full of healthy tension, and so is building a company. We embrace the unknowns, practice humility and are a culture of learners.

• Deliver Ounce by Ounce - Our customers have entrusted us to feed their babies. We lose sleep over the details, so they don’t have to.

• Don’t Assume - We embrace our unique perspectives, withhold judgment, and find beauty in the paths that brought us all to Bobbie. Our strength is celebrating each other and our collective voice.

Compensation and Benefits:

Compensation

Our salaries are based on paying competitively for our size and industry. For fully remote roles, we have a salary range per role that is differentiated based on geographic location (Group A, B, or C).

• Group A (SF/Bay Area, Seattle, NYC): $148,525 – $175,000

• Group B (Los Angeles, Chicago, Austin, Denver, Boston, Washington DC, San Diego, Philadelphia, Portland, Sacramento): $133,670 – $157,500

• Group C (All Other Cities): $126,245 – $148,750

Benefits

• Competitive stock options

• 401k with employer match

• Employee medical, dental, and vision insurance 100% covered by Bobbie, with options to add dependents through a subsidized pre-tax deduction

• US-based remote work model

• Flexible Time Off Policy (including Summer Fridays; half days on Fridays Memorial Day through Labor Day)

• 16 paid company holidays, plus an end of year holiday shut down

• 16 weeks of paid parental leave with the option to take an additional 8 months unpaid

• One year subscription to Bobbie

• $75 monthly internet stipend

• Co-working space reimbursement

At Bobbie, we are committed to building a diverse and inclusive company. We seek to create a culture where everyone can belong because we believe that people do their best work when they can show up every day as their authentic selves. We welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities, and perspectives.

Bobbie is an equal opportunity employer. We do not make hiring or employment decisions on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status or genetic information, in compliance with applicable federal, state and local law.

title: Langfuse - Product Designer
description:
Why Design at Langfuse

Your work will shape how engineers build with AI.

Langfuse is often the primary interface engineers use to debug, evaluate, and improve their LLM applications. The designs you ship will be used for hours each day by thousands of developers and non-developers. They'll tell you about it in GitHub issues, on X, and in our community Slack channels. Everything we build is open source (MIT-licensed) and immediately visible.

The design challenges here are genuinely hard. You're designing for technical users and business users alike who care about information density, speed, and precision. Traces contain dozens of nested LLM calls with massive prompts and completions. Users need to set up evaluators, manage prompt versions, configure integrations, and build monitoring dashboards before they even start analyzing results. You need to make both the setup and the daily use feel intuitive and easy.

You will also have direct exposure to how cutting-edge LLM applications are built. Deeply understanding the problems our users solve will make you a better designer and along the way makes you an expert on LLM engineering yourself.

You will grow at Langfuse by

•
Owning our product design end-to-end. You'll be the first dedicated designer at Langfuse. Today, our engineers design as they build, which has gotten us far, but we need someone who can elevate the entire experience. You'll own the design system, and visual language across the product. You'll set the standard for how Langfuse looks and feels.

•
Making data-dense interfaces intuitive. Langfuse surfaces traces, scores, costs, latencies, token counts, prompt versions, and evaluation results. You'll figure out how to present complex, nested data in ways that help engineers find what they need fast.

•
Simplifying complex workflows. Our users run evaluations across datasets, compare experiment results, manage prompt versions, and set up monitoring. You'll map these workflows, identify friction, and design flows that feel obvious in hindsight.

•
Collaborating directly with product engineers. You'll pair with engineers, whiteboard solutions together, and ship designs that work within our existing component system (shadcn/ui, Tailwind). You'll create reusable, consistent UI patterns that the whole team can build with.

•
Shipping design straight to code. You'll use AI coding tools to implement smaller design fixes, build components for the design system, and polish UI details yourself. We are not looking for a perfect engineer here but for someone who can help themselvesherself.

•
Experience in designing complex web applications, incl. a portfolio showcasing product work that users loved

You want to talk to users

Hard worker and thrive working in a small and accountable team

ML/AI experience or familiarity with the LLM tooling ecosystem

Former founder or early startup experience

Contributions to open source projects or design systems

Side projects that show craft and taste

Art direction skills and the ability to establish and maintain a strong visual direction.

title: PhD Researcher – Video Understanding & VLMs
description:
About Almetra

We build vision-language models that understand what happens on real factory floors. Cameras on 20+ production lines stream video into our models, which turn every step (assembling, screwing, inspecting) into structured data several times per second. Customers use it to see where time gets lost and how to improve their processes.

Your role

You’ll do your PhD with us from day one, working closely with Sascha, our Head of ML (VLM), on research problems that come straight from our product. Your research runs on real industrial video at a scale few academic labs have. The PhD is co-supervised by a university professor, and you’ll be enrolled at a partner university.

What you’ll work on

•
Video understanding with VLMs: action recognition, temporal grounding and long-video reasoning on factory footage

•
Making models robust in the real world: occlusions, unusual viewpoints, new stations and products with little labelled data

•
Turning research results into improvements in our production models

•
Publishing at top venues (CVPR, ICCV/ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR) together with our ML team

What you bring

•
Master’s degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, AI or a closely related field, with a focus on computer vision or multimodal learning (finished or finishing by early-2027)

•
Solid deep learning foundations and hands-on PyTorch

•
Experience with computer vision, video or multimodal models (thesis, projects or internships)

•
Curiosity about real-world problems, not only benchmarks

•
Fluent English

Nice to have

•
First publications or a strong thesis in vision-language, video understanding or multimodal learning

•
Experience with open VLMs (e.g. Qwen-VL, InternVL, LLaVA) or video models (e.g. VideoMAE, ViViT)

•
Training on GPU clusters (DDP / FSDP)

Why a PhD with us

•
A full-time, paid PhD position in Berlin

•
Mentoring from our Head of ML plus academic co-supervision

•
Unique real-world video data and the compute to use it

•
Your research reaches a real product, not just a paper

What we offer

Employee Share Options Program for all permanent employees*

An increasing benefits list: currently includes Urban Sports club and quarterly team retreats.

Be on the forefront in defining what artificial intelligence means in manufacturing

Gain hands-on experience in working in an AI-first software company

Supportive and inclusive culture that values diversity and promotes the advancement of underrepresented groups within the company

Collaborate with a diverse (currently more than 10 nationalities) and talented team, working on cutting-edge projects with real-world impact

Network with professionals and leaders in the field, opening doors to potential future career opportunities

We have a very flat hierarchy, open 360° feedback, and flexible working hours

Almetra is committed to creating a workplace that is diverse, fair, and inclusive. We encourage candidates from all backgrounds, even if they do not meet every qualification, to submit their application. Support pre-test thermal predictions in collaboration with thermal analysts.

Process and analyse test data to assess hardware and system performance against requirements.

Contribute to thermal model correlation and the investigation of discrepancies between predictions and test results.

Recommend design or test improvements and capture lessons learned.

Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Thermodynamics or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

3+ years of relevant experience in spacecraft thermal engineering, including thermal hardware development, integration or testing.

Hands-on experience contributing to thermal test campaigns, such as TVAC or Thermal Balance testing.

Good understanding of spacecraft thermal control hardware, such as MLI, temperature sensors, heaters and fluid loop components.

Familiarity with spacecraft qualification and acceptance processes, requirements traceability and verification documentation.

Experience contributing to hardware development or supplier follow-up, including reviewing technical documentation and tracking actions.

Familiarity with thermal instrumentation, data acquisition systems and test facility interfaces.

title: Product Design Manager
description:
The AI orchestration of your wildest imagination.

n8n is the open workflow orchestration platform built for the new era of AI. We give technical teams the freedom of code with the speed of no-code, so they can automate faster, smarter, and without limits. Backed by a fiercely inventive community and 500+ builder-approved integrations, we’re changing the way people bring systems together and scale ideas for impact.

Since our founding in 2019, we’ve grown into a diverse team of over 260 - working across Europe and the US, connected by a shared builder spirit and with our centre of gravity in Berlin. Along the way, we’ve:

•
Cultivated a community of more than 650,000 active developers and builders

•
Earned 190K+ GitHub stars, making us one of the world’s Top 40 most popular projects

•
Backed by top investors, from Sequoia’s first German seed to our SAP's recent strategic investment - bringing us to a $5.2bn valuation

That’s the company we’ve built. Now we’d love to see what you can build. If you’re applying, try n8n out - whether you’re technical or not - and share a screenshot of your first workflow with us. The easiest place to start is here: app.n8n.cloud/register.

We’re in a defining moment of an incredible journey. Come and build with us.

We're looking for an experienced design manager to lead our Product Design team.

This is a management role. Your job is to develop designers, raise the quality of the work, and make sure design has real influence on where the product goes. It is not a player-coach role, and it is not a step up for a strong IC looking for their first management position. We need someone who has already managed product designers and can do it well from day one.

n8n is a powerful, flexible technical tool, which means the problems your team tackles are complex. Design decisions have to account for diverse user workflows, technical constraints, and how changes ripple across the whole platform. You'll need enough craft depth to recognise excellent work, challenge it constructively, and help designers get better. The team needs a manager whose design judgment they trust.

You'll manage a team spanning product designers, design engineers and user researchers at a range of seniority levels, working across our product areas. You'll work alongside our other design manager. You'll report to our VP of Product until our Head of Design joins the team. That search is running now.

More than 80% of workflows built on n8n involve AI agents, and we're widening from a developer audience to a broader set of builders. That shift is the central design problem here, and your team is at the centre of it.

🎯 Your main goal is to build a Product Design team that consistently produces excellent work and shapes how n8n's product evolves. Here's what that involves:

Lead and develop the team

•
Run regular, high-quality 1:1s and coach designers, design engineers and researchers across different levels.

•
Own performance management: evidence-based reviews, honest feedback, and real support for anyone who isn't where they need to be.

•
Help people understand what's expected at their level and what growth looks like, evolving our progression framework for Product Design.

•
Hire excellent designers as the team grows, and broaden the range of backgrounds and perspectives on the team.

Raise the design bar

•
Set and hold a high standard across problem framing, user understanding, interaction design, information architecture and visual craft.

•
Facilitate design critiques and reviews that measurably improve the work, and help designers think beyond the feature in front of them.

•
Develop designers' judgment and autonomy rather than becoming the final approval layer for every decision.

Own the whole product experience

•
Keep a holistic view across features and product areas, identifying inconsistencies, recurring UX problems, and opportunities for more coherent patterns.

•
Work with the team to address fragmentation systematically rather than feature by feature.

Make design a real partner

•
Partner closely with Product and Engineering leadership so design contributes early to problem definition and product direction, not late to execution.

•
Help designers influence product decisions through strong reasoning rather than positional authority.

•
Improve how the team works across critique, collaboration, decision-making and knowledge sharing, introducing structure where it helps the team scale and resisting process that slows things down.

How much of this is hands-on?

Worth being direct, because it's the question every good candidate asks. This is a management role: developing designers, raising the bar, and making design count in product decisions is the job, and that's where your time goes.

You'll stay close to the craft in critiques, in reviews and in the detail of the work, and you'll occasionally pick up design work yourself. When that happens it sits outside the squads and varies with the period: an exploratory concept, a gap during someone's leave, a problem that needs a first pass. It is not a 50/50 split, and if what you want is to keep a squad's worth of delivery alongside managing the team, this isn't the role.

REQUIREMENTS

Must-haves

•
👥 Proven design management: You've managed product designers in a product-led technology company for 3+ years, with a team of five or more. This is not a first management role.

•
🧭 Running a team well: You've run effective 1:1s, evidence-based performance reviews and difficult feedback conversations, including with people who weren't performing. You've built or improved a career progression framework for designers, and you're comfortable with the administrative side of managing a team rather than treating it as overhead.

•
📈 Growing people: You coach and mentor, you run critique that changes the work, and you can point to specific designers who got measurably better or grew in scope while reporting to you.

•
🎨 Design taste and judgment: Your own craft is strong enough that designers trust your read on quality, you can articulate what separates adequate design from excellent design, and you'll step into the work directly when the situation calls for it.

•
🎯 Hiring: You've hired designers consistently well, you know where good design talent is and how to attract it, and you can tell the difference quickly.

•
🤖 AI fluency: You use AI tools hands-on in your own work and in how your team designs, and you have an informed view on designing AI-enabled products. AI agents are the product here, so this one is not optional.

Nice-to-haves

•
🛠️ Technical products: You've managed design teams in B2B SaaS, developer tools, workflow automation or similarly technical products.

•
🧠 Technical mindset: You don't need to write code, but genuine curiosity about what's happening underneath (APIs, webhooks, data structures, how workflows actually execute) earns you credibility with engineers here.

•
👩‍💻 Designing for developers: You've designed products for developers, technical operators or other sophisticated users.

•
🔭 Systems view: You can step back from individual projects to spot patterns and UX problems across a broader product experience.

•
🤝 Influence without authority: You bring Product and Engineering peers with you through reasoning rather than positional authority.

•
📊 Scaling teams: You've grown a design team through a period of rapid company growth.

•
🌍 Distributed teams: You've managed designers in remote-first or highly distributed organisations.

•
🔓 Open source: You've worked on open-source or community-driven products.

•
🌱 Inclusive hiring: You've meaningfully broadened the diversity of a design team through how you hire.

Our hiring process

We'll tell you the whole shape of it upfront, and there's very little homework.

•
Screening call with our recruiter. 45 minutes, no prep.

•
Leading designers with the hiring manager, 75 minutes. You'll present for 20 minutes on a team you built, grew or turned around. Reuse existing material; it shouldn't take more than two or three hours. We don't need case studies of your own design work.

•
Live critique and coaching, 60 minutes. We'll send you a real piece of n8n design work 24 hours ahead. You'll critique it, then have a coaching conversation with the designer who made it. No preparation beyond reading it and trying the product.

•
Conversation with our VP of Product, and a culture call with Jan, our CEO. 45 minutes each, same day where we can.

•
Meet two or three of the designers you'd be managing. Not scored; it's for you as much as for us.

We'll also ask for two references, one of them a former direct report. A portfolio is welcome if you have one, though we know not every design manager keeps theirs current.

Why join us?

At n8n, your work won't disappear into a slide deck. You'll lead design for a product that hundreds of thousands of builders use to automate real work, sitting right where developer tools, AI agents and no-code interaction models meet. The design problems are genuinely hard and largely unsolved.

You're inheriting an established team with strong designers, not building from zero, and there's real room to shape how the team coaches, critiques, grows and works with Product and Engineering, rather than inheriting a rigid design organisation. You'll stay close enough to the craft to influence quality directly, while your main job is making the designers around you better.

You'll join a fast-growing, Europe remote-first company where autonomy, experimentation, and craft matter, at the point where n8n is scaling from a beloved open-source project into a major B2B platform. Design's contribution to product thinking is established here, and has a long way still to run.

Sound like a challenge you're excited to take on?

Apply now and help us build the future of automation.

We can sponsor visas to Germany; for any other country, you need to have existing right to work.

Our company language is English.

You care about diversity and inclusion? We do too! Check out our Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging initiatives at n8n (https://www.notion.so/n8n/Diversity-inclusion-and-belonging-n8n-c1bec2fff536422d868b1a438d990e35).

Benefits

•

•

US: Multiple low-premium, low-deductible medical plans with coverage for individuals and families—plus a no-cost premium HDHP option with a pre-seeded HSA—along with dental and vision coverage.

Future planning 💰 –

Europe: We provide pension contributions according to local country norms.*

Europe: We provide benefits according to local country norms.*

Career growth 📈 – We hire rising stars who grow with us! You’ll get €1K (or equivalent) per year to spend on courses, books, events, or coaching to level up your skills.

A passionate team 🤩 – We love our product, and we prove it with regular hackathons where we see who can build the coolest thing with it!

Remote-first 🌏 – Our team works remotely across Europe, with regular off-sites for team bonding. Some roles, like sales in the US, are hybrid—please check the job description.

Dig into one of the most genuinely interesting UX challenges in the space: n8n has historically had a steep learning curve for new users. Your job is to lower that floor without losing the power that experienced builders love.

Drive design's strategic influence

•
Shape product strategy, not just respond to it. Bring design thinking into roadmap conversations and help surface user problems before they become someone else's brief.

•
Help lead n8n's expansion toward a broader, less technical audience, a deliberate and exciting strategic shift that design should be leading.

•
Build the kind of relationships with Product, Engineering, and leadership where design is a genuine thought partner at every stage.

Build and grow the team

•
Lead a team of around 14 designers today: 2 Design Leads each working with ~6 ICs, plus Design Engineering and UX Research (with more hires ahead).

•
Shape the team structure, career framework, and progression paths so people know where they stand and where they're going.

•
Create a culture of high standards and honest feedback, where people feel supported to do their best work and have a clear sense of what great looks like.

•
Own hiring and headcount planning for the department, and help us grow without losing what makes the team good.

Build research into how we make decisions

•
Establish a pragmatic, continuous research practice from the ground up. We're making our first dedicated UX research hires, so there's real room to shape this.

•
Make customer insight, product data, and community feedback a live input to product decisions, so teams are building from evidence at every step.

•
Connect research to the decisions that matter most: activation, adoption, retention, and helping new users find their way into n8n with confidence.

Help the team work in new ways

•
Champion practical AI adoption inside the design org, from prototyping and research synthesis to design QA and workflow efficiency.

•
Help the team stay curious and current as the tools, patterns, and expectations around AI products continue to evolve fast.

•
Model the kind of working style you want to see: thoughtful, adaptive, and genuinely excited about what's changing.

Requirements

Must-haves

•
🧭 Product design leadership: You have managed managers, coached senior designers, and built design teams that improve both craft and business outcomes, including making hard performance calls when needed.

•
🧩 Complex product systems experience: You have led design across complex or developer-facing products where UX quality depends on deep product understanding.

•
🎨 Craft authority: You are a quality bar, not just someone who appreciates quality. You can identify great work, explain why it's great, and hold the line on standards even when it's uncomfortable.

•
📣 Strategic influence, not just strategic thinking: You have made design a co-equal in product conversations, not a downstream function. You know how to bring people with you, create debate, and drive decisions.

•
🔀 Structured problem-solving under ambiguity: You find your way into unclear problems and create a plan. You don't just ask good questions, you answer them. You move forward when there's no map.

•
🤖 AI-era product judgment: You understand the AI, automation, or adjacent tooling landscape and can turn emerging patterns into usable, trustworthy product experiences.

•
🔍 Research literacy: You know how to build research into product development so insight becomes part of how teams make decisions, not a separate artifact.

•
📊 Data-informed decision making: You use product analytics, research, and customer evidence to guide decisions instead of relying on taste or opinion alone.

•
🧱 Org design and performance management: You can design team structures, define career paths, raise expectations, and handle difficult performance conversations with clarity.

Nice-to-haves

•
🌱 Open-source or community product experience: You have worked on open-source, fair-code, community-led, or builder-driven products and understand what it means to design for a community that has strong opinions.

•
💻 Design engineering credibility: You have enough front-end or design engineering fluency to partner deeply on design system adoption and implementation quality.

•
🌍 Remote-first operating systems: You have built design rituals, critique, QA, and collaboration practices that work across distributed teams and time zones.

•
🚀 Growth surface experience: You have worked on activation, onboarding, templates, time-to-value, or product-led growth surfaces.

•
⬆️ Rising Design Manager profile: We are open to someone who has been an exceptional Design Manager and is ready for their first Head-level role, if the fundamentals are exceptional.

Working at Atlassian

Atlassians can choose where they work – whether in an office, from home, or a combination of the two. That way, Atlassians have more control over supporting their family, personal goals, and other priorities. We can hire people in any country where we have a legal entity.

Responsibilities

Atlassian is used by teams around the world for everything from pizza deliveries to space travel. To help us achieve our mission of unleashing the potential of every team, the Atlassian Creative Team is looking for a Lead Designer to guide how our identity system evolves and scales across a growing portfolio and audience. We're looking for someone who pairs brand strategy and identity expertise with a deep understanding of how individual systems connect to create a brand. You'll be a hands-on player/coach who is actively on the tools and owning the quality of the work.

In this role, you'll

•
Shape and evolve the Atlassian brand system: its core elements, how it all scales, and the vision for where it goes next.

•
Lead brand systems projects from brief to delivery, directing designers, art directors, and copywriters and setting the creative bar for the work.

•
Be the main point of contact for leadership, clients, and agency partners. You'll align on goals, manage feedback, and keep projects moving.

•
Partner with other design teams across Atlassian so that our brand and product systems connect into one coherent experience for our customers.

•
Extend the brand into new territories, developing product and sub-brands alongside strategy, marketing, and product teams.

•
Turn the brand system into living, AI-ready guidance and tools that people and AI can both work from, so teams and partners can create on-brand work independently and quickly.

•
Shape how our team uses AI in brand work. Set the standard for where it belongs across concepting, production, and review, and protect quality as these tools become part of how work gets made.

On the first day, we'll expect you to have

•
8+ years of professional experience, with a portfolio of ambitious brand systems work and problem-solving at scale.

•
A track record of leading complex, multidisciplinary projects and directing other creatives toward a shared vision.

•
Deep expertise in the core elements of identity, including typography, color, layout, grid, hierarchy, iconography, and imagery. You bring a clear aesthetic point of view and an uncompromising eye for detail and quality.

•
Applied experience building and evolving design systems for brands, with a technical understanding of how they're implemented at scale. You know how type, color, and layout behave across print, web, product, and motion, and you can turn brand decisions into tokens, specs, and assets that teams and engineers can use.

•
Strong stakeholder and agency management skills. You build alignment, balance competing priorities, give clear creative direction, and earn the trust of leadership.

•
Fluency in Figma, Adobe Creative Suite, and Keynote, and hands-on experience with AI tools for generation, workflow building, and automation.

•
A considered point of view on AI's role in brand and creative work. You've used it in real projects, you can judge generated work critically, and you can guide a team on where it helps without lowering the bar.

•
A collaborative mindset: you seek out feedback, mentor others, and believe the best work comes from productive debate.

title: Senior Solar Design Engineer [Remote]
description:

About Us:

At EDF power solutions North America, the Distribution-Scale Power team is a leading provider of customized PV, BESS, and Substations in the United States, with a proven track record of developing over 1,600 MW of renewable energy capacity. We specialize in delivering efficient and cost-effective development, engineering, construction, and operations tailored for utilities, cooperatives, landowners, communities, and institutions, anywhere from 2-200MW+. With more than 20 years of industry experience, our collaborative team provides value at every phase of the project lifecycle, utilizing expertise in permitting, development, EPC, financing, QA/QC, and SCADA systems to offer comprehensive turnkey solutions.

Joining the DSP team means working on impactful projects in a fast-paced and efficient environment while contributing to the advancement of renewable energy in a diverse setting.

Be a part of an innovative and collaborative team environment that fosters our goal of delivering renewable solutions to lead the transition to a sustainable energy future.

Benefits & Perks:

EDF power solutions offers best-in-class employee benefits, including the following:

• Competitive bonus incentives. This position is eligible for our annual bonus program.

• Comprehensive health coverage. We provide low-cost health & wellness coverage for employees and their eligible dependents.

• Rewarding 401k. We provide a generous matching contribution.

We are also proud to offer:

• Favorable paid time off programs, including paid parental leave after one year of service.

• Rewarding learning & career development and advancement opportunities.

• Supportive mentorship & buddy programs.

Salary Range: The full pay range for this role is $107,200 to $178,600 annually, and the good faith estimated starting pay for this position upon hire is $128,00 to $150,00 annually. We generally base our salary decisions on factors including but not limited to, relevant work and leadership experience, education, demonstrated performance, internal equity, and in some cases, geographic location.

Scope of Job:

We are seeking an experienced, highly self-directed Senior Solar Design Engineer with a strong technical background in solar PV and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) who can take ownership of engineering deliverables and operate effectively with a high degree of autonomy.

This position requires a high level of working knowledge of the National Electrical Code (NEC), renewable energy electrical design, and industry design best practices. The successful candidate should be able to independently evaluate engineering problems, make sound technical decisions, identify design and constructability issues, and drive projects forward without requiring extensive day-to-day direction.

Our company operates in a fast-moving, deadline-driven environment with high expectations for technical quality, accuracy, responsiveness, and accountability. Project schedules can be aggressive and priorities may change quickly. The successful candidate must be comfortable managing multiple projects and competing priorities while maintaining the quality and attention to detail expected of professional engineering work.

Responsibilities

• Prepare engineering deliverables, including plan and elevation drawings, schematics, calculations, POs, and schedules in support of PV (photovoltaic) energy generation system design, for commercial and utility projects in the 500 kW to 20 MW scale. Review and revise engineering deliverables prepared by others. Develop designs in consideration of company safety program and OSHA safety requirements for construction and system operation.

• Conduct site assessments, prepare energy models and conceptual design deliverables in support of business development and new product/vendor integration.

• Communications with Project Managers, who coordinate scheduling and permitting for project execution.

• Create, organize, and maintain documents associated with projects’ basis of design throughout the project life cycle; assist the business development team in identifying key project design risks and enabling effective decisions.

• Implement strategies for integration of new tools, new products, new vendors, code changes, and best practices, and disseminate to internal departments as needed.

• Other duties as assigned.

Working Conditions: Most work time will be spent in an office environment, but occasional site visits may be performed. Significant time spent on the phone and working on computer.

Qualifications

Education/Experience

• Bachelor of Science degree in mechanical or electrical engineering required.

• Minimum of ten years’ relevant design experience, particularly including experience in designing mechanical or electrical systems or electrical systems for construction; commercial PV design preferred.

• Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) certificate.

• Registered Professional Engineer (PRE) preferred

• NABCEP certified

• Experience with industry standard PV systems and energy modeling tools.

• Application and interpretation of the NEC, applicable to PV, energy storage, interconnected power production sources, grounding and bonding, overcurrent protection, conductor sizing, and electrical equipment preferred.

• Experience with:

• Solar PV and BESS electrical system design, including DC and AC collection systems, inverter and PCS selection, transformers, switchgear, switchboards, and associated balance-of-system equipment.

• Medium-voltage electrical systems, including MV collection systems, feeder design, conductor and cable sizing, voltage drop, equipment selection, and system configuration.

• Development and review of single-line diagrams, electrical plans, equipment layouts, wiring and interconnection details, specifications, calculations, and construction/IFC drawing packages.

• Equipment ratings, available fault current, protection requirements, grounding, and coordination with system studies.

• Utility interconnection requirements and coordination with utilities, AHJs, equipment manufacturers, and other project stakeholders.

• Designing systems with consideration for constructability, equipment availability, cost, schedule, commissioning, and long-term operation and maintenance, rather than approaching engineering solely as a code-compliance exercise.

• Substation engineering experience is highly desirable, particularly experience with renewable-energy collector substations, MV/HV equipment, transformers, breakers, protection and control systems, grounding, relaying, and utility interconnection facilities.

Skills/Knowledge/Abilities –

Requires knowledge of:

• National Electric Code and other model codes

• Project management experience

• Computer-based drafting experience (AutoCAD)

This position is particularly well suited for an engineer who:

• Takes ownership of their projects and engineering deliverables.

• Can independently manage their workload, priorities, and deadlines.

• Has strong knowledge of the NEC and understands how to apply it to real-world solar and BESS installations.

• Has strong electrical engineering fundamentals and exercises sound engineering judgment.

• Is comfortable working with medium-voltage systems and complex renewable-energy electrical infrastructure.

• Has substation experience or is capable of effectively coordinating with substation and utility engineers.

• Can identify technical, constructability, and coordination issues before they become field problems.

• Understands that a successful design must work not only on paper, but also during procurement, construction, commissioning, and operation.

• Communicates proactively and does not wait for others to identify problems or determine the next step.

• Can communicate technical concepts to non-technical people effectively.

• Can manage multiple simultaneous projects in an environment with tight deadlines and high expectations for performance.

• Works effectively with engineers as well as project managers, construction personnel, vendors, utilities, and other stakeholders.

• Is comfortable being accountable for the quality and completeness of their engineering work.

• Combination of technical knowledge with practical engineering judgment, ownership, and execution.

Physical Requirements:

Ability to lift up to 50 lbs. on occasion.

Working Conditions: Most work time will be spent in an office environment, but occasional site visits may be performed. Significant time spent on the phone and working on computer.
