title: Director of Performance Creative
description:
The job in one line

You run the team that makes our video ads.

Not the brand film. Not the packaging. The hundreds of pieces of video that go into paid social every month, get measured against hook rate and CPA, and either scale or die.

Creative is our single biggest growth lever. Right now it's the constraint. We're hiring the person who removes it.

What you'll actually do

Build and run the creative engine. Hire and lead a pod of creative strategists and performance editors. Set the concept volume, the testing cadence, and the standard. Own the pipeline from insight → brief → shoot/edit → launch → read → iterate. You are accountable for throughput and for what the work does to blended CAC.

Decide what we make and why. Translate performance data and customer research into creative frameworks — angles, hooks, formats, and segmented lanes across our product line. You should be able to look at a week of results and say what to make next, and defend it. Build out personas and scale into new ones.

Own the creative testing system. Structured hypotheses, clean reads, real learning loops. We want a library of what works and why, not a folder of ads. You'll partner closely with growth on measurement and with our data team on the numbers behind it.

Direct creator and UGC output. Write the briefs. Set the formats. Make sure what comes back from creators is built to perform, not just built to look nice. Own content acquisition strategy end to end.

Set the visual and tonal guardrails. Energy, pacing, tone, what feels undeniably Everyday Dose — and what converts without eroding trust. Direct creative across the full customer journey, including subscription retention, not just first purchase. We are not chasing trends. We're defining a lane.

Work across the company. Product on launches and positioning. Retail on adaptation. CX on mining what customers actually say. Growth on where the money goes.

What success looks like in 90 days

• A functioning creative pod with a clear operating cadence

• A step change in concept volume and iteration velocity

• Improved blended CAC attributable to creative, not just to spend

• A documented point of view on what works for our customer, backed by tests

• A team that thinks in hypotheses, not in trends

Requirements

What we're looking for

• 8+ years in performance creative and/or direct-response marketing, with real ownership of paid video

• You have personally led a team producing video ads at volume — in-house or at a performance creative shop. If you've worked at or alongside a TubeScience-model operation, we want to talk.

• Experience marketing physical products direct to consumer. App, SaaS, and digital-only backgrounds aren’t a fit.

• DTC or CPG background. Supplements, wellness, beauty, or fitness is a strong plus.

• Fluent in the numbers. Hook rate, thumbstop, hold, CVR, CPA, blended CAC, LTV. You can read a creative report without a translator.

• Strong instincts for female-focused wellness brands and an understanding of the midlife female consumer

• Taste, and the ability to explain it. You can articulate why something works, not just that it did.

• You use AI tooling daily to move faster on ideation, iteration, and QA

Bonus

• You've helped scale a nine-figure DTC brand

• You've built and mentored a creative team while managing up to a demanding exec

• Direct-response or VSL background

• You’re in Austin, or open to relocating there.

• Experience with ingestible or supplement brands, and with subscription replenishment models.

What this role is not

• Not a brand-only storyteller

• Not a pure art director

• Not a production or post manager

• Not a media buyer

If your portfolio is beautiful but you can't tell us what it did to CAC, this isn't the right fit — and that's fine.

How to apply

Skip the cover letter. Instead, send us:

• Three ads you made that worked — link or file. For each, one or two lines on the insight behind it and what it did to performance. Numbers if you have them; honest estimates if you don't.

• One ad you made that failed, and what you learned.

• A short answer: you're handed a wellness brand doing eight figures with a CAC that's crept up 30% in six months. Creative is stale. What are your first three moves, and in what order?

We read these carefully. Applications without them won't move forward.

Compensation
$180,000–$200,000 base, plus a performance bonus and equity.

• Your offer will depend on your skills, experience, education and location. The range above is base salary only; total compensation also includes bonus, equity and benefits.

Health, vision and dental. Full medical, vision, dental and prescription coverage for anyone working 32+ hours a week, starting the first of the month after you join. We cover 75% of your premiums.

title: Senior Service Designer/Innovation Lead
description:
As part of the Cabin Crew, you will play a pivotal role in designing and orchestrating end-to-end services and experiences for our clients. You’ll help them navigate complex ecosystems of people, processes, policies, and technology while connecting customer experiences to the operations and systems that enable them.

You’ll collaborate closely with clients to understand their business objectives, assess their current capabilities, and shape strategies, services, and products that deliver real value. Your expertise in human-centered and service design will be instrumental in identifying opportunities, mapping and improving services, and guiding teams through ambiguity toward confident decisions.

We’re seeking a Strategist who embodies our passion for creating exceptional user and customer experiences through innovation. This is a hands-on individual contributor role for someone who can think in systems, lead with service design, and still roll up their sleeves to do the work, balancing strategy, design, and technology to solve real-world problems.

Responsibilities:

Lead service and product initiatives end-to-end

• Lead and execute service and product initiatives from discovery through definition and into delivery, using human-centered and service design frameworks to ensure everything is deeply rooted in real user and customer needs.

• Develop and execute experience, service, and product strategies that align user needs, business goals, and operational feasibility.

Drive service design and ecosystem thinking

• Lead service blueprinting, journey mapping, ecosystem mapping, and stakeholder mapping efforts to align teams on how a service works today and how it should work tomorrow.

• Connect frontstage experiences (customers, end users, partners) with backstage realities (teams, processes, systems, policies) to design services that are both delightful and deliverable.

• Identify gaps, failure points, and opportunities across the end-to-end service, beyond any single touchpoint or interface.

Create clarity in ambiguous spaces

• Facilitate problem framing and visioning work when the problem and solution are not yet clear, helping teams understand what to tackle first and why.

• Design and structure experiments, prototypes, and pilots that test not just interfaces, but entire service moments (people + process + tech).

• Translate complex ecosystem insights into clear narratives, options, and recommendations for decision-makers.

Champion human-centered & service design practices

• Oversee and integrate user research processes, including interviews, contextual inquiry, concept testing, and usability testing to inform service and product direction.

• Champion experience and service design practices (including UX), guiding multidisciplinary teams in creating user-centric, service-aware designs and prototypes that adhere to best practices in usability and accessibility.

• Advocate for a culture of innovation, encouraging creative problem-solving and exploration of new ideas and technologies to enhance user and customer experience.

Orchestrate cross-functional collaboration

• Collaborate with stakeholders across strategy, design, product, engineering, data, and operations to ensure strategic alignment and successful delivery of services and products.

• Use service design artifacts (blueprints, journeys, future-state stories, experience principles) as alignment and decision-making tools in workshops, working sessions, and stakeholder reviews.

• Drive continuous improvement of our methods and frameworks, incorporating project learnings to enhance future work.

Communicate, coach, and support growth

•

• Articulate and present strategic visions, service and experience concepts, and roadmaps to diverse audiences, including executive teams and client partners.

• Teach and coach client teams in service design methods—such as blueprinting, journey mapping, and experience principle development—while delivering high-quality artifacts and leading teams toward outcomes.

• Assist business development efforts by analyzing and articulating client needs, framing opportunities, and contributing to proposals. Act as a subject matter expert on service design, human-centered innovation, and select industries, as well as Cabin’s strategic frameworks.

Requirements:

• Proven track record leading service or product strategy and experience design initiatives, with a strong portfolio showcasing service blueprints, journeys, and/or complex ecosystem work for digital and/or omnichannel services.

• Deep understanding of human-centered and service design principles, with a systems mindset and a user-first approach to shaping services and products.

• Demonstrated experience using service blueprinting, journey mapping, and ecosystem mapping to connect customer experience with operational and technical realities.

• Expertise in conducting user and stakeholder research and translating insights into actionable service and product strategies, concepts, and roadmaps.

• Exceptional facilitation skills, with an uncommon ability to design and lead workshops and problem-solving sessions that bring together diverse stakeholders and move them toward alignment.

• Strong communication and storytelling skills, capable of conveying complex concepts clearly and persuasively across different audiences—from frontline staff to executives.

• Comfort working in highly ambiguous problem spaces, where defining the right question and narrowing the focus is as important as generating solutions.

• Collaborative, low-ego approach with the ability to inspire and motivate cross-functional teams without formal authority.

• Familiarity with design and prototyping tools (e.g., Figma, FigJam, Miro) and an understanding of current trends in digital products, services, and enabling technologies.

description:
Position Purpose

Magpie Health Analytics is seeking a Human-Centered Design (HCD) Specialist to improve digital applications and services supporting the federal health clients. The role focuses on understanding how people use these systems and making them easier to navigate and use. The HCD Specialist will research user needs, test design ideas, and work with product managers, developers, and customer stakeholders to turn findings into practical improvements.

Primary Duties & Responsibilities

• User Research and Discovery: Plan and conduct qualitative and quantitative user research, including interviews, usability studies, and collaborative discovery sessions, to understand user needs, workflows, and challenges.

• Analysis and Synthesis: Analyze research findings, develop user personas and journey maps, and define problems and opportunities for improvement to inform product and design decisions.

• Agile Collaboration: Work with product managers, developers, and testers to translate research findings and design recommendations into user stories, acceptance criteria, and prioritized backlog items.

• Documentation and Communication: Document and present research findings, design decisions, testing results, and recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders

• Bachelor's degree in Human-Computer Interaction, User Experience Design, Psychology, Information Science, Human Factors, Design, or a related field.

• Experience with user interviews, usability testing, and journey mapping.

• Ability to turn research findings into design recommendations, requirements, or user stories.

• Knowledge of Section 508, WCAG, and accessible design practices.

• Strong analytical, communication, and collaboration skills.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with Figma, Miro, Mural, Lucidchart, or similar tools.

AI Tools & Validation: Practical experience with Claude, ChatGPT, Figma AI, Cursor, or similar tools. Ability to structure AI workflows, validate outputs, and identify inaccuracies and missing requirements.

UX/UI Expertise: Advanced Figma skills, including user flows, interactive prototypes, reusable components, design systems, and developer-ready specifications.

Technical Collaboration: Experience working with React/frontend engineers, understanding API/data constraints, and producing specifications suitable for AI-assisted development.

Research & Problem-Solving: Strong skills in user research, usability testing, complex workflow analysis, and identifying edge cases.

Autonomy & Communication: Ability to independently prioritize, document decisions, and deliver high-impact results within a 20-hour workweek.

Preferred Qualifications

A senior product designer who combines complex B2B SaaS experience, strong UX judgment, technical understanding, and genuinely AI-native working practices.

Acting as the central creative integrator, the CD ensures alignment across disciplines while maintaining creative integrity, feasibility, and craft, without personally executing every component.

The CD represents the creative team in client and internal forums, guiding work forward through direction, feedback, and decision-making. Success in this role requires strong creative judgment, leadership, and the ability to balance ambition with real-world constraints.

Requirements

title: Creative Director - Brand Narrative
description:
In 1977, Charles and Ray Eames began a film with a picnic beside Chicago’s lakefront. Over the next nine minutes, Powers of Ten traveled out toward distant galaxies and back into the microscopic world inside a human hand. An enormous subject became a journey you could follow, built around a simple change in perspective. Images, language, movement, and sound brought the idea to life together.

That’s the kind of creative thinking we’re looking for at Mercury: finding a compelling idea inside something complex, then bringing together the people and crafts that make it unforgettable.

We’re looking for a Creative Director to build and lead Brand Narrative, a new team within Brand Creative. You’ll turn company strategy, product truths, customer insight, and cultural observations into original concepts for our most important launches, campaigns, and brand moments. You’ll originate ideas yourself and stay closely involved as they become finished work.

Your background might be in art direction, design, or copywriting. What matters is your ability to develop exceptional concepts, recognize the best idea wherever it comes from, and bring the whole creative studio together to make it real. Whatever your starting discipline, you’ll bring deep experience in film-led storytelling.

You’ll lead Brand Narrative in close creative partnership with your peers leading Brand Design and Writing. Together, you’ll shape concepts, language, and visual expression from the beginning, bringing distinct perspectives and shared ownership to the work. You’ll contribute strong ideas of your own, invite others to challenge and improve them, and build on theirs. This is a role for someone who enjoys making work together, not developing ideas in isolation and handing them off.

You’ll also shape what Brand Narrative becomes. That means building its culture, developing its people, and establishing ways of working that make the entire studio more creatively ambitious. The opportunity is to make great work while building a team that can keep making it.

What you’ll do

In your first year, your focus will be roughly 70% leading creative development for our highest-priority launches and campaigns, and 30% building the Brand Narrative function.

•
Originate and lead big creative ideas. Partner with Product Marketing and Brand Marketing on the brief, then turn the agreed audience, opportunity, and product proof into original creative concepts. Develop ideas that can take distinctive forms across film, social, out-of-home, digital, experiences, and partnerships.

•
Bring ambitious concepts to life with your creative peers and the full studio. Work side by side with the Brand Design and Writing leads and their teams from the earliest explorations through delivery. Develop ideas together, exchange thoughtful critique, and make creative choices that draw on each discipline’s expertise. Stay hands-on, contribute through your own craft, and partner closely with Motion and Production throughout. For film, remain closely involved through scripts, visual development, production, and the final edit.

•
Build audience and distribution thinking into the idea. Shape concepts around how people will discover, watch, and share the work. Work with marketing partners to consider channels and viewing contexts from the beginning, so the work belongs where people encounter it rather than simply being resized to fit.

•
Push beyond the first good answer, and learn quickly. Lead thoughtful concept development and critique. Use rough scripts, prototypes, and AI tools to test ideas quickly, learn, and move the strongest work forward. Know when to keep exploring and when to commit, then protect what makes an idea interesting through feedback and production.

•
Find opportunities before a brief arrives. Bring curiosity about Mercury’s products, customers, and the wider world. Develop proactive ideas and cultural opportunities that give the brand something meaningful to say or do.

•
Help decide where creative ambition matters most. Partner early with Product Marketing, Brand Marketing, Product Design, Comms, and Insights. Help identify which moments deserve our largest creative investment, present recommendations to senior leadership, and use results from marketing and insights partners to inform what comes next.

•
Build and lead Brand Narrative. Define the team’s purpose, priorities, creative standards, and ways of working. Help hire and develop the team, shaping its structure and capabilities. Set clear expectations, and coach people to grow their judgment and conceptual strength.

•
Create a culture where the best idea wins. Make room for experimentation, honest feedback, and contributions across disciplines. Lead with generosity and conviction, share ownership of the work, and help people challenge one another without making creativity a competition for credit.

•
Build practices that strengthen the work. Establish a clear path from insight and an agreed brief to concept and execution, with useful critique and close collaboration throughout. Develop relationships with external creatives and agencies who can add a distinctive perspective or capability when needed.

What you’ll bring

•
A strong creative foundation in art direction, design, or copywriting. Your portfolio shows original concepts developed into ambitious, well-crafted work across multiple formats. You can explain what you contributed, how the idea evolved, and how collaboration made it better.

•
Deep film experience. You’ve developed film-led ideas from concept through production, with strong instincts for story, scripts, performance, pacing, and sound. You understand how these choices work together to make an audience feel something, not just make a film look good.

•
A track record of deep creative collaboration with design and writing peers. You’ve led ambitious multidisciplinary work from concept through production by building trusted partnerships. You bring a clear point of view, listen closely, work through creative disagreements constructively, and recognize when someone else’s approach makes the work stronger. You can show how your collaborators shaped the outcome, not just what you personally originated.

•
Strong taste, cultural awareness, and product curiosity. You can get close to a complex business or product, find the human truth within it, and turn that understanding into something clear, surprising, and memorable.

•
Experience developing creative people and shaping how a team works. You give specific, useful feedback, set a high bar with care, and create an environment where people can take creative risks. You’re excited to build a new function, including the everyday practices that give it a culture.

•
Clear communication and sound judgment. You can rally people around an ambitious concept, explain why it deserves investment, and navigate competing perspectives without losing the idea. You take ownership in ambiguous situations and balance creative ambition with the need to move work forward.

What success looks like

A year in, you’ll have led major launches and film-led campaigns from original concept through finished work, with Brand Design and Writing as creative partners from the beginning. The studio’s disciplines will have shaped the work together, with audience and distribution informing the creative approach.

Brand Narrative will have a clear identity, shared creative standards, and working practices that help people test and develop stronger ideas together. Alongside planned launches, you’ll have established a pipeline of proactive opportunities that gives Mercury more ways to express its product ambition with originality and cultural relevance.

Please include a portfolio featuring film-led work and broader campaign concepts. We’d love to understand your role in developing the ideas, the choices you made through production, and how you brought the work to life with others.

We believe great UX is not just about usability, it’s about deeply understanding our customers’ workflows and building experiences that feel tailored, intelligent, and indispensable to how they work.
As AlphaSense evolves into an AI-native platform, Design plays a critical role in defining how AI shows up in real workflows, from search to synthesis to decision-making. We partner closely with Product and Engineering to turn complex data and advanced AI capabilities into cohesive, intuitive, and high-quality experiences.
Our team is a global group of craftspeople, systems thinkers, and innovators who care deeply about quality, velocity, and impact. We operate with a strong sense of ownership, a bias toward action, and a commitment to raising the bar for what great product design looks like in an AI-first world.

About the Role:
We are seeking a Principal Design Engineer to play a key role in shaping the future of AlphaSense’s product experience. This is a senior individual contributor role, where you’ll lead through craft, systems thinking, and technical excellence, building AI-powered experiences that feel tailored, intelligent, and essential to our customers’ workflows.
You will operate at the intersection of design, engineering, and product strategy, translating complex, data-rich problems into high-quality, production-ready experiences. You won’t just prototype ideas; you’ll define how they are built, scaled, and experienced in the product.
As a senior member of the Design team, you’ll act as a multiplier—mentoring others, guiding technical and design decisions, and strengthening the connection between user needs, business goals, and engineering realities.

Why this role matters
At AlphaSense, design is a core driver of how we win. As we build an AI-native platform, the quality of our user experience will define how effectively customers can navigate complexity, build conviction, and make decisions.
In this role, you will help define that standard—through the systems you build, the experiences you ship, and the team you help elevate.

What You’ll Do

• Create high-fidelity, coded prototypes and interaction models that bring complex, AI-powered workflows to life and clearly communicate product direction.

• Own high-impact initiatives from concept through production, shipping experiences that reflect strong design thinking, technical rigor, and a deep understanding of customer workflows.

• Lead technical design discussions, make architectural decisions, and guide cross-team implementation efforts.

• Advance AlphaSense’s design system as a core piece of product infrastructure—defining scalable patterns, enabling consistency, and accelerating teams building across AI-native experiences.

• Collaborate closely with product managers, engineers, and other stakeholders to research and evaluate user requirements, translate them into effective designs, and ensure that the final product meets both user and business needs.

• Collaborate with engineering teams during development, advocating for design quality and user experience by championing design fidelity and attention to detail throughout the development lifecycle.

Design Leadership & Team Impact

• Act as a senior leader within the Design team, mentoring designers and engineers, raising the bar for craft, and contributing to a strong, collaborative design culture.

• Serve as connective tissue across design, product, and engineering—helping teams navigate tradeoffs between technical constraints, business goals, and user experience to deliver high-quality outcomes.

Who You Are

• 12+ years of experience in product design, design/UX/front-end engineering, design systems, or a related discipline.

• A bachelor’s degree or higher. A degree in design, computer science, information sciences, psychology, or human-computer interaction is preferred.

• Hands-on experience with modern front-end technologies (e.g., HTML/CSS, JavaScript/TypeScript, React) and evolving design systems.

• Experience building AI and agentic experiences, and you are already leveraging AI to speed up and augment your end-to-end design and development process.

• Expertise with modern AI technologies and ability to apply them to design problems (e.g., MCP, Claude Code, Codex, Skills).

• Experience shipping production-ready experiences and influencing technical and design choices across teams.

• Strong understanding of user-centered design principles, end-to-end customer workflows, and the ability to turn new users into habitual users.

• Excellent communication and collaboration skills with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Demonstrated experience in project leadership, mentorship, and providing constructive feedback to foster professional growth.

description:
About Us:

YipitData is the leading market research and analytics firm for the disruptive economy and most recently raised $475M from The Carlyle Group at a valuation of over $1B. Every day, our proprietary technology analyzes billions of alternative data points to uncover actionable insights across sectors like software, AI, cloud, e-commerce, ridesharing, and payments.

We operate globally with offices in the US, APAC, and India. Our award-winning, people-centric culture—recognized by Inc. as a Best Workplace for three consecutive years—emphasizes transparency, ownership, and continuous mastery.

What It’s Like to Work at YipitData:

YipitData isn’t a place for coasting—it’s a launchpad for ambitious, impact-driven professionals.

From day one, you’ll take the lead on meaningful work, accelerate your growth, and gain exposure that shapes careers.

Why Top Talent Chooses YipitData:

•
Ownership That Matters: You’ll lead high-impact projects with real business outcomes

•
Rapid Growth: We compress years of learning into months

•
Merit Over Titles: Trust and responsibility are earned through execution, not tenure

•
Velocity with Purpose: We move fast, support each other, and aim high—always with purpose and intention

If your ambition is matched by your work ethic—and you're hungry for a place where growth, impact, and ownership are the norm—YipitData might be the opportunity you’ve been waiting for.

About The Role:

YipitData is looking for a Lead Web Designer & Developer to own the design and development of our public-facing websites. This is a hands-on role for someone who can move fluidly from user experience and visual design to responsive implementation in Webflow.

You will establish the systems, templates, and technical foundations that allow our teams to publish high-quality content quickly and consistently—without relying on engineering for routine website work. You will help evolve our website into a scalable growth platform that supports YipitData’s businesses, strengthens our brand, and creates clear, intuitive experiences for our audiences.

As the company’s in-house website design and development expert, you will partner closely with Design, Brand and Communications, Demand Generation, Corporate and Investor Marketing, Product, and business stakeholders across YipitData. You will also help us build internal website expertise and reduce our long-term reliance on external agencies.

Working hours: This is a fully remote role with a standard working schedule of approximately 9 am – 5 pm. Because you will collaborate with teams and stakeholders across both East and West Coast time zones, you will need the flexibility to occasionally accommodate meetings in a variety of time zones.

This is a remote-friendly opportunity that can sit in NYC (where our headquarters is located), one of our office hubs, or anywhere else in the US. However, depending upon where the remote work is performed, income could be subject to New York State tax withholding.

As Our Lead Web Designer & Developer You Will:

• Own the end-to-end design and development of YipitData’s public-facing websites, from early concepts and user flows through launch and ongoing iteration.

• Translate business objectives, brand strategy, content requirements, and growth opportunities into clear information architecture and compelling web experiences.

• Design and build responsive, accessible, production-ready pages, templates, components, and interactions in Webflow.

• Create and maintain a scalable website design system that improves consistency, quality, and speed across YipitData’s web properties.

• Serve as the technical owner of our Webflow environment, including CMS architecture, reusable components, custom code, integrations, permissions, documentation, and publishing workflows.

• Partner with Demand Generation and Marketing to support SEO and AEO, conversion optimization, experimentation, analytics, lead flows, and campaign launches.

• Collaborate with Brand and Communications to ensure that every website experience reflects YipitData’s visual identity, narrative, voice, and editorial standards.

• Work with business and product teams to turn complex offerings—including data, research, and AI-powered products—into intuitive, credible, and engaging digital experiences.

• Establish website quality standards and conduct ongoing reviews for usability, accessibility, responsiveness, performance, and cross-browser compatibility.

• Manage website projects and priorities across multiple stakeholders, communicating tradeoffs and moving work forward in a fast-paced environment.

• Develop self-service templates, guidance, and governance that enable non-technical teams to publish and update content safely.

• Collaborate with external agencies and specialized partners when needed while steadily increasing YipitData’s in-house capabilities.

You Are Likely To Succeed If:

• You have 5+ years of professional experience designing and building high-quality marketing or corporate websites, with a portfolio demonstrating both strong UX/visual design and hands-on implementation.

• You are highly proficient in Webflow, including CMS architecture, reusable components, responsive layouts, interactions, and custom code when needed.

• You have strong front-end fundamentals, including HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and can independently troubleshoot technical and implementation issues.

• You have deep experience with responsive design, information architecture, design systems, accessibility standards, browser compatibility, and website performance.

• You are comfortable owning work from initial request through discovery, design, stakeholder alignment, development, QA, launch, and iteration.

• You combine a high visual bar with pragmatic execution—you know when to refine a solution and when to ship, learn, and improve.

• You are an effective cross-functional partner who can translate among design, marketing, technical, and business stakeholders.

• You use qualitative feedback and quantitative signals to improve user experience, content discoverability, conversion, and overall site performance.

• You communicate clearly, manage competing priorities thoughtfully, and take responsibility for outcomes rather than waiting for detailed direction.

Nice-to-have experiences include:

• Designing websites for B2B technology, data, analytics, research, financial services, or other complex products.

• Technical SEO, AEO, structured data, content discoverability, or large-scale CMS publishing.

• Conversion-rate optimization, experimentation, analytics, and lead-generation workflows.

• Figma and component-based design systems.

• Connecting Webflow with analytics, marketing automation, CRM, forms, APIs, or other third-party platforms.

• Working with multiple brands, audiences, or business lines within one organization.

• Collaborating with (and eventually reducing reliance on) external design and development agencies.

What We Offer:

Our compensation package includes comprehensive benefits, perks, and a competitive salary:

• We care about your personal life, and we mean it. We offer flexible work hours, flexible vacation, a generous 401K match, parental leave, team events, wellness budget, learning reimbursement, and more!

• Your growth at YipitData is determined by the impact that you are making, not by tenure, unnecessary facetime, or office politics. Everyone at YipitData is empowered to learn, self-improve, and master their skills in an environment focused on ownership, respect, and trust. See more on our high-impact, high-opportunity work environment above!

•
Base Salary + Performance-Based Bonus: The annual base salary range for this position is anticipated to be $150,000 with eligibility for an annual performance-based bonus of up to 10%. Final compensation may be determined by a number of factors, including, but not limited to, the applicant’s experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, and internal team benchmarks.

This role may be performed fully remotely within the United States. Please note that our US headquarters are located in NYC. If the remote work is performed outside of these offices, income may be subject to New York State tax withholding.

title: Senior Product Designer
description:
Aetonix is a digital health company building a chronic care management platform for U.S. health systems, clinics, and ACOs. Our product has two faces:

• A mobile app that helps Medicare patients (65+) complete simple, guided check ins, and

• A desktop app that helps care teams know which patients need them most — and act.

We are backed by Trudell Medical International (TMI), a Canadian-headquartered medical device company. We operate with patient capital and startup urgency.

The next 6 months are about proving product-market fit with real clinical evidence in a category where fewer than 4% of eligible U.S. patients are currently receiving the care they are entitled to.

ABOUT THIS ROLE

You'll join our design team – working alongside our Product Designer and Lead Product Designer – as a senior contributor across the patient mobile app and care-team desktop app, owning specific product surfaces end-to-end and raising the craft bar within your area.

You’ll report directly to the VP of Product, and partner closely with the Lead Product Designer on shared design system standards, growing our research practice, and raising the bar on the team’s design craft.

HATS YOU WEAR

Craft Contributor Your work sets the example within your surface area, and raises the bar for the team around you.

• Deliver high-quality, well-reasoned design from problem framing through shipped product.

• Give structured critique that builds design taste and judgment in others.

• Contribute to our evolving design system across web and mobile surfaces.

Researcher You run and synthesize lean research, and share those learnings with peers.

• Lead qualitative and quantitative research with care teams and Medicare patients.

• Recognize when data or research is missing and go get it — designing the study, recruiting, and synthesizing findings.

• Translate complex clinical workflows into clear, intuitive software interactions.

Discovery Partner You bring a user-grounded point of view to the product decisions that shape your surface.

• Participate in product decisions as a full voice, grounded in user insight.

• Push back when a problem needs more framing before solutions are explored.

• Frame recommendations in the language of outcomes and impact.

Communicator You tell a crisp story that connects the design to the people it serves.

• Confidently present design work to cross functional peers, innovation partners, and executives when needed.

• Use story maps, journey maps, and similar tools so product, design, and engineering align on risks and priorities.

• Bring patient and clinician voices into trade off discussions so core perspectives shape final decisions.

MUST HAVE

• 5–7+ years of experience in product design, with a portfolio showing end-to-end ownership from research through shipped product.

• Strong research skills: able to run a usability study, synthesize findings quickly, and share what you learn with others.

• Hands on with AI/ML powered product design. You have experimented with AI or ML features, and can explain what “good” looks like.

• Experience contributing to and working within a shared design system (web + mobile), in partnership with other designers and engineers.

• Solid accessibility practice baked into your work (keyboard and screen-reader flows, clear focus states, robust interaction patterns).

• Familiarity with product analytics tools (e.g., Amplitude) to uncover usage patterns and inform design decisions.

• Active use of AI design and research tooling (e.g., Claude, Figma Make or equivalents) to accelerate prototyping, synthesis, and research; teaches others to do the same.

• Ability to craft compelling design stories that win buy-in from engineers and cross-functional stakeholders.

• Comfort giving and receiving structured feedback, with genuine interest in helping other designers grow, even without a formal mentorship mandate.

NICE TO HAVE

• Background in healthcare, clinical, or regulated software. You understand what HIPAA and clinical workflows mean for design decisions.

• Behavioral science experience; designing for habit formation, engagement, or behavior change.

• Familiarity with CCM, RPM, or chronic disease management platforms.

• AI/ML product design experience in a healthcare or clinical context: conversational interfaces, clinical decision support, or data-heavy dashboards.

• WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility expertise in a regulated health context.

WHO YOU ARE

• A builder. Most energized when you are crafting something new, not polishing something established.

• Mission-driven. You care about patients and want your design work to have measurable impact on how chronic disease is managed.

• Humble enough to listen deeply to a care coordinator, confident enough to challenge a product decision, and persuasive enough to translate both for executive stakeholders.

WORKING CONDITIONS

• Fully remote: open to candidates in Canada or the United States. EST/CST overlap preferred for core collaboration hours.

• Occasional in-person team meetings in Ottawa, London (Ontario) and Toronto, Canada areas (travel required on a quarterly basis at minimum).

• Comprehensive benefits package including health insurance, RSP matching, and professional development opportunities.

WHAT WE OFFER:

• An agile, dynamic and motivated team working together in a fast-growing company that is changing the future of virtual care

• The ability to make a real difference in people’s lives

• Health insurance including medical, dental, vision and life

title: Creative Director, Visual
description:
Some problems are too important for ordinary thinking.

How do you change behavior at scale? Build trust when trust is hard to earn? Make something complicated feel simple? Get millions of people to see things differently—and do something about it?

These are the kinds of problems we work on at ICF Next. The stakes are high. The answers aren't obvious. And the work has to do more than look good.

We're looking for a Creative Director who loves that kind of challenge. Someone with a restless imagination, exceptional instincts and the ability to turn a difficult brief into an idea that feels inevitable once you've seen it.

Someone who knows great creative work doesn't happen by accident. It takes curiosity, conviction, craft and people who care enough to keep pushing.

About ICF & ICF Next

ICF is a global consulting and technology services company working on some of the most pressing challenges facing businesses, governments and communities. From energy and climate to public health, infrastructure and government, our teams bring deep expertise to problems that don't have easy answers.

ICF Next brings creativity into that equation.

We're writers, designers, strategists, technologists and creative thinkers working together to help organizations connect with people and move them to action.

We have the creative ambition of an agency and access to the expertise of a global consultancy. That combination gives us an unusual opportunity: to understand difficult problems from the inside, find the human story and create work that makes a difference in the real world.

There's no shortage of interesting briefs. The challenge is doing something extraordinary with them.

The Role

You'll lead creative across major client engagements, from the first conversation about a problem to the last detail of the finished work.

You'll find the idea that makes everything click. Set the visual direction. Push the thinking. Bring writers, designers, strategists and producers together around a shared ambition.

The work spans integrated campaigns, brand experiences, film, digital, social, experiential and whatever else the idea calls for.

You'll be expected to have a point of view, make decisions, challenge work that isn't good enough and know when to let a better idea win.

You'll also help shape the creative culture at ICF Next. Not through speeches about excellence, but through the work you make, the standards you set and the people you help develop.

What You'll Do

•
Find the idea. Get beneath the brief, ask better questions and turn complicated challenges into original, compelling creative concepts.

•
Set the standard. Bring a sharp eye, strong art direction and a deep respect for design, storytelling and execution. Care about the big idea and every detail that makes it work.

•
Make people care. Take subjects that can be technical, sensitive or difficult to explain and make them clear, relevant and human.

•
Think beyond the medium. Lead creative across digital, social, film, video, experiential, paid media, out-of-home and emerging platforms. Start with the idea, not the format.

•
Make the team better. Inspire, mentor and challenge creatives. Give useful feedback. Recognize talent. Create the conditions for people to do the best work of their careers.

•
Stand behind the work. Present ideas with clarity and conviction. Build relationships with clients. Know how to push without making it personal, and how to protect a strong idea while making it stronger.

•
Get it made. Work across disciplines, manage competing priorities and navigate the realities of complex projects without losing sight of what made the idea worth pursuing.

•
Stay curious. Explore new tools, technologies and ways of working, including AI, without confusing what's new with what's good.

Who You Are

You came up through art direction or design, but you've never thought of yourself as just a visual person.

You think in ideas. You understand the power of an image, the precision of a line of copy and the way everything comes together to tell a story.

You have taste. You have opinions. You can explain both.

You know the difference between a clever execution and a genuinely good idea. You can spot what's missing, see what's possible and help a team get there.

You're comfortable leading a room, but you listen. You know how to sell an idea without overselling it. And you're not afraid to roll up your sleeves when the work needs you.

You've worked on difficult briefs, with demanding clients and tight deadlines. You've learned that constraints aren't an excuse for mediocre work.

Most importantly, you still get excited when something great comes together. You haven't lost the instinct to make it better.

What You Bring

Required Qualifications

• 12+ years of creative experience in an agency, design studio or comparable environment, including senior-level creative leadership.

• A portfolio that shows exceptional conceptual thinking, art direction, design craft and integrated creative work.

Professional Skills

• Experience leading creative teams and developing campaigns across multiple channels.

• Strong visual storytelling, strategic thinking and presentation skills.

• The ability to take ambitious ideas from concept through production while managing complex projects, stakeholders and deadlines.

Why ICF Next

The problems we work on aren't always easy to explain. They don't always come with glamorous briefs or obvious answers.

That's what makes them interesting.

You get to work with people who know their subjects inside out, tackle challenges that affect how people live and make decisions, and bring your creative instincts to places where they're genuinely needed.

There's room here for big ideas. For unexpected thinking. For the kind of work that makes you proud of what you do.

If you believe the hardest problems deserve the best creative minds, we'd like to meet you.

Show us your work. Show us how you think.

Bot and Third-Party Applications

Please note that this application must be submitted directly by the applicant for consideration. Failure to do so may result in the application being excluded for consideration. Applicants needing an accommodation for disability or religious purposes in connection with the application process should contact for assistance.

Working at ICF

title: Product Designer (US - Part-time, Contract)
description:
Spate is a trend intelligence platform for consumer brands in beauty, wellness, and food and beverage. We analyze anonymous, aggregated public consumer data to spot emerging trends early and explain why they're growing, so brands can make product and marketing decisions with confidence.

Our founders, Yarden Horwitz and Olivier Zimmer, started Google's Trendspotting division and called trends like turmeric, cold brew, and face masks before they went mainstream. Spate is Y Combinator-backed, and more than 200 brands use it, including Sephora, L'Oréal Paris, Estée Lauder Companies, Unilever, P&G, and e.l.f. Our data regularly appears in The New York Times, WWD, British Vogue, and The Business of Fashion.

About the role

We're looking for a part-time contract product designer to shape Spate's core product: the dashboard where brand teams explore trends, build reports, and work with our AI assistant.

Our platform will change a lot over the next year or two as we rebuild around LLM-powered features. We already ship an AI Assistant, AI Reports (an LLM powered dashboard builder), and in-dashboard summaries and analysis. We need someone who can work out what those experiences should be, not just how they should look.

Our users are brand innovation teams, product marketers, social media teams, and agencies. Most aren't data analysts, so much of the job is turning dense trend data into something clear and actionable.

You'll join the Frontend & UX team, four people including you, and work closely with our frontend lead. The role is fully remote and part-time, about 20 hours a week. You’ll need to be based in US Central Time (UTC−6) or US Eastern Time (UTC-5). We require you to be available for core collaboration hours of 9:00 AM–12:00 PM Eastern.

This is a remote, Part-time contractor position.

What you'll own

The product, not just the screens. At Spate, product design and UI/UX design happen together. Features aren't fully defined and then handed to a designer. You'll help decide what we build and why, and stay involved from the first conversation to launch. You'll work with our frontend lead to choose the right deliverable for each problem: a written proposal, a user flow, a prototype, or a full Figma spec.

Finding problems worth solving. Find user pain points on your own, through customer calls, feedback, and usage data. Then take them from problem to proposal: frame the problem, explore options, and make the case for a direction. Leadership sets the overall direction and can help point you at problems, but you won't need our input to get started.

How our AI features work. Decide when something should be a chat, a report, or an inline summary. Define how we show where an insight came from, and how we handle loading, uncertainty, and wrong answers. Help shape the voice and structure of AI-generated insights, because in an LLM product the words are part of the UX.

The design system. We have a Figma library and a React component library that are only loosely in sync. You'll own the system's principles and the Figma side, and partner with our frontend engineers to make the two a single source of truth. The goal is that everyday design decisions are answered by the system, so engineers can ship UI that feels like Spate without waiting on design.

AI quality, over time. As the role settles in, you'll help define what a good AI answer looks like for our users, and contribute to how we review user feedback and evaluate our LLM features.

Requirements

What we're looking for

We care more about mindset than years of experience. You're driven, you care about making a good product, and you have a growth mindset. You value autonomy and self-direction.

• 2+ years of product design experience, with work shipped in a real product.

• Strong product opinions. You think about what to build and why, not just how it looks, and you're comfortable defending and revising your ideas.

• A portfolio that shows how you framed problems, not just how you solved them. At least one case study should start from a fuzzy problem with no spec.

• Experience with, or a strong interest in, data-heavy products such as dashboards, analytics, or reporting tools.

• You've worked within or contributed to a design system, and understand how components and patterns scale.

• Real curiosity about AI products, ideally with some hands-on exploration.

• Strong written communication. We're remote and you're part-time, so your proposals and decisions need to stand on their own.

• Experience working as a freelancer or contractor, managing your own time and deliverables.

• Fluent in Figma, with AI tools in your everyday workflow.

Nice to have

• Experience as the first or only designer on a team.

• You've built or substantially evolved a design system that engineers adopted.

• Experience designing AI features, or reviewing the quality of LLM output.

• Depth in data visualization.

• Familiarity with consumer goods, beauty, food, or marketing and insights tools.

• Comfort building quick functional prototypes with AI tools to test ideas against real outputs.

Your first 90 days

• At 20 hours a week, we'll keep the first three months focused.

• First 30 days: Learn the product and the people who use it. Watch a few customer calls, review feedback and usage data, and ship your first improvements to the user experience.

• By day 60: Design your first feature solving a major user pain point or goal.

• By day 90: Work with the rest of the team to ship your feature into production.

How we work

Contributors at Spate work flexibly, with few meetings, a lot of impact, and real say over the direction of their work. Leadership sets product direction and priorities, and you shape how we get there. That means bringing proposals rather than waiting for briefs.

Our aesthetic is cool, smart, data-driven, and approachable. We want a designer who can hold that line while the product changes quickly.

This role does not include:

• Writing production code. Figma is your main tool, and our frontend engineers build.

• Brand and marketing design, such as the website, sales decks, or client reports.

• Other product surfaces like our API and MCP server.

Compensation

• Hourly rate: $75/hour.

• About 20 hours a week, as an independent contractor.

Recruitment Process

• Video interview (30 min). About you, in your own words.

• Assessment (10 min). A quiz designed to assess your problem solving abilities and approach to work.

• Intro call with our frontend lead (~20 min). Your background, how you like to work, and whether the role fits.

• Case study (60 min). Work through a solution to a real-world problem and record your process.

• Case study review (45 min). Walk us through your case study, focusing on how you framed the problem and arrived at your solution.

• Conversation with our CEO (45 min). Product vision, how we work, and your questions.

title: Creative Director
description:
Real opportunities. Real impact. Your career, redefined.

(NOTE: A human reviews every application at Oceans, so please apply for only one position and only once a year—if you're a better fit for another role, we’ll route your application accordingly and if we’re not quite ready for you, we’ll reach back out later.)

At Oceans, we believe that talent knows no boundaries. That’s why we connect the best and brightest professionals with career-defining opportunities that challenge, inspire, and accelerate their career growth. Our community, whom we call Divers, don’t just work—they dive deep, solve complex challenges, and make a real impact with global industry leaders. And in doing so, they don’t just support bold ideas—they expand their skills, broaden their expertise, and grow their careers.

As a Creative Director, you will join a fast-growing beauty and hair-care brand expanding its digital operations across the LATAM region. You will take charge of a lean, high-performing creative function built to support rapid digital expansion through short-form content, paid advertising, organic social media, and e-commerce creative. Rather than traditional, big-budget agency productions, this business prioritizes high-volume, performance-driven content production executed with efficiency and resourcefulness.

This is a true "player-coach" role designed for a creative leader who thrives on both setting direction and rolling up their sleeves to execute hands-on. You will oversee copywriting, graphic design, and video editing as a single, integrated creative pod, establishing visual standards, guiding team members, and maintaining high output velocity. Balancing creative quality, brand consistency, and budget discipline, you will drive impactful storytelling and content repurposing that fuels sustainable growth across digital channels.

Accountability

As a Creative Director, your success will be defined by your ability to lead a multidisciplinary creative pod and consistently deliver high-volume, performance-oriented content that drives engagement and brand consistency.

Here’s how you’ll make an impact:

Creative Leadership & Pod Management

• Lead the copywriting, graphic design, and video editing functions as one unified creative team.

• Provide clear creative direction, actionable feedback, and workload prioritization to pod members.

• Establish efficient production workflows to resolve creative bottlenecks and ensure on-time asset delivery.

• Review all creative output for visual quality, narrative relevance, and strict brand alignment.

Creative Strategy & Performance Concepting

• Develop high-converting creative concepts for paid advertising and organic social channels.

• Translate marketing objectives into concise, executable creative briefs for static, motion, and video assets.

• Identify creative hit rates across campaigns and iterate on successful concepts to generate variations.

• Leverage AI tools to accelerate ideation, storyboarding, and rapid content repurposing.

Organic Content Production & Activation

• Directly create and produce organic social content hands-on, maintaining a weekly content calendar.

• Coordinate creative production tailored specifically to short-form platforms like TikTok and Instagram Reels.

• Repurpose existing footage and user-generated content (UGC) into engaging organic assets.

• Review organic reach and engagement metrics to continuously inform future creative direction.

Paid Advertising & UGC Repurposing

• Oversee the production of fresh performance advertising creative across paid channels.

• Collaborate with copywriters on hooks and messaging, designers on visual hierarchy, and video editors on short-form execution.

• Transform UGC and creator content into multi-platform paid advertising variations.

• Review advertising asset performance with digital stakeholders to continuously improve hit rates.

Lean Production & Budget Ownership

• Plan, schedule, and direct practical, monthly photo and video shoots within defined budget parameters.

• Maximize the volume of reusable photo and video footage generated from every lean production shoot.

• Manage the monthly creative production budget, tracking cost per asset and optimizing resource allocation.

• Maintain an organized, on-brand creative asset library to streamline future content development.

Colleagues

You will report directly to the Chief Marketing Officer while partnering closely with the VP of Digital, performance marketing leads, and affiliate stakeholders to align creative execution with broader growth targets. On a daily basis, you will manage a multidisciplinary creative pod consisting of a Senior Copywriter, Senior Graphic Designer, and Video Editor.

At Oceans, you’ll also receive guidance and support from your Operations Manager, who will help you succeed in the role and ensure that you’re continuously growing and developing in your career.

Skills and Qualifications

At Oceans, we believe in T-shaped individuals—those who bring deep expertise in one area, paired with broad curiosity and interests. As a Creative Director, your vertical strength will be Creative Concepting, Storytelling & Short-Form Content, while your horizontal capabilities should span Team Leadership, Performance Creative Optimization, and Lean Budget Management.

To excel in this role, you should have:

•
Experience: Proven track record leading small, fast-paced creative teams (in-house or DTC brand experience preferred), with hands-on experience in short-form social content (TikTok, Instagram Reels) and paid social advertising. Experience in the DTC beauty or personal-care space is a strong plus.

•
Tools/Systems: Proficiency across visual design and video editing software (e.g., Adobe Creative Suite, Figma, frame-accurate review tools), social platforms, and asset management systems. Comfort utilizing AI tools for ideation and storyboarding.

•
Analytics/Process: Ability to interpret creative hit rates, CPC/CPA metrics, and engagement data to refine content; strong production management skills with experience establishing high-volume content workflows and managing lean shoot budgets.

•
Mindset: A player-coach mentality with high operational agency, speed, and resourcefulness—prioritizing output efficiency and output speed over expensive, complex setups.

title: Principal, UX Design
description:
The Principal, UX Design owns Summit K12’s product-experience architecture, UX standards, design system, and proportionate validation approach. This is a hands-on functional leadership role accountable for coherent, accessible experiences across the product portfolio, personally delivering complex and consequential design work.
The Principal directs UX design practice through standards, judgment, implementation follow-through, and cross-functional partnership, while the UX Design Lead independently owns assigned experiences. The Principal does not require a separate design management layer or routine approvals. Product Managers retain product priorities, requirements, acceptance, and outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

1. Experience Architecture & Standards

• Define coherent navigation, information architecture, interaction patterns, and experience principles across student, educator, administrator, and applicable family workflows.

• Personally design and resolve complex or consequential cross-product experiences using working prototypes and explicit decisions.

• Make recurring UX debt visible and recommend evidence-based improvements to accountable Product leaders.

2. Design System & Accessibility

• Own governance, documentation, versioning, and evolution of shared components, patterns, UX writing conventions, and accessible interaction standards.

• Collaborate with the UX Design Lead on reusable patterns while keeping routine experience decisions close to assigned work.

• Work with Engineering and QA to verify material accessibility and experience expectations in production.

3. Research, Validation & Implementation

• Set lean, risk-proportionate research and usability standards; personally execute consequential validation and interpret user evidence.

• Deliver complete implementation-ready specifications for owned work, including critical states, behaviors, accessibility, and edge cases.

• Resolve systemic implementation-fidelity gaps and ensure relevant post-release signals inform improvements.

4. Functional Leadership, AI & Capacity

• Partner with Product leadership to sequence design demand, make capacity tradeoffs visible, and preserve clear product decision rights.

• Establish approved AI-supported methods for prototypes, research synthesis, documentation, and design checks, with human verification.

• Work directly with PMs, Engineering, Academic, Creative Studio, and customer-facing functions without introducing unnecessary review gates.

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

Required

• 7+ years in product or UX design, or equivalent demonstrated capability, including complex production workflows.

• Expertise in interaction design, information architecture, research, design systems, accessibility, and prototyping.

• Proven ability to lead through hands-on judgment, clear standards, and cross-functional influence.

• Ability to make defensible tradeoffs and independently deliver complex experience work.

• Practical fluency with Figma or equivalent production design tools.

• Experience using measured usability and product outcomes to guide design priorities.

• Responsible use and validation of AI-enabled design workflows.

Preferred

• K-12 EdTech, learning-platform, assessment, reporting, or complex SaaS experience.

• Experience modernizing legacy platforms and designing for multilingual or varied-accessibility users.

Definition of Success

Portfolio experiences become more coherent, accessible, and effective; complex design work moves through implementation reliably; a reusable design system and practical evidence reduce UX rework.

Benefits

Summit K12 offers a comprehensive benefits package. Highlights include:

• Medical, dental, and vision insurance with multiple plan options

• Company-paid short-term disability, long-term disability, and life insurance

• 401(k) retirement plan

title: Creative Director IA
description:
ABOUT US

Contáctica is the leading Martech Creative Agency in Puerto Rico, a strong challenger in Latin America, and a dynamic catalyst for growth in the U.S. mainland. For over 20 years, we have challenged the status quo and accelerated the evolution of visionary companies and their teams by delivering pioneering knowledge, transformative Martech solutions, and full-spectrum marketing agency services.

With headquarters in Puerto Rico and Colombia, and a closely integrated team working across ten countries, we are uniquely positioned to serve key industries such as Banking, Insurance, and Consumer Packaged Goods (CPGs), while tackling the most complex brand, product, and business challenges of today and tomorrow.

As we continue into a new era of Hyper-Evolution, we are passionately committed to driving growth and innovation by leveraging the Power of Humanity + Artificial Intelligence. Our unwavering focus remains unchanged: to deliver exceptional business outcomes through strategic thinking, creativity, and deep client insight, augmented by cutting-edge technologies.

If you share our beliefs—and are committed to acting on them fully—we invite you to review the requirements of this position and consider applying.

JOB DESCRIPTION

We are looking for a visionary, strategically minded, and technology-forward Creative Director to lead the conceptual, creative, and technological development of our assigned brands.

This role is responsible for transforming complex business and communication challenges into relevant, innovative, and executable ideas that deliver measurable value for our clients. The ideal candidate combines exceptional conceptual thinking, strong creative leadership, digital fluency, and a deep understanding of how Artificial Intelligence and emerging technologies are transforming the creative process.

The Creative Director will lead Associate Creative Directors, Copywriters, Content Creators, and strategic creative partners, while guiding multidisciplinary teams that may include Designers, Motion Designers, AI Specialists, Creative Developers, and Production Partners.

Working closely with the Chief Creative Officer, the Head of Art & AI Leader, and the Audiovisual General Producer & AI Leader, this person will turn the company’s creative vision into concrete solutions that combine strategic relevance, creative excellence, and technological feasibility.

This is not a role in which Artificial Intelligence is viewed solely as a production tool. We are looking for someone who understands that technology can also become the origin of an idea, an experience, a product, or a new business solution.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Lead the conceptual development of integrated campaigns, content platforms, digital experiences, and special projects.

• Transform business challenges, consumer insights, and strategic briefs into simple, relevant, memorable, and executable creative ideas.

• Ensure the conceptual quality, creative consistency, and executional excellence of all work developed by the assigned teams.

• Translate the creative vision established by the Chief Creative Officer into concrete solutions for clients and brands.

• Incorporate Artificial Intelligence and emerging technologies from the earliest stages of the creative process.

• Identify opportunities where AI can become an integral part of the concept, customer experience, product, or business solution—not only a tool for accelerating production.

• Explore new technologies and creative methodologies that enable the development of ideas that would be difficult or impossible to execute through traditional processes.

• Design and implement specialized AI agents to support creative research, insight generation, content development, production, workflow management, and knowledge sharing.

• Develop and maintain reusable libraries of prompts, agents, methodologies, and automated workflows for the creative department.

• Build intelligent workflows using automation platforms such as n8n, Make, or Zapier to improve productivity, consistency, and scalability.

• Use AI-assisted research tools to accelerate benchmarking, competitive analysis, trend identification, cultural exploration, and insight discovery.

• Lead the development of relevant creative insights, even when a project does not require a formal strategy workstream.

• Create rapid prototypes and proof-of-concept executions to evaluate ideas before entering full production.

• Understand how creativity connects across CRM, Social Media, Paid Media, Websites, E-commerce, Marketing Automation, Customer Journeys, and Conversational AI.

• Collaborate closely with Strategy, Accounts, Media, Technology, Production, and Project Management teams to ensure that ideas are strategically relevant and operationally viable.

• Partner with the Creative Intelligence Lead to strengthen brand platforms, communication frameworks, creative methodologies, and award narratives.

• Build compelling stories and narratives for campaigns, products, content ecosystems, digital experiences, and client presentations.

• Lead creative presentations and defend ideas with clarity, strategic reasoning, confidence, and the ability to inspire clients and internal teams.

• Act as a trusted creative and innovation advisor for assigned clients and brands.

• Anticipate creative, technological, operational, and reputational risks and address them with sound judgment and professionalism.

• Lead, inspire, mentor, and develop Associate Creative Directors, Copywriters, Content Creators, and other multidisciplinary talent.

• Provide clear, continuous, and actionable feedback that raises the quality of the work and supports professional growth.

• Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, experimentation, continuous learning, and creative ambition.

• Participate in talent selection, onboarding, development planning, and performance evaluation processes.

• Coordinate and evaluate external specialists and strategic partners in creativity, Artificial Intelligence, automation, technology, development, and production.

• Ensure that external partners meet the creative, technical, operational, and quality standards required by each project.

• Document and share methodologies, experiments, prompts, agents, workflows, case studies, and best practices across the creative department.

• Contribute to the development of new creative capabilities, technology-enabled services, and differentiated solutions for clients.

• Participate actively in new business opportunities, pitches, and strategic proposals.

• Identify campaigns and projects with the potential to become successful case studies or award submissions.

• Collaborate on the conceptual development and storytelling of entries for national and international creative festivals.

• Represent and live Contáctica’s values in every interaction with clients, teams, partners, and suppliers.

QUALIFICATIONS

• Proven experience as a Creative Director, Associate Creative Director, or in a comparable senior creative leadership role.

• Strong portfolio demonstrating outstanding conceptual thinking, integrated campaign development, storytelling, and creative execution.

• Experience leading multidisciplinary creative teams and developing creative talent.

• Strong ability to transform business challenges, strategic briefs, consumer insights, and cultural trends into relevant creative solutions.

• Solid understanding of branding, advertising, content, digital experiences, social platforms, and integrated marketing ecosystems.

• Demonstrated experience incorporating Artificial Intelligence into creative research, ideation, content development, production, or workflow optimization.

• Hands-on knowledge of leading generative AI and research platforms such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Midjourney, Adobe Firefly, Runway, Sora, and ElevenLabs.

• Ability to determine which AI platform, model, or technological solution is most appropriate for a specific creative objective.

• Experience designing advanced prompts, structured prompt systems, or conversational architectures that generate consistent and scalable results.

• Experience designing, configuring, or implementing specialized AI agents for research, creativity, production, automation, or knowledge management.

• Functional knowledge of automation platforms such as n8n, Make, or Zapier.

• Understanding of how CRM, Social Media, Paid Media, Websites, E-commerce, Marketing Automation, Customer Journeys, and Conversational AI connect within a client’s digital ecosystem.

• Ability to use AI-assisted research to conduct benchmarking, competitive analysis, trend exploration, and insight discovery.

• Strong presentation, storytelling, communication, and idea-selling skills.

• Ability to defend creative recommendations with strategic reasoning while remaining open to feedback and collaboration.

• Strong client-facing skills and the ability to act as a trusted advisor in creativity, innovation, and emerging technology.

• Experience working with external production partners, technology specialists, developers, and creative suppliers.

• Entrepreneurial mindset with a strong interest in developing new services, products, methodologies, and client solutions.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities, make sound decisions, and maintain creative excellence in a fast-paced environment.

• Strong curiosity and a continuous-learning mindset regarding creativity, culture, consumer behavior, Artificial Intelligence, technology, and innovation.

• Bachelor’s degree in Advertising, Design, Communications, Marketing, Creative Technology, or a related field.

• Fluency in English and Spanish, both written and spoken.

START THE JOURNEY

If you share our beliefs—and are committed to act on them fully—we invite you to apply to join our team and experience the thrill of working in a fast-paced, cutting-edge, mostly remote environment.

Apply here and start the journey. Please include a personal letter with your application explaining why you're the best person for this position.

Title: Senior Sediment Remediation Design Engineer and Project Manager

Location: Remote (Atlanta)

Job Type: Regular Full-time

What’s the Opportunity?

Anchor QEA is seeking a senior design engineer and project manager with 10 to 15 years of relevant experience to deliver upland remediation and contaminated sediment cleanup projects in the Southeast. You will spend most of your time focused on developing solutions for our clients' most challenging issues, combining engineering design with management of scopes, schedules, budgets, and multidisciplinary teams. Your work will span investigations, feasibility studies, remedial excavation, dredging and capping design, contractor procurement, and engineering support during design and construction. You will collaborate with experienced scientists and engineers, mentor junior staff, and develop practical, protective remedies for rivers, lakes, and industrial waterfronts.

Responsibilities:

• Manage concurrent remediation projects and design tasks, coordinating staff, subcontractors, scopes, budgets, and schedules to meet client commitments and project financial goals.

• Prepare engineering calculations, basis of design reports, dredge plans, cap designs, construction drawings, specifications, and cost estimates for practical, protective sediment remedies.

• Plan investigations and evaluate sediment chemistry, bathymetry, geotechnical conditions, and other site data;

• Evaluate and compare remedial alternatives and their costs and benefits.

• Work with geotechnical, coastal, structural, groundwater modelers and environmental specialists across offices to address cap performance, cap settlement, dredge slope and riverbank stability, erosion, residuals, ground and surface water quality, and adjacent infrastructure.

• Develop approaches for dredging, capping, sediment processing, disposal, and habitat restoration.

• Support pilot studies through vendor coordination, permitting, field planning, and evaluation of results.

• Support contractor procurement, bid evaluation, submittal review, construction oversight, and resolution of field questions and proposed construction changes.

• Direct junior staff on project and field assignments, establish clear safety and technical expectations, verify their interpretation of results, and coach them in design and project management.

• Prepare and review reports, plans, specifications, and proposal content in accordance with project quality requirements.

• Communicate clearly with clients, agencies, contractors, and colleagues.

• Track progress and project costs, communicate status promptly, document and obtain authorization for scope and budget changes, and coordinate timely invoice preparation and follow-up on outstanding payments.

• Strengthen client relationships through reliable project delivery, recognize opportunities for additional work, and support proposals and selected client development activities.

• Travel to attend client meetings and site visits in person, up to 25% of the time depending on project stage.

What Are We Looking For?

Ideal candidates will have the following:

• Bachelor’s degree in civil, environmental, geotechnical, ocean, chemical, or a related engineering discipline.

• 10 to 15 years of relevant engineering experience, including hands-on contaminated sediment remedial design and project or task management.

• Professional Engineer license, or ability to obtain licensure within one year.

• Demonstrated ability to prepare engineering calculations, plans, specifications, cost estimates, and contractor procurement documents for upland and sediment cleanup projects.

• Experience with dredging and capping remedies and the design considerations that affect constructability, performance, and cost.

• Experience coordinating multiple assignments, managing budgets and schedules, tracking project financial performance, and communicating with clients and multidisciplinary teams.

• Working knowledge of CERCLA, RCRA, TSCA, CWA, and applicable state cleanup programs, with experience coordinating with regulatory agencies.

• Ability to work effectively with teams across multiple offices.

• Strong technical writing, communication, problem-solving, and mentoring skills; willingness to travel for project meetings and field assignments.

Preferred Qualifications

• Master’s degree or specialized experience in geotechnical, coastal, or sediment remediation engineering, including experience with dredge slope and riverbank/shoreline stability or cap design.

• Construction oversight or engineering support experience, including submittals, contractor coordination, and change evaluation.

• Environmental consulting experience, Bluebeam Revu and AutoCAD Civil 3D familiarity, and current 40-hour HAZWOPER training.

What Can You Expect?

A collaborative work environment where we encourage everyone to bring their authentic self. We offer competitive compensation and benefits. Benefits are detailed below.
