description:
Request for Proposals: User Experience (UX) Review and Redesign Recommendations for asiapacific.ca

Issued byAsia Pacific Foundation of Canada (APF Canada)RFP reference no.APFC-2026-UX-01Date issuedOctober 22, 2026Questions dueNovember 2, 5:00 p.m. PTProposals dueNovember 23, 5:00 p.m. PTSubmit to[]

1. About APF Canada

The Asia Pacific Foundation of Canada is Canada’s only national public‑purpose institution dedicated exclusively to Canada‑Asia engagement. Our vision is a prosperous, secure Canada shaping its future through high‑impact engagement with Asia, and our mission is to enable Canadians to understand, connect with, and succeed in Asia.

2. Background and Purpose

APF Canada is seeking a qualified UX consultant or firm to conduct an independent, evidence-based review of asiapacific.ca and to deliver clear, prioritized, and implementable recommendations for modernizing the site’s structure, usability, and visual design – without diminishing the visibility of our core research outputs, programs, and networks.

This engagement is a strategic re-design engagement. It is not an implementation contract (see Section 6).

3. Objectives
The successful proponent will help APF Canada achieve the following:

• Understand our audiences. Establish who actually uses asiapacific.ca, what they come for, and where the current experience fails them – grounded in analytics and primary user research, not assumption.

• Simplify the information architecture. Recommend a navigation and content taxonomy that is intelligible to a first-time visitor while still surfacing the full breadth of our research, programs, and networks.

• Make our research findable. Recommend search, filtering, and browsing patterns appropriate to a large and growing publications archive.

• Modernize the visual design. Recommend a contemporary, credible, distinctly APF Canada visual direction appropriate to a national policy institution – clean, readable, and confident rather than decorative.

• Clarify the digital ecosystem. Advise on the relationship between asiapacific.ca and our satellite properties.

4. Timeline

RFP issuedOctober 22, 2026Deadline for written questionsNovember 2, 2026Answers posted to all proponentsNovember 6, 2026

Proposals due

November 23, 2026, 5:00 p.m. PT

Anticipated engagement duration is [14–18] weeks from kickoff. Proponents should propose a schedule aligned to their methodology and flag any dependencies on APF Canada staff availability.

5. Budget

The total budget for this engagement is not to exceed C$30,000, inclusive of all professional fees, participant incentives, software and research tool costs, travel, and applicable taxes.

Proponents must provide a detailed cost breakdown by phase and by deliverable. Where a proponent believes the objectives cannot be fully met within this budget, they should identify which elements they would recommend prioritizing and price optional components separately.

6. Proposal Requirements
Proposals must not exceed 20 pages excluding appendices, CVs, and portfolio samples, and must include:

• Cover letter (1 page) – primary contact, firm overview, and a statement of interest.

Page of

• Understanding of the assignment – your reading of APF Canada’s challenge, based on your own review of asiapacific.ca. We are particularly interested in what you observe that we may not have.

• Proposed approach and methodology – including research methods, participant recruitment strategy, and how you will balance modernization against preservation of our core content.

• Work plan and schedule – phases, milestones, deliverables, and dependencies.

• Team – named individuals, roles, time allocation, and relevant experience. Identify who will lead the engagement and who will conduct research and design. Note any subcontractors.

• Relevant experience – three comparable projects, ideally involving content-heavy, research-driven, mission-based, bilingual, or public-sector organizations. Include client references with contact information (references contacted only for shortlisted proponents).

• Portfolio – samples demonstrating both research rigour and design quality. Where possible, include evidence of measured outcomes.

• Bilingual and accessibility capability – describe your French-language research capacity and your accessibility expertise, including relevant certifications or auditing experience.

• Detailed budget – as described in Section 5.

• Assumptions, exclusions, and requirements of APF Canada.

7. Submission Instructions

Submit proposals as a single PDF to [] with the subject line “APFC-2026-UX-01 – [Proponent Name]” no later than November 23, 2026, 5:00 p.m. Pacific Time. Late submissions will not be considered.

Written questions may be submitted to the same address until November 2, 2026. Questions and answers will be compiled, anonymized, and circulated to all registered proponents to ensure fairness.

Contact: Michael Roberts, Communications Director, Asia Pacific Foundation of Canada,

• Experience with multiplayer, live-service or competitive shooter UI, including HUDs, scoreboards, matchmaking, stores and battle passes.

title: ​​Civil Design Engineer II/III​
description:
Role Summary

As a Civil Design Engineer II/III, you will design the site layouts, grading, drainage, and access roads that make utility-scale solar PV and battery energy storage projects buildable. Civil design sets a project’s footprint on the land and shapes how it is permitted, priced, and constructed. You will turn survey, geotechnical, and site constraint data into civil land development sheet sets in AutoCAD and Civil 3D, working with structural, electrical, environmental, and project management colleagues to deliver projects that bring more renewable generation onto the grid.

As an employee-owner, you will share in the results of the work and help build a team where careful, well-documented engineering earns the trust of clients and colleagues. Candidates may be considered at either the Engineer II or Engineer III level depending on experience, technical depth, independence, and demonstrated ability to lead scope.

Duties & Responsibilities

Across both levels, this role may include:

Core Technical & Functional Responsibilities

• Create site layouts and civil land development sheet sets in AutoCAD and Civil 3D for utility-scale and commercial solar PV and battery energy storage projects.

• Design site grading, earthwork, and surface drainage that balance constructability, cost, and site performance.

• Lay out access roads, internal roads, and laydown areas that meet project and jurisdictional requirements.

• Prepare stormwater management and erosion and sediment control plans with supporting calculations.

• Evaluate site constraints such as topography, setbacks, wetlands, and floodplains, and develop layouts that respond to them.

• Prepare drawings, calculations, and technical documentation for development, permitting, and issued-for-construction packages.

• Evaluate, select, and apply standard civil design methods, adapt them for nonroutine site conditions, and bring unconventional problems to senior engineers for review.

Project & Portfolio Execution

• Lead small civil projects, or defined portions of larger ones, from kickoff through issued-for-construction.

• Help determine schedule and budget requirements for assigned civil scope, and report progress and risks to the project lead.

• Assign tasks to and coordinate work with designers and discipline team members to complete assignments.

• Track design changes and update deliverables when project inputs change.

Quality, Standards & Compliance

• Ensure designs comply with company, industry, trade, and jurisdictional standards, practices, and codes.

• Follow Revamp QA/QC procedures, self-check drawings and calculations, and resolve review comments before issue.

• Document design criteria and assumptions so reviewers and clients can verify the basis of design.

Collaboration & Communication

• Coordinate with structural, electrical, environmental, and project management staff on site layouts, equipment pads, and access.

• Coordinate with clients, project managers, and subcontractors on project expectations and design inputs.

• Attend project meetings and present specific aspects of civil design assignments.

Additional Expectations at the Engineer III Level

• Lead multiple civil projects at once, preparing and owning scope, schedule, and budget for assigned work.

• Independently formulate and solve complex grading, drainage, and site design problems, seeking guidance only on unconventional conditions.

• Support client interaction for multiple projects in a portfolio, including design reviews and technical clarifications.

• Develop work plans for project tasks, and assign and direct the work of discipline team members.

• Mentor Engineer I and II staff and review their drawings and calculations.

• Assist with proposals for professional engineering services.

• Act as Engineer of Record on civil design packages when licensed and assigned.

Additional Responsibilities

• Perform essential duties including meeting deliverables and deadlines.

• Perform additional related duties as assigned or directed.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering or a related field, or similar applicable work experience.

• Civil engineering design and drafting experience: typically 2+ years for Engineer II and 5+ years for Engineer III.

• Working proficiency in AutoCAD and Civil 3D.

• Experience preparing civil land development sheet sets, including grading, site drainage, and access road design.

• Working knowledge of civil engineering principles, standards, and codes for site development.

• Ability to identify and solve complex design problems and document the engineering judgment behind them.

• Effective written and verbal communication skills.

• Ability to manage multiple projects at once, prioritize work, and meet deadlines.

Preferred Qualifications

• Engineer in Training (EIT) certification or Professional Engineer (PE) license.

• Experience with utility-scale solar PV or battery energy storage projects.

• Advanced grading design experience on large, complex sites.

• Experience with stormwater management or erosion and sediment control design.

• Working knowledge of GIS software.

Benefits for Full-Time Positions

• Participation in Revamp’s Employee Ownership ESOP program.

• Competitive compensation with bonus.

• Full benefits package offerings including 99% employer-paid health, vision, life, and dental insurance.

• Medical, dependent care, and commuter FSA.

• Monthly health and wellness stipend.

• Attractive vacation, sick, and holiday pay.

• Paid parental leave.

• 401(k) savings plan with 100% match up to 6%, vested immediately.

• Paid volunteer time off and charitable donation matching.

About Revamp

Founded in 2016, Revamp is the premier employee-owned engineering design firm dedicated to advancing large-scale renewable energy projects. Our team is united by a shared commitment to accelerating the global energy transition and creating a workplace where talented people can make a tangible impact in the fight against climate change.

As employee-owners, we take pride in building a culture of collaboration, innovation, and accountability where every individual’s contribution drives both company success and personal growth. Revamp engineers have supported the design of more than 10% of the utility-scale solar generation capacity in the US since 2020, contributing directly to the renewable energy transformation.

So much more than just an engineering firm; we are a diverse, international team of artists, singers, dancers, pastry chefs, outdoor enthusiasts, animal lovers, travelers and problem-solvers who bring curiosity and creativity to everything we do. For more information, visit www.revamp‑eng.com.

Disclaimers

Employment with Revamp Engineering Inc. may be subject to background checks that are permitted by applicable law and relevant to the position. Any such checks will be conducted in compliance with all legal requirements, including providing notice, obtaining consent where required, and allowing candidates to access and correct personal information as permitted by law.

Revamp Engineering Inc. is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating an inclusive workplace. We provide equal employment opportunities without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law. We value diversity and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply. Revamp Engineering Inc. is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities. If you require an accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact us.

title: Lead Product Designer
description:
About ECP

ECP is a market-leading SaaS solution that enables senior living communities to better care for their residents. ECP is used in over 8,000 communities. We're looking to further expand by increasing the number of customers that use our software and increasing the scope of how we serve our customers by developing and releasing new products.

Senior living is deeply under-penetrated with software and ECP is one of the largest and fastest-growing software companies in the industry. We recently raised a growth round of equity to reinvest in our product, technology, and go-to-market. Our mission is to build world-class software that improves the quality of life for seniors and improves clinical, business, compliance, and operational performance for our customers.

Role Overview

ECP is hiring a Lead Product Designer to lead our product experience and be a true thought partner to product and engineering leadership. Reporting to our VP of Product, you'll shape the experience across our full suite (clinical, CRM and billing), modernizing what customers use today and defining what we build next. Our goal is the best-looking, easiest-to-use software in senior living, with AI that takes work off the plates of community staff and operators.

This is a hands-on IC role. You'll start as our sole designer, with the opportunity to grow into leading design as the team expands. We want someone who will obsess over our product, our industry, our customers and their pain points.

Who You'll Design For

Our users run senior living communities: caregivers, nurses, med techs, sales and leasing teams, business office staff and executive directors. They work long, busy shifts, often on shared devices, and staff turnover means many are new to the job. Every extra click or confusing screen costs them time they'd rather spend with residents.

That's why ease of use is non-negotiable: workflows should take as few steps as possible and be learnable without training.

Responsibilities

• Design vision. Set and own the design vision across the product suite, establish process and quality standards, and be the voice of the user in roadmap conversations. Mentor designers as the team grows.

• Business impact. Tie design work to business outcomes such as adoption, customer satisfaction and sales win rates. Define how success is measured and use the results to guide what you design next.

• Craft and simplicity. Own the visual direction that makes us the best-looking software in our market. Remove steps, reduce clicks and push back on complexity users don't need. Design experiences that work seamlessly across desktop, tablet and mobile.

• AI feature design. Lead AI-powered features from concept through launch. Define how users interact with AI and how they review, trust and correct its outputs. Look for places where AI can remove work entirely, not just assist with it.

• Design system. Build and evolve a design system, starting where it has the most impact, and drive adoption with engineering so our products look and behave consistently. Set it up in Claude so PMs can build on-brand prototypes themselves.

• Customer research. Join customer calls, visit communities, shadow staff on shift and run usability tests. Keep personas current and track competitor and AI trends.

• Execution and collaboration. Deliver wireframes, mockups and working prototypes built in code with AI tools, provide development-ready specs, and resolve tradeoffs directly with PMs and engineering. Present and defend decisions with evidence.

• Accessibility. Set accessibility standards aligned to WCAG and champion them with engineering.

Requirements

• 7+ years of product or UX design experience, including leading design for a product area end to end, mentoring other designers and presenting confidently to leadership, and tying design decisions to measurable business outcomes.

• A portfolio showing exceptional visual and interaction craft, including examples of simplifying complex workflows and designing responsive experiences across desktop, tablet and mobile.

• Experience shipping AI-powered features that real users rely on, with a solid grasp of AI UX patterns (setting expectations, showing sources, handling errors, keeping humans in control).

• Experience building or significantly evolving a design system and driving adoption, including setting it up in Claude so PMs can build with it.

• Expert in Figma and fluent in using Claude to iterate quickly, including building working prototypes in code that give engineering something functional, not just a mockup.

• Hands-on user research and usability testing.

• Working knowledge of WCAG accessibility standards, with experience tracking and fixing violations.

Preferred qualifications

• Experience designing healthcare, senior living or other regulated-industry software, especially AI features where accuracy and trust matter.

• Experience supporting multiple product lines, including scaling a design system across them.

• Experience as an early or sole designer, or building a design team.

• Bachelor's degree in design, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Cross-Functional Delivery

We're a passionate team united by three cultural drivers:

Impact – We do work that matters.

Collaboration – We are in it together.

Human touch – We care deeply.

We're also embracing AI, both in how we work and in the products we build. We're looking for people who share our curiosity about emerging technologies and are excited to explore their potential responsibly.

What you will be doing

As a Senior Product Designer within our Clinical team, you'll design experiences that support healthcare professionals in making decisions, documenting care and managing complex clinical workflows.

You'll also help evolve how our design team works, using AI and emerging technologies to explore ideas, learn faster and deliver better outcomes.

At this level, we expect you to work with a high degree of autonomy, independently owning complex design challenges and influence decisions beyond your immediate workstream.

We're looking for someone who combines strong design fundamentals with sound judgement, curiosity and a constructive approach to collaboration.

Key skills and experience

• Complex, high-risk product experience – Proven experience designing clinical systems or similarly high-risk software, where errors can have significant consequences. Experience working alongside safety, risk or regulatory specialists.

• Excellent design craft – Strong UX, interaction and visual design skills, with a portfolio demonstrating complex workflows, accessible interfaces and shipped product experiences.

• Innovation and safety judgement – Ability to explore ambitious solutions while understanding risk, recognising trade-offs and knowing when a simpler, more predictable approach is appropriate.

• Work alongside an inspiring team – our two founders have started Semble after a successful startup exit, and your future colleagues are all knowledgeable and innovators in their field.

Diversity and inclusion

description:

Newsweek Recognizes Sedgwick as America’s Greatest Workplaces National Top Companies

Certified as a Great Place to Work®

Fortune Best Workplaces in Financial Services & Insurance
UX Designer – Sedgwick AI
PRIMARY PURPOSE OF THE ROLE: The UX AI Designer within the Transformation Office serves as a senior user experience and product design professional responsible for shaping intuitive, human-centered AI experiences that support large-scale business transformation. This role translates complex artificial intelligence capabilities, including Generative AI, agentic workflows, LLM-powered tools, and conversational interfaces, into accessible, effective, and scalable user experiences across enterprise systems, Lines of Business, and operational workflows.

Operating at the intersection of user experience design, product strategy, AI innovation, and business transformation, the UX AI Designer partners closely with AI architects, product owners, engineering teams, data teams, business stakeholders, and end users to design AI-enabled experiences that are practical, trustworthy, and aligned with business outcomes. This role plays a critical part in ensuring AI solutions are not only technically sound, but also usable, explainable, governed, and adopted effectively by colleagues and clients.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES MAY INCLUDE

• Leads the user experience strategy and design direction for AI-enabled products, tools, platforms, and workflows, ensuring solutions are intuitive, accessible, scalable, and aligned with enterprise transformation objectives.

• Designs user experiences for Generative AI platforms, conversational AI tools, agentic AI systems, copilots, chat-based interfaces, recommendation tools, and workflow automation solutions that support complex business processes.

• Partners with AI architects, engineers, product owners, business leaders, and end users to translate advanced AI capabilities into practical, user-centered designs that improve productivity, decision-making, and operational efficiency.

• Develops user journeys, personas, service blueprints, wireframes, prototypes, interaction models, and usability flows that define how colleagues and clients engage with AI-enabled solutions across systems and processes.

• Designs conversational and prompt-based experiences, including user prompts, interaction patterns, response flows, escalation paths, feedback loops, and human-in-the-loop review experiences.

• Applies human-centered design principles to ensure AI tools are transparent, explainable, trustworthy, and easy to adopt, with a strong focus on minimizing user friction and supporting responsible AI use.

• Conducts user research, stakeholder interviews, usability testing, journey mapping, and feedback sessions to identify user needs, pain points, adoption barriers, and opportunities for AI-driven process improvement.

• Collaborates with data, analytics, engineering, and platform teams to ensure AI experiences are informed by accurate data, appropriate context, sound design logic, and clear user expectations.

• Supports the design of enterprise AI governance experiences, including consent, disclosure, confidence indicators, explainability, exception handling, auditability, and user feedback mechanisms.

• Creates design standards, reusable interaction patterns, and UX best practices for enterprise AI solutions to promote consistency across AI products, platforms, and digital experiences.

• Partners with change management, communications, training, and business readiness teams to support user adoption, colleague enablement, and effective rollout of AI-enabled tools.

• Evaluates the effectiveness of AI experiences through qualitative and quantitative measures, including usability outcomes, adoption metrics, user satisfaction, task completion, productivity impact, and feedback trends.

ADDITIONAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

• Provides design guidance, coaching, and thought leadership to product teams, delivery teams, and business stakeholders on effective AI experience design.

• Contributes to the evolution of enterprise AI design standards, product strategy, tooling, and governance practices within the Transformation Office.

• Stays current on emerging AI design trends, human-AI interaction models, responsible AI practices, conversational design, and enterprise UX best practices.

• Supports cross-functional workshops, discovery sessions, design reviews, and stakeholder presentations related to AI-enabled transformation initiatives.

• Performs other duties as assigned.

• Travel as required.

QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor’s degree in User Experience Design, Human-Computer Interaction, Product Design, Interaction Design, Cognitive Science, Psychology, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field from an accredited college or university required. Master’s degree in Human-Computer Interaction, Design Strategy, Human Factors, AI Interaction Design, or a related discipline preferred.

Experience

• Seven (7) years of related experience in user experience design, product design, digital experience strategy, or human-centered design, with at least three (3) years supporting AI-enabled products, enterprise platforms, digital transformation initiatives, conversational interfaces, automation tools, or complex workflow design required.

• Experience designing user experiences for Generative AI, conversational AI, copilots, workflow automation, decision-support tools, enterprise software, or data-driven platforms strongly preferred.

• Experience working in complex corporate environments with cross-functional teams, including product, engineering, data, analytics, security, risk, compliance, operations, and business leadership preferred.

• Equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.

Skills & Knowledge

• Strong ability to translate complex AI, data, and technical concepts into clear, intuitive, and user-centered digital experiences.

• Advanced knowledge of UX design methods, including user research, journey mapping, service design, wireframing, prototyping, usability testing, accessibility, and design systems.

• Demonstrated understanding of human-AI interaction principles, including explainability, trust, transparency, user control, ethical AI use, feedback loops, and human-in-the-loop design.

• Experience designing conversational interfaces, chat-based experiences, prompt flows, AI-assisted workflows, decision-support experiences, or intelligent automation tools.

• Proficiency with design and collaboration tools such as Figma, FigJam, Miro, Adobe Creative Suite, or similar platforms.

• Strong understanding of product development lifecycles, agile delivery practices, enterprise technology environments, and cross-functional delivery models.

• Ability to partner effectively with AI architects, data scientists, software engineers, product owners, business stakeholders, and change management teams.

• Strong communication, facilitation, storytelling, and presentation skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders and clearly articulate design decisions.

• Ability to balance user needs, business objectives, technical feasibility, governance requirements, and operational constraints.

• Knowledge of accessibility standards and inclusive design principles.

• Ability to work in a team environment.

• Ability to meet or exceed Performance Competencies.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

When applicable and appropriate, consideration will be given to reasonable accommodations.

Mental: Clear and conceptual thinking ability; excellent judgment, troubleshooting, problem solving, analysis, and discretion; ability to handle work-related stress; ability to handle multiple priorities simultaneously; and ability to meet deadlines

Physical: Computer keyboarding, travel as required

Auditory/Visual: Hearing, vision and talking

description:
Real opportunities. Real impact. Your career, redefined.

(NOTE: A human reviews every application at Oceans, so please apply for only one position and only once a year—if you're a better fit for another role, we’ll route your application accordingly and if we’re not quite ready for you, we’ll reach back out later.)

At Oceans, we believe that talent knows no boundaries. That’s why we connect the best and brightest professionals with career-defining opportunities that challenge, inspire, and accelerate their career growth. Our community, whom we call Divers, don’t just work—they dive deep, solve complex challenges, and make a real impact with global industry leaders. And in doing so, they don’t just support bold ideas—they expand their skills, broaden their expertise, and grow their careers.

As a Senior Graphic Designer, you will join a fast-growing digital operations team within a dynamic beauty and hair-care brand expanding across LATAM. Operating as part of a high-output creative team, you will be responsible for producing consistent, performance-oriented visual content across paid advertising, organic social, email marketing,landing pages, and e-commerce touchpoints.

In this hands-on design role, you will take ownership of maintaining visual consistency across digital channels using established brand guidelines, reusable templates, and organized design systems. You will balance creative direction with production efficiency to deliver high-quality static, motion, and marketplace assets at speed.

Accountability

As a Senior Graphic Designer, your success will be defined by your ability to maintain visual brand consistency, maintain high creative production volume, minimize revision rounds, and produce effective assets that support digital performance goals.

Here’s how you’ll make an impact:

Brand Identity & Visual Consistency

• Maintain visual identity and standards across digital touchpoints, ensuring every asset remains recognizably aligned with brand guidelines.

• Apply standardized typography, colors, layouts, imagery, and design treatments across all customer-facing materials.

• Maintain, update, and manage brand style guides, reusable design templates, and organized asset libraries to streamline high-volume production.
Partner with creative leadership to enforce visual standards and prevent brand dilution across channels.

Paid Advertising Creative Execution

• Design high-converting static and motion advertisements for paid digital and social campaigns.

• Produce weekly ad sets containing multiple creative variations, alternative layouts, and messaging treatments.

• Translate campaign briefs and performance feedback into optimized visual concepts that improve creative effectiveness.

• Deliver advertising assets rapidly to support high-velocity testing and campaign deadlines.

Social Media & Email Design

• Design creative graphics and layouts for organic social media channels to engage target audiences.

• Craft visually compelling email marketing designs and promotional templates that maintain lifecycle consistency.

• Adapt visual concepts across different formats, aspect ratios, and campaign goals while collaborating with the broader creative team.

Landing Page & E-Commerce Visuals

• Design visual assets for landing pages, product detail pages (PDPs), and marketplace listings.

• Create, optimize, and refresh product detail page imagery for DTC storefronts and sales platforms including Amazon and TikTok Shop.

• Ensure product visuals clearly communicate key features, benefits, and usage instructions while aligning with visual identity standards.

Motion Graphics & Design Variations

• Produce animated graphics, motion-based ad creatives, and dynamic visual treatments from static design briefs.

• Develop multiple variations of top-performing creative assets to support ad iteration and prevent ad fatigue.

• Implement automated resizing and efficient design workflows to maintain speed and visual quality across all output formats.

Colleagues

You will report directly to the Creative Director as your primary functional manager while collaborating closely with the Chief Marketing Officer and cross-functional creative partners, including video editors, copywriters, and performance marketers. At Oceans, you’ll also receive guidance and support from your Operations Manager, who will help you succeed in the role and ensure that you’re continuously growing and developing in your career.

Skills and Qualifications

At Oceans, we believe in T-shaped individuals—those who bring deep expertise in one area,paired with broad curiosity and interests. As a Senior Graphic Designer, your vertical strength will be DTC visual asset creation and template design systems, while your horizontal capabilities should span channel-specific creative optimization, motion design, and cross-functional campaign execution.

To excel in this role, you should have:

•
Experience: Proven graphic design experience within DTC, e-commerce, beauty, hair-care, or consumer goods brands, with a strong portfolio showcasing multi-channel digital design.

•
Tools/Systems: Advanced proficiency in Figma, Adobe Creative Suite, and Canva; experience with AI-assisted design, image generation tools, and automated resizing workflows is preferred.

•
Analytics/Process: Strong background in executing creative briefs independently, managing design template libraries, and adapting visuals for e-commerce platforms like Amazon PDPs and TikTok Shop.

•
Mindset: High production speed, meticulous attention to visual detail, low revision requirements, and a collaborative approach to performance feedback.

During the interview process, you’ll have the opportunity to showcase your skills in the following areas:

•
Brand Consistency & Systems: How do you maintain and scale visual brand standards across channels using reusable template systems?

•
Paid Advertising Design: How do you design static and motion ad assets structured for digital conversion?

•
Multi-Channel Adaptation: How do you adapt design concepts across social media, email, PDPs, Amazon, and TikTok Shop listings?

•
Production Speed & Efficiency: How do you manage high-volume creative production and fast turnarounds with minimal revision rounds?

Diversity of experience is core to Oceans. You are expected to work inclusively with individuals from a variety of backgrounds, ensuring that both personal and collective dignity are supported.

Role Specifications

This is a remote role, where you will be expected to work a split shift with some overlap with our client’s time zone. You will, however, be expected to be present for in-person training programs during your first 3.5 weeks with us. During the offer process, we’ll share more information about our benefits and compensation philosophy, considering both market trends and individual factors.

About Oceans

At Oceans Talent, we connect the world’s top talent with visionary companies building what’s next. Here, you’re not just stepping into another role — you’re joining a team that values individuality, ambition, and growth without limits. Unique, like you.

We’re always excited to share more about our journey, where we’re headed, and how you can grow with us throughout the interview process.

DESIGN DIRECTOR ROLE AT SKETCHDECK

This role has four key focuses:

• Partner with Business Development & Project Managers to build and deliver creative pitches

• Lead overall design / brand / creative vision within your accounts

• Lead high-level creative projects

• Mentoring your team to support projects of all sizes and scopes

This role will work closely with the Project Managers to oversee the team's work and success. You’ll report directly to the VP, Creative Impact.

You’ll succeed in this role if you have great client skills, strong and efficient design processes, prioritization and project management skills and an entrepreneurial instinct. If you enjoy working with clients to elevate their creativity and have experience supporting larger corporate accounts with ambitious goals, this role will be a great fit for you.

SketchDeck is an entrepreneurial environment. You’ll be expected to jump into new work and help other teams. Priorities can shift quickly with clients’ condensed timelines

As the Design Director, you’ll have three (3) areas of responsibilities:

CLIENT PROJECTS: (65%)

• Partner with Project Managers on project scoping and estimates on higher creative projects

• Support larger corporate accounts with shifting priorities and time-sensitive deadlines.

• Lead kick-off calls (internal/external), creative presentations and problem-solving meetings with clients, Project Managers and Designers

• Feel comfortable brainstorming ideas live during client calls. Think quickly during client conversations, proposing creative ideas, asking focused questions, and adapting recommendations as new information emerges.

• Shift efficiently between accounts and tasks, reassessing priorities and communicating tradeoffs as needs change.

• Identify which projects could benefit from high-level strategic input vs. more production-focused projects that could be led by a Brand Manager

• Communication/coordination of project needs, timelines, team skills and creative staff availability with Project Managers

• Set up briefs, provide creative direction and inspiration to the design team on projects

• Work with the Project Manager defining workflow and scope of work for the team

• Lead communication from brainstorm to final production

• Provide creative reviews and feedback to designers

• Decide who should work on each project, building collaborative and strategy-led teams for creative projects

• Drive design excellence, knowing when to push creative boundaries, and not settling for the status quo

ACCOUNTS, BRAND STRATEGY AND NEW BUSINESS: (25%)

• Lead the onboarding of new client accounts by reviewing brand materials, setting up brand pages, and ensuring seamless integration into our workflow. Ask the right questions to uncover client goals, setting the foundation for a strong partnership.

• Build collaborative, creative partner relationships with our clients

• Learn and understand our clients goals and how to best support them creatively

• Master clients’ brand guidelines and preferences

• Maintain and improve account-level design quality

• Train designers on keeping brand pages, templates, Adobe CC libraries and brand assets in general updated

• Push existing brands’ creative boundaries and finding new opportunities to elevate brands

• Train and mentor Designers and Brand Managers on brands

title: Fractional Senior Game Designer
description:
About Exient

Exient is an independent games studio with a long track record of building and operating high-quality titles for mobile and beyond. Our portfolio spans original IP and world-renowned franchises, and our teams work across the full lifecycle, from concept and prototyping through live operations and ongoing content. We are a small and highly collaborative studio where designers have real ownership over the features they ship.

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced Senior Game Designer to join us on a contract basis to strengthen our design capacity across multiple live and upcoming projects. This is a hands-on role for someone who can hit the ground running: contributing complex design work from day one, raising the quality and velocity of the team, and helping to advance our AI-assisted design workflows.I

This is a distinct, self-directed contractor engagement. You will operate as an independent supplier of design services under a contract for services, using your own judgement and working methods to deliver agreed outcomes across our project roadmap.

You will work closely with our existing design, art, engineering, and production disciplines to design, balance, and polish key features, and to flex onto proposals, pitches, and new opportunities as they arise.

What You'll Work On

As a Senior Game Designer at Exient, you'll play a central role in the design of our live mobile games, with Lemmings, one of gaming's most iconic franchises, at the heart of your work. This is a hands-on role for someone who can own features end to end and thrive across multiple projects at once.

Day to day, you'll:

• Own feature and systems design for live free-to-play games. This means taking ideas from opportunity and concept through to detailed, implementation-ready documentation, then tuning and balancing them post-launch. It spans everything from onboarding and early-retention flows to monetisation, economy and live-ops events.

• Design against data and player behaviour, working closely with Product, Analytics and Production to shape decisions around KPIs, retention and revenue, validate ideas through A/B testing, and turn insights into clear, actionable design.

• Deliver a steady stream of seasonal and event content, keeping our games fresh through regular seasons, events and live-ops moments, often to external client and platform requirements.

• Work across a varied portfolio. Lemmings is the core focus, but you'll also contribute to our wider slate of live and partner titles, taking ownership of your projects and balancing priorities as they shift.

• Contribute to new concepts and pitches, helping shape GDDs, proposals and concept pitches for prospective projects and partners, including competitive analysis and scoping.

• Design within real-world constraints, building features that meet evolving compliance and regulatory requirements as part of a responsible, player-first approach.

• Help push our craft and ways of working forward, including making the most of AI-assisted design workflows, which are increasingly part of how our team works.

• Partner across disciplines, working closely with artists, engineers and producers to take designs from documentation through to polished, well-integrated features in the game.

• Prototype and pressure-test ideas quickly, using rapid iteration and playtesting to refine gameplay and feel before committing to full production.

You'll be a senior, autonomous member of a small, collaborative team, trusted to lead your own work, raise the bar on quality, and support and mentor those around you.

This list is indicative rather than exhaustive. The specific mix of work will flex with the studio's roadmap and priorities during the engagement.

AI-Assisted Design Workflow

You'll help elevate the AI-assisted ways of working already part of our design process. Our focus is workflow AI, using AI tools to work faster and smarter. The ideal contractor already treats these tools as part of their everyday craft and knows when to rely on them and when not to.

We're looking for practical, demonstrable experience using AI to accelerate design work, for example:

• Ideation: generating and stress-testing divergent ideas at speed, then applying senior judgement to select what's worth building.

• Structured specification: turning rough mechanics into explicit rule sets, state tables, and documentation ready to critique and prototype.

• Economy and balance: accelerating the arithmetic-heavy work of curves, progression, and tuning tables, then validating through playtesting.

• Rapid prototyping: reaching a playable, testable prototype faster, so more time goes on judgement, feel, and polish.

• Documentation and iteration: drafting and maintaining design documentation, and feeding playtest results into the next iteration.

Just as important is knowing where human taste is irreplaceable: the strongest designers use AI to reach a playable build faster, then spend their judgement where it counts.

Experience & Qualifications

• A minimum of five years' game design experience, the majority within a mobile games company.

• A demonstrable track record of shipping and operating live mobile titles.

• A degree in Games Design, Interactive Media, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

• Experience working on complex design projects in a fast-paced, multi-project environment.

• A portfolio or case studies that show senior-level design thinking across mechanics, economy, and player experience.

Technical Skills

• Strong command of core-loop, meta-game, game balance, economy, and monetisation models.

• Excellent understanding of UI / UX and a strong sense of game flow, pacing, and player experience.

• Ability to conceptualise, prototype, and implement game concepts using a range of tools, and to iterate from data and player feedback.

• Practical, hands-on experience integrating AI tools into a design workflow (as described above).

• Proficiency with design tooling such as Figma, Unity, Git, Jira, Confluence and Claude.

• Confident with data: reading analytics, forming hypotheses, and using KPIs to guide balancing decisions.

• Broad knowledge of games, with genuine passion for casual, mobile, and classic arcade genres.

Ways of Working

• Self-motivated, organised, and able to deliver reliably while working largely autonomously.

• Clear written and verbal communication in English, with the ability to document and present design decisions.

• Collaborative and dependable when working across disciplines and time zones.

• Strong sense of accountability and ownership, with openness to self-critique and constructive feedback.

• Comfortable moving between projects and adapting quickly to shifting priorities.

title: Product Designer (AI-Native, B2B)
description:
About Simulmedia

Since 2008, Simulmedia has helped brands and agencies turn TV into a measurable growth channel. Our AI-powered media platform for planning, activating, and measuring campaigns works across linear, local, and connected TV.

Everyone here owns problems end-to-end, and our design team is small, so your decisions ship and matter.

About the role

Think about it as a mix of a product manager's mindset with a strong design vertical skills. Design here is AI-first and builder-led. We expect you to take a problem, define ways to solve it, identify the best ways to shape the output, and involve stakeholders throughout the solution's development. Your output might be a Figma design mockup, a prototype, shipped production code, a PRD, or a decision document.

What you'll do

•
Own problems end to end. Define the problem with your PM and engineers, decide what should exist at all, explore options, validate them, and ship improvements that move key metrics. Stay with the work after handoff.

•
Work across the business. Client-facing products, internal tools, sales enablement, or customer experience, depending on priorities.

•
Start in writing. Use AI to clarify hypotheses, surface risks and edge cases, write short PRDs or decision documents. Sometimes the document is the final outcome: not every problem needs a UI solution.

•
Use research to go faster. Talk to sales managers, customer success managers, and internal users, run quick tests, and adjust direction based on what you learn. Use research to speed up decisions, not block them.

•
Prototype with AI. Build and iterate on flows in Claude Code, Cursor, or similar. AI writes the code, and you own structure, behavior, and UX quality.

•
UI Design. When it makes sense, turn validated concepts into production-ready designs with every state covered and aligned with our design system.

•
Ship with engineers. You'll occasionally ship small UI fixes to production; engineers own production code, and your share can grow over time.

What we expect from you

• 3+ years as a product designer on complex B2B products with dense, data-heavy interfaces: tables, filters, reporting, multi-role flows.

• A portfolio that shows product thinking, interaction design, and craft

• At least several products you've built or prototyped in code with AI tools.

• You proactively build domain and technical knowledge and get up to speed quickly on new problems.

• Comfort in Claude Code, or similar: you can work in an existing codebase and get a prototype running without waiting for an engineer.

• Good UI skills: your mockups are neat, balanced, and focused on user value.

• Based anywhere in Ukraine

• English at B2+ (upper-intermediate) or higher.

Nice to have

• Ad tech, media, or analytics/reporting product experience.

• A public GitHub or shipped side projects.

• Experience in data visualization

• Interest in growing your product management and engineering skills alongside design.

How we hire

Apply with a link to your portfolio. The process has three steps:

•
Technical interview. Walk us through your portfolio and how you work: your research, how you prototype, and the decisions behind one project you built.

•
Test task. We'd like to understand how you operate within an new domain and are ready to defend your own work

•
Product manager interview. Product thinking and collaboration: how you define problems and success, prioritize, and work with a PM day to day.

We’re seeking the self-motivated, the hard-working, the problem solvers, and the dedicated to join our team of experts. Ingenuity, adaptation, and evolution are at the core for us at Cavallo.

Our Grand Rapids-based headquarters is focused on helping change the way organizations do business through our software products, customizations, expertise, and support. title: Network Designer, IP & Services
description:
We are seeking a Network Designer, IP & Services to design and develop networks and services delivered across fibre, coaxial, fixed wireless, and transport infrastructure. This role is responsible for creating the technical blueprints that support Internet, voice, video, core and transport networks, as well as corporate LAN and WLAN environments. Responsibilities include developing network architectures, detailed designs, capacity plans, bills of material (BOMs), and technical standards that ensure networks are scalable, reliable, and efficient.

A key focus of this position is establishing and maintaining standardized network and service designs. The successful candidate will work closely with technical and project teams to develop reference architectures, design standards, and documentation that support new deployments, network expansions, capacity upgrades, and technology lifecycle initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

Architecture & Standards

• Develop and maintain reference architectures for Internet, voice, video, core routing and transport services, and corporate LAN/WLAN environments.

• Establish design standards, naming conventions, IP addressing schemes, and documentation templates.

• Incorporate security, resiliency, scalability, and operational requirements into all network designs.

• Ensure adherence to established standards while documenting approved deviations.

• Collaborate with operations and engineering teams to continuously refine and improve design standards.

Network & Service Design

• Produce high-level and low-level designs for new services, network expansions, and infrastructure upgrades.

• Design broadband service delivery platforms across FTTH, MDU, coaxial, and fixed wireless access environments.

• Design voice, IPTV, OTT, multicast, and QoS-enabled service solutions.

• Develop designs for IP/MPLS core networks, DWDM transport systems, and carrier interconnections.

• Define standards and architectures for corporate networking environments, including LAN and WLAN infrastructure.

Capacity & Lifecycle Planning

• Develop utilization forecasts and capacity plans for core, transport, access, and service platforms.

• Create lifecycle management plans identifying end-of-life infrastructure and recommended replacement strategies.

• Evaluate design options to improve network capacity, resiliency, performance, and scalability.

• Contribute to long-term technology and network roadmap planning.

Design Documentation & Records Management

• Create implementation-ready design packages, including technical documentation, diagrams, routing policies, IP/VLAN assignments, QoS requirements, and acceptance criteria.

• Review deployment and commissioning results to ensure alignment with design objectives.

• Maintain accurate network records, diagrams, and addressing documentation within network management tools.

• Reconcile design records with as-built field information.

Materials, Estimating & Procurement Support

• Prepare bills of material for network hardware, optics, software licensing, and related infrastructure.

• Develop cost estimates for projects, capital planning, and funding initiatives.

• Evaluate vendor solutions and emerging technologies through documentation reviews, vendor engagement, and proof-of-concept testing.

• Support business cases, funding applications, and project reporting requirements with accurate design and cost information.

Collaboration & Project Support

• Work closely with Project Managers to support project schedules and identify design risks and dependencies.

• Coordinate with outside plant, transport, facilities, and power teams to ensure integrated design solutions.

• Review designs with operational and engineering teams prior to implementation.

• Provide technical guidance and support during project delivery and deployment activities.

• Respond to design-related inquiries and support troubleshooting efforts during implementation.

Required Qualifications

• Diploma or degree in Networking, Telecommunications, Engineering Technology, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent industry experience.

• Minimum of five (5) years of experience in network design, network engineering, or architecture within a telecommunications or service provider environment.

• Strong knowledge of IP routing and switching technologies, including BGP, OSPF, MPLS, EVPN, and QoS.

• Working knowledge of service provider access and transport technologies, including GPON, XGS-PON, DOCSIS, DWDM, IPTV multicast, and VoIP.

• Experience producing detailed network designs, diagrams, IP addressing plans, and technical documentation.

• Experience in network capacity planning, lifecycle management, and infrastructure modernization.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to produce clear technical documentation.

• Ability to work independently and collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.

• Ability to manage confidential and sensitive network information.

• Successful completion of a background check.

• Eligibility to obtain and maintain Government of Canada security clearance.

.

title: Executive Creative Director
description:
About Oxford Road

Oxford Road is the world’s largest podcast advertising agency. We unite brands and creators through strategy and technology for outcomes only we can deliver.

Since the beginning of podcasting, we’ve been here building the playbook, setting the standards, and scaling brands through the power of audio and creator-driven media. Today, we manage campaigns across podcasts, radio, streaming audio, YouTube, and emerging creator platforms for clients that include half of the top advertisers in podcasting.

What really sets us apart? We’re not just buying media. We’re shaping the market itself.

Our thought leadership defines the conversation. Our newsletter reaches thousands of industry decision-makers every week. Our podcast, The Media Roundtable, convenes the most influential voices in audio advertising. Our annual Chief Audio Officer Summit is the premier gathering for marketers, platforms, and creators shaping the future of the medium. Our research (from attribution methodologies to brand safety frameworks) becomes industry standard.

We don’t wait for the market to tell us what’s next. We build it.

The Role

The Executive Creative Director is Oxford Road's most senior creative leader, accountable for the quality, performance, and culture of everything the Creative department produces across host-read, pre-produced audio, and bespoke 360-degree campaigns. This role owns the creative standard across every client account, not just the highest-profile ones, and is responsible for ensuring that standard is consistently met, measurably tied to results, and strengthened by every test the team runs.

This is a leadership role built around three commitments: quality on everything that ships, creative tied to performance, and testing built in as a standard practice rather than an afterthought. The ECD is the keeper of the craft and the driver of the creative department's contribution to client outcomes, agency growth, and new business.

Scope of Ownership

• Owns creative quality end-to-end across all client accounts: reviewing work in flight before it ships, closing the feedback loop to writers directly, and maintaining a consistent standard across host-read and pre-produced disciplines

• Owns how Audiolytics is used across the department: as a benchmark and coaching tool integrated with compliance and performance data, not as a checkbox exercise

• Owns the talent onboarding, briefing, and feedback process: ensuring every host receives a clear creative jumping-off point, product familiarity, and structured ongoing feedback that improves their reads over time

• Owns the connection between creative output and market performance: working with Analytics and account teams to establish performance baselines and translate results into creative direction

• Owns a test-and-learn culture in partnership with Analytics: bringing creative hypotheses, making testing a standard part of how briefs are written, and ensuring what the team learns shapes the next round of work

• Owns the full creative team: leading and developing writers across Bespoke and Format tiers and producers across host-read and pre-produced disciplines

• Owns key client and talent relationships at the senior creative level: these relationships stay direct, not delegated

• Owns the department's presence in new business pitches: concept development, pitch decks, and demo work, including a repeatable three-ways-in approach (functional, emotional, and host-story angles)

• Owns creative support for bespoke, creator-first partnerships and 360-degree campaigns

• Does not own test design, statistical analysis, or tracking infrastructure; those sit within Analytics

• Does not own production cost, change-order pricing, or P those sit within Finance

Decision Rights

• Final decision-maker on creative quality: what ships and what does not, across all accounts and both production disciplines

• Owns how Audiolytics is applied, evolved, and integrated with compliance and performance data across the department

• Authority to direct the creative team across writing and production in service of quality and performance outcomes

• Owns casting, talent direction, and host feedback structures

• Owns creative concept and approach for new business pitches; coordinates with account leadership on pitch strategy and timing

• Escalates resource, capacity, and structural gaps to the Chief Executive Officer with recommendations

• Does not make unilateral commitments on media plans, client contracts, or agency pricing

What You'll Do

Pillar 1: Quality on Everything That Ships

•
Quality control, end-to-end: Own QC across all creative that ships. Review work in flight against a clear quality bar before it reaches a client. Close the feedback loop so direction reaches writers directly. Hold host-read and pre-produced work to the distinct craft standards each discipline requires.

•
Audiolytics as benchmark, not scorecard: Own how Audiolytics is used and where it goes next. Prevent the score from becoming the goal. Integrate it with compliance and performance data to produce real insight, and drive the automation that lets it scale without adding manual burden to writers.

•
Talent onboarding and feedback: Own how talent is onboarded, briefed, and coached. Ensure every host receives a clear creative jumping-off point, product familiarity, and structured ongoing feedback that improves their reads over time.

Pillar 2: Creative Tied to Performance

•
Creative performance and market outcomes: Own the connection between what ships and how it performs. Work with Analytics and account teams to establish performance baselines, then translate performance and Audiolytics data into creative direction so outcomes, not just compliance, shape decisions on every account.

•
Closing the loop: Ensure what the team learns in market changes how they write, cast, and coach. Every round of creative should start smarter than the last.

Pillar 3: Testing Built In

•
Test-and-learn culture: Foster a team that is curious about what is working, what is not, and why. Analytics owns statistical design and tracking infrastructure; this role brings the creative hypotheses and ensures what the team learns shapes the next brief.

•
Test-ready briefs: Make a clear hypothesis and planned variants a standard part of how briefs are written, so testing is part of the everyday process rather than a separate project.

Leading the Department

•
Team leadership and development: Lead and develop the full creative team across writing tiers (Bespoke and Format) and production disciplines (host-read and pre-produced). Shepherd the process from brief through talent-facing direction and production. Shape the team around the skills the department needs as it grows.

•
Key client and talent relationships: Serve as the senior creative point of contact for key clients and talent. These relationships remain direct, not delegated. Clients and hosts should know who owns the creative point of view on their business.

•
New business and pitch support: Own the department's presence in every pitch: concept development, decks, and demo work. Develop and maintain a repeatable three-ways-in approach (functional, emotional, and host-story angles) so account teams walk into every pitch with real creative options.

•
Bespoke and creator-first partnerships: Own creative support for bespoke, creator-first campaigns: the 360-degree work that links show content, social, newsletters, and onsite activation to a client's brand.

•
Agency direction: Surface new formats, offerings, and creative opportunities as they emerge from the work. Bring them to leadership with a clear point of view.

Operating Cadence

•
Weekly: QC review across active accounts with creative on the agenda; one-on-ones with Bespoke and Format writing leads and Producers; cross-functional check-ins with Compliance and Analytics on Audiolytics integration, performance outcomes, and the testing roadmap; pitch and new business support as it arises; ongoing talent feedback touchpoints

•
Monthly: Performance and test result review with Analytics; talent feedback loop assessment; pitch win rate and new business creative review

•
Quarterly: Creative department performance review with leadership; Audiolytics integration and automation progress; test-and-learn record review; team development and capacity assessment

What Success Looks Like

Quality

• Consistent creative quality across every account, with in-market creative meeting the 90% Audiolytics target

• A measurable shift away from Audiolytics-as-checkbox behavior, without losing substantiation or compliance discipline

• Fast turnaround on host-read work and fire drills without a drop in craft

Performance

• Performance baselines established on priority accounts within the first 90 days

• A growing share of active accounts with creative decisions informed by performance data and test results, not just Audiolytics compliance scores

• Measurable performance lift on accounts where creative direction changed based on results

Testing

• A meaningful share of active accounts running at least one creative test per quarter

• A shared test-and-learn record that the team actively uses when briefing new work

Leadership and Growth

• Client and talent satisfaction with the department's creative involvement and responsiveness

• Pitch win rate and the quality of creative options the team brings to new business

• A creative team that is developing, retained, and clear on what great looks like

Specific targets will be confirmed within the first 90 days, once performance baselines are established.

Key Performance Indicators

Creative Quality

• Audiolytics score compliance: percentage of in-market creative meeting the 90% target

• QC turnaround: creative reviewed before client delivery, not after, with no material exceptions

• Host-read turnaround speed on fire drills and standard requests, within defined SLA

Performance and Testing

• Share of active accounts with established performance baselines

• Share of active accounts with creative decisions informed by performance or test data, growing quarter-over-quarter

• Share of active accounts running at least one creative test per quarter

• Test-and-learn record adoption: frequency with which the shared record informs new briefs

Leadership

• Pitch win rate on new business opportunities where Creative is involved

• Creative team retention and development: direct reports growing in capability and remaining engaged

• Client and talent satisfaction with creative quality and responsiveness

What We’re Looking For

The strongest candidates will bring:

• 10 or more years of experience in creative leadership, with a track record of owning creative quality across multiple accounts or productions simultaneously

• Deep fluency in audio advertising: host-read, pre-produced, and bespoke formats; candidates with strong audio or podcast creative backgrounds are strongly preferred

• Demonstrated ability to connect creative decisions to measurable performance outcomes; comfort working with data, analytics teams, and test-and-learn frameworks as inputs to creative direction

• Experience leading and developing creative teams across writing and production disciplines; a coach and standard-setter, not just a practitioner

• Strong point of view on what makes audio creative work: clarity of message, authenticity of voice, structure that converts; able to articulate and transfer that standard to a team

• Experience owning or contributing to new business pitches: concept development, creative presentation, and demo work in high-stakes settings

• Comfort working directly with talent: onboarding hosts, providing structured feedback, and maintaining creative relationships at the senior level

• A bias toward ownership: someone who runs toward gaps, raises the standard without being asked, and holds the quality bar even under deadline pressure

What This Role Is Not

•
Not a hands-on copywriting role for every account. The ECD sets the standard, resources the team, and steps in personally on the highest-stakes work. Writing every script is not the job.

•
Not a testing infrastructure role. Analytics owns test design, statistical analysis, tracking, and reporting mechanics. This role owns what gets tested, why, and what the team does with the results.

•
Not a pricing or P&L role. Finance owns production cost, change-order pricing, and the margin conversation. Creative owns the work itself.

•
Not a media strategy or buying role. Those functions sit within Media. The ECD operates within the creative lane and coordinates with Media as needed.

Key Relationships

•
Chief Executive Officer: Direct reporting relationship; accountable for creative department quality, team performance, and strategic creative direction

•
President: Coordinates on agency-wide creative positioning, new business strategy, and client escalations

•
Analytics Team: Primary partner on performance data, Audiolytics integration, test design, and the test-and-learn record

•
Compliance Team: Coordinates on script substantiation, IO requirements, and the integration of compliance signal into creative coaching

•
Account and Client Growth Teams: Partners on pitch creative, client QBRs, and performance-based creative direction conversations

•
Creator Partnerships: Coordinates on bespoke, creator-first campaigns and 360-degree deal creative

•
Finance: Coordinates on production resource needs; does not own pricing or P&L

Why This Role Matters

Creative is not a cost center at Oxford Road. It is one of the primary drivers of whether clients get results and stay. Every script that ships without a clear value proposition, every host-read that lands flat, every campaign that cannot be connected to measurable outcomes is a missed opportunity to prove what this agency can do. The Executive Creative Director is accountable for ensuring that does not happen, consistently, across every account, not just the ones leadership is watching. A strong ECD means clients win faster, advocacy compounds, and new business is easier to win. Without it, the agency's creative output is only as good as whoever happened to review it last.

title: ​​Civil Design Engineer II/III - Hydraulics & Hydrology​
description:
Role Summary

As a ​Civil Design Engineer II/III - Hydraulics & Hydrology​, you will model the hydrology and hydraulics of utility-scale solar PV and battery energy storage sites and design the drainage that makes them buildable. H&H analysis shows where water goes on a site and shapes how the project is laid out, permitted, and constructed. Working with guidance from senior engineers, you will turn terrain, rainfall, and soils data into hydrologic and hydraulic models, drainage designs, and reports using tools such as HEC-HMS, HEC-RAS, AutoCAD, and Civil 3D, and coordinate with civil, structural, electrical, and environmental colleagues to deliver projects that bring more renewable generation onto the grid. As an employee-owner, you will share in the results of the work and help build a team where careful, well-documented engineering earns the trust of clients and colleagues.

Duties & Responsibilities

Core Technical & Functional Responsibilities

• Build hydrologic and hydraulic models in HEC-HMS, HEC-RAS, SWMM, or similar tools to evaluate existing and proposed drainage conditions on utility-scale solar PV and battery energy storage sites.

• Run 1D and 2D floodplain and flood-depth analyses in HEC-RAS 2D, FLO-2D, or similar software to inform array layout, equipment elevations, and setbacks.

• Calculate runoff, peak flows, and detention or retention requirements, and size culverts, channels, ponds, and other conveyance and storage features.

• Design site drainage, grading, and stormwater management features in AutoCAD and Civil 3D, and produce the supporting civil land development sheet sets.

• Prepare erosion and sediment control plans with supporting calculations.

• Prepare hydrology and hydraulic reports, drainage reports, and stormwater calculations for permitting submittals.

• Process terrain, rainfall, soils, and land cover data, using GIS where needed, to build model inputs.

• Evaluate, select, and apply standard H&H methods, adapt them for nonroutine site conditions, and bring unconventional problems to senior engineers for review.

Project & Portfolio Execution

• Lead small H&H studies or drainage designs, or defined portions of larger civil scopes, from kickoff through permitting or issued-for-construction.

• Help determine schedule and budget requirements for assigned H&H scope, and report progress and risks to the project lead.

• Assign tasks to and coordinate work with designers and discipline team members to complete assignments.

• Update models, calculations, and deliverables when site layouts or project inputs change.

Quality, Standards & Compliance

• Ensure analyses and designs comply with company, industry, and jurisdictional stormwater, floodplain, and drainage standards, practices, and codes.

• Follow Revamp QA/QC procedures, self-check models and calculations, and resolve review comments before issue.

• Document model assumptions, design storms, and data sources so reviewers, clients, and permitting agencies can verify the basis of design.

Collaboration & Communication

• Coordinate with civil, structural, electrical, and environmental staff so drainage design, flood findings, and site layouts align.

• Coordinate with clients, project managers, and subcontractors on project expectations, data needs, and design inputs.

• Attend project meetings and present H&H findings and recommendations for assigned work.

Additional Responsibilities

• Perform essential duties including meeting deliverables and deadlines.

• Perform additional related duties as assigned or directed.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering is required.

• Civil engineering design and drafting experience: typically 2+ years for Engineer II and 5+ years for Engineer III.

• Experience in the creation of civil land development sheet sets including grading, site drainage, and access road design.

• Ability to identify and solve complex problems.

• Effective verbal and written communication skills.

• Ability to be both creative and analytical.

• Detail-oriented and accurate.

• Efficient time management – handle multiple projects simultaneously and with minimal supervision including prioritizing, organizing, and planning effectively to meet all deadlines.

Preferred Qualifications

• EIT Certificate is preferred.

• Knowledge of GIS software tools desirable.

• Prior renewable energy project experience is desirable.

Benefits for Full-Time Positions

• Participation in Revamp’s Employee Ownership ESOP program.

• Competitive compensation with bonus.

• Full benefits package offerings including 99% employer-paid health, vision, life, and dental insurance.

• Medical, dependent care, and commuter FSA.

• Monthly health and wellness stipend.

• Attractive vacation, sick, and holiday pay.

• Paid parental leave.

• 401(k) savings plan with 100% match up to 6%, vested immediately.

• Paid volunteer time off and charitable donation matching.

About Revamp

Founded in 2016, Revamp is the premier employee-owned engineering design firm dedicated to advancing large-scale renewable energy projects. Our team is united by a shared commitment to accelerating the global energy transition and creating a workplace where talented people can make a tangible impact in the fight against climate change.

As employee-owners, we take pride in building a culture of collaboration, innovation, and accountability where every individual’s contribution drives both company success and personal growth. Revamp engineers have supported the design of more than 10% of the utility-scale solar generation capacity in the US since 2020, contributing directly to the renewable energy transformation.

So much more than just an engineering firm; we are a diverse, international team of artists, singers, dancers, pastry chefs, outdoor enthusiasts, animal lovers, travelers and problem-solvers who bring curiosity and creativity to everything we do. For more information, visit www.revamp‑eng.com.
