title: Senior Developer Relations, Twitter Brand Rep
description:
ABOUT SUPABASE

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers: Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search, all deeply integrated.



ABOUT THE ROLE

Developers decide what to build with by listening to people they trust, much of it on Twitter, where Supabase's community, launches, and competitors are all discussed in public. We want a senior DevRel leader who is already a known, trusted voice there, to be a brand ambassador for Supabase. You'll work alongside our New Media and DevRel teams and help shape how Supabase shows up in these conversations. We hire for the voice and following you already have.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Be a visible, trusted voice for Supabase on Twitter: post, reply, and join developer conversations daily.

 - Share sharp, useful content, from launches and tips to opinions on where building is going.

 - Represent Supabase at events, on podcasts, and in the wider developer community.

 - Bring developer feedback to engineering and product, and work with New Media, DevRel, and PMM on launches.
   


YOU MIGHT BE A GOOD FIT IF

 - You have an existing, engaged Twitter following. We'll look at who you talk to and how people respond, as well as follower count.

 - You have senior experience in DevRel, developer advocacy, or a similar developer-facing role.

 - You're credible with a technical audience and a strong writer with a distinctive voice.

 - You're comfortable representing a company publicly, on camera, on stage, and online.

 - High agency and self-directed.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Fully Remote
   
   We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

 - ESOP
   
   Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

 - Tech Allowance
   
   Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

 - Health Benefits
   
   Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

 - Annual Off-Sites
   
   Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

 - Flexible Work
   
   We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

 - Professional Development
   
   Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.
   
   


ABOUT THE TEAM

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

 - ~400 team members

 - 60+ countries

 - 20+ languages spoken

 - Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

 - 540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

title: Influencer Performance Creative
description:
About Eneba

At Eneba, we’re building an open, safe and sustainable marketplace for the gamers of today and tomorrow. Our marketplace supports close to 20m+ active users (and growing fast!), provides a level of trust, safety and market accessibility unparalleled to none. We’re proud of what we’ve accomplished in such a short time and look forward to sharing this journey with you. Join us as we continue to scale, diversify our portfolio, and grow with the evolving community of gamers.

 

About the team

Our influencer team drives revenue through partnerships with creators across multiple countries and game categories. The team handles lead generation, onboarding, relationship management and performance support. You’ll join as the specialist who makes the advertising creative behind those partnerships work harder.




About the Role

This role has two parts that feed into each other.

Creative: You’ll research what competitors and the wider market are doing, work out which creative solutions we can run, and turn that into a high volume of clear, usable creative briefs for influencers.

Performance: Once influencers run the briefs, you’ll own the performance side. You’ll set up A/B tests, track KPIs and work out which creative angles are driving results, then feed those insights back into the next round of briefs.

 

Responsibilities

 - Research competitor and market advertising to spot angles, formats and trends

 - Develop a high volume of creative angles and briefs for influencers

 - Tailor creative approaches by country, audience and game category

 - Review influencer content and give constructive feedback

 - Design and run A/B tests across creatives, markets and categories

 - Analyse creative performance using KPIs and structured testing, then adjust the approach based on what the data shows

 - Manage and optimise influencer advertising budgets, including YouTube spend

 - Use AI tools to analyse data, find patterns faster and improve your workflow

 - Report on creative impact to influencer managers, media buyers and leadership

 - Work closely with influencer managers, media buyers and creators

 

Requirements

 - Proven experience writing creative briefs

 - Strong skills in measuring and analysing campaign and creative results

 - Hands-on experience managing YouTube spend

 - Budget ownership, ideally managing 100,000+ per month in influencer marketing

 - Experience working closely with influencer teams, or running ads with influencers

 - Hands-on experience using AI tools in your daily work, particularly to analyse data

 - Good English level required, proficiency preferred



Nice to have 

 - A background in a B2C brand, B2C SaaS or consumer subscription company where influencers are a top marketing channel

 - Experience across multiple markets and countries

 - Experience in a business with a large content creator team (10+ people)







SALARY : €42,000 - €45,000 A YEAR

*Salary ranges may vary. We’re seeking candidates with varied experience levels; from individual contributors to functional leaders in this space.

*We’re an international team and our business language of choice is English. Good English level is required, proficiency is preferred.

 

What it’s like to work at Eneba


 - Opportunity to help scale a unique product.

 - Opportunity to join our Employee Stock Options program

 - Various bonus systems: performance-based, referral, additional paid leave, personal learning budget.

 - Paid volunteering opportunities.

 - Work location of your choice: office, remote, opportunity to work and travel.

 - Personal and professional growth at an exponential rate supported by well-defined feedback and promotion processes.

 
 

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

description:
👋 Hi there,

We're a small startup building AI-powered video tools for brands. We're looking for a designer who wants to work in a new way: you make the design decisions, and AI does most of the building.

Here, a good day isn't one polished video built by hand. It's ten good videos, where you set the look, direct the tools, judge every render, and fix what they got wrong. Product and UI animation, ad templates, social cuts, and launch videos, all from written creative briefs.

Make the design calls: type, layout, framing, color, and pacing. You decide what good looks like on each piece.

•

•
When the AI gets something wrong, open the After Effects project and fix it yourself.

•
When a tool falls short, write it up so we can fix the tool. Don't quietly work around it.

What we're looking for

•
A strong design portfolio. Layout, type, and color are your foundation, and you can explain your choices.

•
Working knowledge of After Effects. You can open a project, find the problem, and fix it. Motion design work on your reel is a plus, but this is a design role first.

•
You already use AI tools in your work and want to push them further: Claude, ChatGPT, Midjourney, Runway, Flow, Kling, or others. Tell us which ones and how. You'll learn Babou with us.

•
You care more about the result than the method, and you'd rather ship ten good pieces than one perfect one.

•
Written English good enough to work from briefs and give updates in Slack.

•
Nice to have: Figma, kinetic type, AI image and video tools, expressions.

How it works

•
Freelance, hourly, and remote. Paid for tracked time.

•
Your rate is yours to quote. Work the hours that suit you, including fully async.

Individuals only, no agencies or studios.

title: Staff Content Designer
description:
ABOUT US

Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.

Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes.

2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler.

We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.

Joining Legora means three things.

 - We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.

 - We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.

 - We grow together: as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.

The role

At Legora, we're building the category-defining AI product for legal work. Our users are lawyers. They read for a living and they notice every word. In an agentic product, words are most of the interface. Whether lawyers trust the product depends on getting that language right.

As our first Content Designer, you will own the verbal layer of Legora. You will set the standards and encode them into our design system and the judgment tools our designers and agents draw on.

This is a hands-on senior role. You will build the content design practice at Legora, working directly with product designers, PMs, engineers, legal engineers and our brand team.

This position can be based in Stockholm, NYC, or London.


What you will be doing

 - Define Legora's product voice and the principles behind it.

 - Design conversational and agentic experiences end to end: instructions, confirmations, progress updates, interruptions, handoffs, and how agents communicate results, sources and uncertainty.

 - Own naming and terminology across the product. Decide what things are called and keep the vocabulary consistent.

 - Write and shape in-product content with product designers on our highest-stakes surfaces.

 - Build content standards into how we work: design system guidelines, rules that automated PR checks can enforce, and guidance designers and agents can use on demand.

 - Make our agents into exceptional writers. Turn your judgment into instructions, examples and evals that coding and design agents follow, so on-voice copy is produced automatically and your time goes to the cases that need a human.

 - Partner with Brand and Product Marketing so the product sounds like the company that makes it.

 - Audit existing experiences and use customer feedback and product data to find where language is failing users.


Who you are

 - Extensive experience as a content designer or UX writer on complex, high-stakes software products.

 - You have designed conversational or AI-driven experiences.

 - Exceptional writing and editing, combined with systems thinking: you see the patterns behind individual strings and build the frameworks that keep them consistent at scale.

 - Comfortable in ambiguity and in a domain where you are not the expert. You know how to extract the right vocabulary from lawyers and legal engineers and make it usable.

 - Fluent in how modern product teams build. You use AI tools in your own workflow.

 - Experience working in code, comfort with docs-as-code, and writing and owning agent skill files.

 - You make the case for content decisions with evidence and get product, engineering and leadership behind them.

 - Experience managing high demand work flow from cross-functional teams, ability to project manage and set expectations for your own deliverables

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.

The role

At Legora, we're building the category-defining AI product for legal work. Our design team is growing fast across Stockholm, London and New York.

Design is being rebuilt for the AI era: new tools, new workflows, humans and agents building together, and a higher bar on both speed and craft. The Design Operations Manager is the operator who makes that change land at Legora. You will partner with design and product leadership to structure the org, set the operating rhythms and lead the cross-functional initiatives that free designers to spend their time on product and craft.

You own org structure, planning, prioritisation and the systems that keep everything moving. Your job is to make sure the right things happen at the right time, across every team.

You will report to the Head of Design. This is a hands-on senior role: you design the systems and you run them.

This position can be based in Stockholm, NYC, or London.


What you will be doing

 - Keep a live, accurate map of how design is organised against what it needs to deliver. Flag structural gaps before they show up as missed deadlines or duplicated work, and make sure every headcount decision has a clear rationale tied to what the team actually needs.

 - Own how design hires. Tie every open role to a named strategic priority before it is approved, agree the archetype and level before the loop starts, run the process end to end with our Talent team, and own onboarding and offboarding for designers.

 - Put design on a stable planning cadence and make reviews produce decisions and unblock work. Give design clear goals and bets that ladder to company-wide OKRs, and when priorities shift, make the tradeoffs visible so they get made on purpose.

 - Be the DRI for cross-team programmes and move them from vague problem to shipped outcome on a visible timeline. Product, Engineering and PMM should be able to see where design work stands at any point without asking.

 - Help move the team to more agentic ways of working and keep documentation and process current as they change. Track adoption and impact so the org can tell what is working from what is still an experiment.

 - Make sure a written quality bar exists for design work and gets applied consistently, and build the reporting that shows, cycle over cycle, whether speed gains are costing us quality, so that tradeoff gets decided early.


Who you are

 - 4–6+ years of experience running operations, programmes or a chief-of-staff function inside a product or design organisation, ideally through a period of rapid growth.

 - A track record of building org structures, planning cadences and hiring processes from scratch, and the judgment to know which ones earn their keep.

 - A systems thinker who is comfortable with ambiguity: you see the structural gap before it becomes a missed deadline, and you close gaps that are technically someone else's problem.

 - Fluent in how modern product teams build, and an early adopter of AI-native and agentic ways of working who brings others along.

 - A strong communicator who makes tradeoffs legible and gets product, engineering and leadership behind a decision.

 - Line management experience is a plus. Caring about design, and the people who do it, is required.

RELEX runs the planning decisions behind 700+ retailers and manufacturers worldwide, deciding, at real scale, what gets forecast, stocked, priced, promoted, and produced across the entire value chain. Few problems combine this much data, this much complexity, and this much real-world weight: get it right and a shelf stays stocked, a factory line doesn’t stall, food doesn’t rot in a warehouse before it’s sold. Get it wrong, and it shows up in actual losses, for some of the largest retail and manufacturing brands in the world.

We’ve grown for 76 consecutive quarters straight, and it’s accelerating: the first half of 2026 was the strongest in the company’s history, with new contract value up 83% year over year. We’re a team of 2,000+ people, headquartered in Helsinki, with offices across Europe, North America, and Asia-Pacific.

You will also have the support of Design Excellence community of 15+ designers across RELEX to share your craft and learn from your peers.

Our five values are our playbook. We speak up when things don’t make sense. We stop doing what doesn’t add value. We stay curious, back each other up, and make space for both innovation and laughter.

• Preliminary Substation Design and Technical Ownership

• Participate in routine client meetings to review technical exhibits, explain preliminary design assumptions, identify risks, and clarify requirements outside of SOLV standards.

title: Founding Designer (Brand, Web & Product)
description:
•
Location: Remote. US, UK or Europe; you'll need at least four working hours overlapping Mountain Time. The range below is for US-based candidates and is adjusted by location elsewhere.

•
Reports to: Growth lead, with regular meetings with the executive team for brand work.

About Breathe for Change

Breathe for Change is building the category of Human Intelligence in Education to address the crises of educator stress and burnout, student mental health, and AI disruption. Our accredited higher-education program, a Master of Science in Education in Transformative Teaching & Learning awarded by William Jewell College and accredited by the Higher Learning Commission, equips educators with the human skills they and their students need most to thrive. More than 20,000 educators in every U.S. state have come through our programs. We reach teachers through TeacherCon, our free three-day online event, through paid social, email and a podcast, and we enroll them through honest conversations with our Educator Development Counselors.

The role

You'll be our first design hire. You'll own how Breathe for Change looks everywhere a prospective student meets us, and you'll make it yourself: the website, the curriculum made visual, email, paid-social creative, event materials, brand. The heart of it is making a complicated thing legible: a 30-credit, three-semester master's and a five-layer Human Intelligence framework, explained visually, in a sequence a tired teacher can follow in one scroll.

This is a making role. You design in Figma and you build what you design, in Webflow, Framer or front-end code. Direction comes from our growth lead and our exec team; the craft, the system and the shipped work come from you. There is a mountain of hands-on design to do, and we'd rather hire one person who can do it beautifully than a director who can't.

Your first big project is already scoped: a refresh of our website, borrowing the clarity of the best program sites in education while keeping our brand. You design it. You build it. It's the fastest way for both of us to see what working together is really like.

Where it grows. We don't have a product engineering team yet, so product design here starts with the student-facing surfaces we already ship: onboarding, program materials, the theme and content of the learning platform our partner college provides, and the dashboards and AI tools our team runs on. The first one is student onboarding. As we build more of the student experience, you're the designer in the room from the start, and because you build, you'll ship a good deal of it yourself with AI-assisted tooling and our technology lead on the plumbing. It's not the core of the role, but the information design you do on the website becomes the design language for everything a student touches.

Three things to know about how we work, because they tell you whether this seat is for you:

You'd be making, not managing

We have agencies and freelancers who produce at volume, and a growth lead who sets direction. What we don't have is one person who can take a page from blank to shipped, or an email from brief to sent, and make it look like us. This seat is in Figma and the site builder most of the day.

We're small, flat and fast

The founders are still in the work. Decisions get made in a conversation, not a committee. You'll work with our co-founder, who is the voice and face of the brand, and with the people who run growth, enrollment and product. We use AI in nearly every workflow and expect you to as well.

We sell a regulated degree with integrity, structurally

Teachers are trust professionals and our buyers for life. Every public claim about the degree has to be exact: who awards it, what it costs, what it can and cannot promise. That's a design constraint, not a legal footnote, and the best work here makes the truth land harder than hype would.

What you'll actually do

•
Bring the brand and curriculum to life. Turn the program, the framework and the accreditation story into pages, sequences, diagrams and decks that a prospective student grasps at a glance. This is the core of the job.

•
Design and build the website. Sequence the story, design the system, build the pages (Webflow, Framer or code; you choose and make the case), ship, and iterate on what the data says.

•
Design email. Lifecycle and campaign email in HubSpot: templates, hero creative, the weekly sends that matter.

•
Design the ad-creative system. The visual language for paid social and the first batches yourself; our production partners scale it from there.

•
Design the student surfaces we ship. Starting with onboarding, then program materials and the learning platform's theme, with our product lead.

•
Carry the brand into everything. Event materials, decks, documents, internal tools. Shape headlines and copy as you design.

Who we're looking for

•
Someone who explains complicated things visually. You've turned a complex product, program or curriculum into a visual system people could follow: program pages, course maps, explainers, decks. We weight this at least as heavily as ad creative.

•
Someone who builds. You've shipped marketing websites you built yourself, in Webflow, Framer or code, and you can show us which parts you built.

•
A senior generalist. 7+ years designing for consumer brands, ideally with a stretch as the first or only designer somewhere, or a freelance practice with real clients.

•
Performance-literate. You've designed email and paid-social creative with the numbers in front of you, and changed what you made because of them.

•
Fluent in the tools. Figma, one site builder, basic video editing. Motion is a plus.

•
A writer by necessity. You can shape a headline and cut a paragraph in half, and you'd rather cut than add.

•
In the open. You show work early, ask for the number, and change your mind when the data says to.

Nice to have: you've designed customer-facing product surfaces (an app, a portal, an onboarding flow) and carried a brand into them. Education or mission-driven consumer experience. AI-native design and build workflows.

You do NOT need education-industry experience. We'll teach you the program, the audience and the rules. What we can't teach is taste and the ability to ship.

Growth

This is the first design seat at the company, and it grows with the work. As the engine scales, so does the team around you: production, video, and whoever else the work needs. You'd shape that from the inside, having built the system yourself first.

How we'll hire

A portfolio screen, a paid design-and-build exercise for finalists (a real page of ours, your sequence, one section built live; about six to eight hours, paid), and one conversation with the founders. We move in weeks, not months.

Compensation & benefits

•
Base salary: $130,000–$165,000 for US-based candidates, depending on experience and the depth of what you've shipped; adjusted by location elsewhere

•
Stock options

•
Health, vision and dental insurance

•
401k and FSA/HSA eligibility

•
Unlimited PTO

How to apply

The application asks for three live sites you built, one piece where you explained something complicated visually, one email or ad, and five sentences on what you'd cut from one of our pages. Those matter more than your résumé, and we read every answer.

Breathe for Change is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Compensation Range: $130K - $165K

title: Senior Lead Motion Designer
description:
Remote (US-based, Pacific hours) · Full-time · $105,000–$120,000 annually, DOE Applications accepted on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

About Red Door Collaborative

Red Door Collaborative is a creative agency serving enterprise tech organizations and SMBs with visual design, content, and motion work. We're a small, human-centered team — highly collaborative, quietly intense, and genuinely good at what we do. We're also evolving: AI is reshaping our industry, and we're leaning into it as a tool that enhances our work rather than replaces the people doing it. We're rooted in SoCal and the PNW, but we're a fully remote team of creatives. We work Pacific hours and meet in person rarely — this is a real remote role, not a "remote for now" situation. This role requires someone who can lead motion design with craft and conviction in a remote environment — directing a team of animators, representing the discipline to clients, and delivering work that moves without the benefit of being in the same room.

About the Role

We're hiring a Senior Lead Motion Designer to own motion design at Red Door — leading the discipline, setting the quality bar, and representing motion to our clients and prospects. In this role you'll lead a small team of full-time animators and a rotating group of individual collaborators, and you'll also get your hands into the work when capacity and complexity demand it. The split between directing and doing will flex with project load — this isn't a role where you've fully stepped back from the craft. But your primary responsibility is the discipline: the team, our standards, and the client relationships. On the client side, this role goes beyond execution. You'll be a key voice in how Red Door presents and sells motion design — identifying opportunities to expand motion work within existing accounts, articulating the value of motion in client conversations, and helping prospective clients understand what's possible. You'll report to our Associate Creative Director and work alongside Creative Project Managers, discipline leads in Visual Design and Content, and our small but mighty team of creatives delivering excellent work, day after day.

What You'll Do

•
Discipline leadership and mentorship: Lead, direct, and develop a team of animators and several contracted collaborators. Set expectations, give direct and constructive feedback, and establish what "excellence" looks like within the motion discipline. You're building a team that does great work consistently — not just when you're in the room.

•
Motion production: Stay hands-on with motion work when project load or complexity requires it. Create and direct animatics, motion graphics, branded motion pieces, and UI/interface animation to a high standard. Your work sets the bar your team reaches toward.

•
Creative direction and quality control: Review work across the motion discipline before it leaves the team. You're not checking boxes — you're evaluating whether the animation serves the client's intent, tells the story clearly, and clears our quality bar. Flag what needs another pass and explain why.

•
Client representation and motion evangelism: Be a credible, compelling voice for motion design in client-facing settings. Identify opportunities to expand motion work within existing accounts, participate in new business conversations, and help clients understand what motion can do for their marketing and communication needs. This is a material part of the role — not a secondary responsibility.

•
Creative standards and process: Establish and maintain creative standards, workflows, and production practices for the motion discipline. Partner with Creative PMs to keep motion work moving through production phases without losing quality. When standards drift, you bring them back.

•
Cross-discipline collaboration: Work closely with the ACD, CD, and other discipline leads (Visual and Content design). Motion doesn't live in isolation — you'll collaborate across disciplines on integrated projects and contribute to how Red Door's creative output comes together.

Who You Are

• You have 7+ years of professional motion design experience — creating animatics, motion graphics, and branded motion for real clients in a production workflow. Not adjacent to the work but doing it.

• You've led or mentored other animators or motion designers — this isn't a first-time leadership role. You've given hard feedback, helped someone develop their craft, and know what it takes to build a discipline that produces consistent work.

• You have agency experience — not adjacent to agency work but embedded in it. You know the pace, the client dynamics, and the particular pressure of delivering motion work on deadline.

• You have strong proficiency in Adobe After Effects and working familiarity with Cinema 4D, Maya, Premiere, and Frame.io. You don't need to be equally expert in all of them, but you understand the ecosystem and can speak to it credibly.

• You're comfortable in client-facing settings — presenting work, fielding questions, and identifying opportunities to expand the scope of what motion can do for a client. This isn't a stretch for you; it's energizing.

• You have a reel and portfolio that shows both your craft and your range — work you made, projects you directed, and examples that demonstrate how your motion thinking serves a client's communication goals.

• You've worked with enterprise clients — tech organizations, professional services, large-scale marketing campaigns. You understand the complexity, the stakeholder layers, and the long timelines that come with large clients.

• You have an open, growth-oriented mindset about AI and are curious about how AI-assisted tools and workflows might expand what your team is capable of. We're exploring this actively — we need someone who wants to be part of that exploration.

Before You Apply

Consider the following before applying:

• If you're at your best as an individual contributor, and leading and directing others' output feels like a step away from the work you love...

• If client conversations, presentations, and upselling motion design feel more uncomfortable than energizing...

• If you're looking for a role where creative standards are already set and your job is to execute within them, rather than establish and own them...

• If you haven't led other animators or motion designers and are looking for your first leadership role...

Then this probably isn't the right role for you.

To Apply

In your cover letter, tell us about a time you pushed a piece of motion work — yours or someone else's — to a level it wouldn't have reached without your involvement. What was the work, what did you see that needed to change, and how did you get there? We're more interested in how you think about craft and leadership than a polished answer. During the interview process, we'll ask you to walk us through your reel — not just what you made, but how you directed it, where you pushed back, and what you'd do differently. Finalists will be asked to provide references from animators or motion designers who've worked with them directly.

Compensation & Benefits

This is a salaried, exempt position with an annual salary of $105,000–$120,000, depending on experience. We offer a full benefits package: PTO, paid holidays, health coverage (medical, dental, vision — plus HSA/FSA options), 401(k) with match, life and disability insurance, a charitable matching program, and stipends to support your remote setup and ongoing work-from-home costs.

Equal Opportunity

Red Door Collaborative is committed to building an inclusive team where everyone is valued and respected. We don't discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other protected status. We don't just welcome diverse perspectives — we actively seek them out. People from different cultures and experiences, solving problems together, is how we do our best work.

About Pinterest:

Millions of people around the world come to our platform to find creative ideas, dream about new possibilities and plan for memories that will last a lifetime. At Pinterest, we’re on a mission to bring everyone the inspiration to create a life they love, and that starts with the people behind the product.

Discover a career where you ignite innovation for millions, transform passion into growth opportunities, celebrate each other’s unique experiences and embrace the flexibility to do your best work. Creating a career you love? It’s Possible.

At Pinterest, AI isn't just a feature, it's a powerful partner that augments our creativity and amplifies our impact, and we’re looking for candidates who are excited to be a part of that. To get a complete picture of your experience and abilities, we’ll explore your foundational skills and how you collaborate with AI.

Through our interview process, what matters most is that you can always explain your approach, showing us not just what you know, but how you think. You can read more about our AI interview philosophy and how we use AI in our recruiting process here.

Pinterest is looking for a thoughtful, highly skilled Staff Motion Designer to join the Design Innovation team. You will define and evolve the motion design language that brings clarity, coherence, and delight to Pinterest across surfaces and flagship features. This is a hands-on, horizontal role for a rare blend of motion craft leader, systems thinker, and design technologist. You will establish reusable motion principles, patterns, tokens, and implementation guidance within the design system; partner directly with product and engineering teams to solve challenging interaction problems; and build tools and prototypes that make it easier to explore and ship exceptional motion at scale. Your impact will extend from the details of a single interaction to the cohesive experience of Pinterest as a whole.

What you’ll do

• Define and evolve Pinterest’s motion design language – principles, interaction and transition patterns, timing and tokens, specifications, and guidance – so motion is intentional, coherent, accessible, and reusable across the product ecosystem.

• Lead motion direction for flagship and AI-forward experiences, using motion to clarify state, cause and effect, hierarchy, feedback, progress, and system responsiveness.

• Partner horizontally with product designers, engineers, product managers, researchers, and content designers to connect individual feature work to a shared motion strategy and raise the quality of shipped experiences.

• Turn high-craft explorations into scalable design system contributions that reduce ad hoc implementation, improve consistency, and enable teams to move faster with confidence.

• Rapidly prototype and validate motion ideas using the right medium – motion studies, design tools, code, AI-enabled tools, or custom prototypes – to create shared understanding and accelerate decisions.

• Work closely with engineering throughout implementation to solve technically ambitious animation challenges while balancing performance, platform conventions, accessibility, and maintainability.

• Develop or enable lightweight tools, templates, and workflows that help designers explore visual and motion ideas quickly and help engineering teams build sophisticated animations reliably.

• Stay at the leading edge of AI-enabled motion and visual-creation tools, applying them strategically to improve ideation, prototyping, and production while maintaining critical thinking, quality validation, and ownership of final outcomes.

• Conduct motion quality reviews, give actionable feedback on designs and implementations, and mentor designers in motion principles, systems thinking, prototype craft, and productive engineering partnership.

• Clearly articulate the rationale, tradeoffs, and user impact behind motion decisions to teams, leaders, and executives; build alignment around a high bar for motion craft and system quality.

What we’re looking for

• Minimum 8 years of experience in motion design, product design, interaction design, or a closely related discipline, with a portfolio demonstrating exceptional motion craft in shipped digital products or platforms.

• A staff/principal-level track record of influencing horizontally across teams, shaping a product or design-system direction, and raising quality without relying on formal authority.

• Deep command of motion and interaction design principles, including timing, choreography, easing, spring behavior, feedback, and transitions – and strong judgment about when motion improves usability, comprehension, emotion, and trust.

• Experience creating or materially evolving scalable motion systems, such as principles, token sets, pattern libraries, documentation, tooling, and governance that teams can adopt across products and platforms.

• Demonstrated experience partnering closely with engineers to implement complex motion; practical fluency in performance, technical constraints, platform conventions, handoff, and quality assurance.

• A design technologist mindset: comfortable using prototyping tools, AI, and code or technical workflows where useful to explore ideas, communicate intent, and improve how teams design and build.

• Strong product and systems thinking: able to connect craft decisions to user needs, product strategy, accessibility, implementation efficiency, and measurable impact.

• Excellent communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to synthesize ambiguity, create clear documentation, facilitate constructive critique, and align diverse cross-functional partners.

• A collaborative, low-ego working style with a passion for learning, experimentation, mentoring, and inclusive design. You consider reduced-motion preferences, cognitive load, and diverse user needs from the beginning of the design process.

• Bachelor’s degree in design, animation, human-computer interaction, a related field, or equivalent experience.

Bonus Points For

• Experience defining motion for AI, conversational, multimodal, or other emerging product experiences.

• Experience contributing to platform-wide design systems, public motion systems, or open-source animation libraries.

• Experience building designer-facing or engineer-facing tools that improve motion prototyping, handoff, or implementation quality.

Pinterest is looking for a Sr. Staff Qualitative Researcher to lead research in our highest-priority ads areas. We are looking for a seasoned researcher who can embed in complex, ambiguous problem spaces, uncover the advertiser and Pinner needs that matter most, and turn them into a clear learning agenda. In this role you’ll bring deep qual and mixed methods experience (as needed) to design, execute and communicate strategic research to senior stakeholders in the Ads org and beyond. You’ll shape strategy by partnering with Product, Design, and Engineering and presenting insights and written POVs directly to senior leadership. You’ll also help us decide where sustained research investment is needed, set direction for large cross-team research efforts, and mentor other researchers to raise the bar for qualitative craft. In this role, you’ll have ownership of a broad problem space, autonomy to set and execute your research agenda, and real influence over the ads roadmap and the holistic Pinner experience.

What you’ll do:

• Lead high-impact qualitative research in our most strategic ads areas: Embed in one or two high-priority problem spaces and own the full research cycle from discovery through execution, delivery, and influence on product decisions.

• Uncover and represent complex advertiser and user problems: Identify the deep, ambiguous customer needs that cut across the ads product, and translate them into clear opportunities for the business.

• Shape the research agenda: Work with Product, Design, Engineering, Data Science, and quantitative UX Research to scope and prioritize the questions that matter most for the areas you support, and independently identify where research can have the greatest impact.

• Choose the right method for the question: Plan, field, and synthesize research using the full range of qualitative methods, and partner with Data Science and quantitative researchers on mixed-methods studies that combine depth with scale.

• Influence strategy and roadmap: Partner with PMs and Designers to deliver informed, actionable recommendations, and communicate insights directly to leadership to help shape product direction. Author written POVs and cross-study syntheses that connect findings into a bigger picture.

• Assess where sustained research investment is needed: Evaluate whether an area warrants a long-term research presence, and make the case to leadership for where to invest.

• Use AI to amplify your craft:. Bring creativity to how you apply AI tools to research workflows and to how you land learnings, making cross-functional collaboration faster and more effective.

• Provide vision and direction for large collaborative efforts: Lead cross-team research initiatives across the ads organization (and as needed across ads and consumer orgs), setting direction and aligning partners around a shared point of view.

• Mentor and raise the bar: Coach and develop other researchers, and elevate qualitative craft across the team.

What we’re looking for:

• Minimum 7 years of experience in qualitative or mixed-methods user research, with a track record of leading research at a staff or senior staff level in a product organization, ideally in ads, marketplaces, or B2B/B2C platforms.

• Deep expertise across the qualitative toolkit. Fluency in interviews, ethnography, diary studies, usability testing, concept testing, and other methods, with sound judgment about which approach best fits the question, timeline, and decision at hand.

• Experience in mixed-methods research. Demonstrated success partnering with Data Science and quantitative UX Research to combine qualitative depth with quantitative scale, and to triangulate findings across data sources.

• Demonstrated ability to influence product strategy and roadmap supported by strong storytelling and recommendations that can drive action

• Strong executive communication skills and comfort presenting insights, written POVs, and recommendations to senior leaders (Sr. Directors +) and cross-functional partners, and tailoring the message to the audience.

• Ability to thrive in ambiguity and take an unstructured, high-urgency problem space, define the right questions, and build a learning agenda with minimal direction.

• Strong strategic judgment and decision quality to assess where research will have the greatest impact, prioritize accordingly, and make a clear case for where sustained investment is (or isn’t) warranted.

• Proven ability to collaborate with PMs, Designers, Engineers, Data Scientists, and quantitative researchers, and to build trust and credibility across disciplines.

• Experience leading large, collaborative research efforts with proven ability to set vision and direction across teams, align stakeholders around a shared point of view, and drive complex initiatives to completion.

• Curiosity and creativity in using AI tools. Enthusiasm for applying AI to research workflows, from synthesis to storytelling, to work faster and land insights in more compelling ways. Working knowledge of standard AI based research tools and capabilities preferred.

• Familiarity with ads (preferred). Understanding of advertiser needs, ad ecosystems and challenges is a plus, though not required.

• Bachelor's degree in a relevant field, or equivalent experience.

title: Agentic Experience Designer
description:
Does this position interest you? You should apply –even if you don’t match every single requirement! We're known as an auto glass company. That's the focus of what we do. But beyond the glass, we're so much more. We'll help you build a fulfilling career and encourage you to have a life. Let us be the best place you'll ever work.

Does this position interest you? You should apply – even if you don’t match every single requirement! We're known as an auto glass company. That's the focus of what we do. But beyond the glass, we're so much more. We'll help you build a fulfilling career and encourage you to have a life. Let us be the best place you'll ever work.

A Brief Overview
We are building the next generation of how customers, clients, and colleagues interact with Safelite, with agentic AI creating new possibilities for how people access services, make decisions, and engage with us.

We are seeking an Agentic Experience Designer to define how intelligent experiences work across Safelite. You will design how people express intent, how agents interpret and respond to it, how experiences adapt to context, and how interaction moves across conversation, voice, interface, and human support.
Reporting to the Director of Product Design, you will work alongside product management and engineering on the teams building these experiences, shaping the product from early exploration through production and continuous improvement.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role for a designer who wants to define interaction models for an emerging class of products and establish what excellent agentic experience design looks like at Safelite.

What you will do

Design agentic experiences

•
Design end-to-end experiences that allow customers, clients, and colleagues to express intent and interact naturally with intelligent systems.

•
Define how experiences move across conversation, voice, visual interfaces, structured inputs, and system actions based on the needs of the interaction.

•
Design how agents interpret intent, gather context, clarify ambiguity, make recommendations, confirm decisions, take action, and communicate outcomes.

•
Account for the complexity of real interactions, including changing intent, incomplete information, interruption, correction, repeat engagement, and exceptions.

•
Design beyond the interaction itself, connecting the agent experience to the underlying service, operational process, and outcome.

Design agency, control, and trust

•
Establish clear interaction models for what an agent can understand, recommend, decide, and act on.

•
Design appropriate levels of customer control based on context, confidence, consequence, and risk.

•
Create experiences that communicate uncertainty and limitations clearly without placing the burden of navigating the system on the user.

•
Design escalation and human intervention as part of the experience, preserving context and continuity across transitions.

•
Integrate transparency, consent, and explainability into the experience in ways that support trust without introducing unnecessary friction.

Define interaction patterns for intelligent experiences

•
Establish reusable patterns for agentic, conversational, adaptive, and multimodal experiences across Safelite.

•
Explore new interaction models made possible by systems that can interpret context, generate responses, take action, and adapt over time.

•
Partner with design system teams to integrate agentic patterns into Safelite’s broader experience system.

•
Codify principles and patterns as the organization learns, creating a foundation that becomes stronger with each implementation.

AI-Enabled Experience Optimization

•
Use AI-native tools to analyze customer interactions at scale, identify patterns, surface emerging issues, and uncover opportunities to improve agent behavior and experience quality.

•
Move between patterns across thousands of interactions and individual conversations to understand where intent, agent behavior, and outcomes diverge.

•
Use AI to form and investigate hypotheses, identify root causes, and determine where changes to the agent or experience can have the greatest impact.

•
Combine conversation intelligence, behavioral data, research, and evaluation to develop a clear point of view on what should change and why.

•
Partner with product and engineering to translate those insights into improvements, then evaluate how those changes perform in live interactions.

•
Create a continuous feedback loop where AI helps us understand and improve the AI-enabled experiences we put into the world.

Performs other duties as assigned

Complies with all policies and standards

Qualifications

•
Bachelor's Degree or equivalent work experience

•
4-6 years of product design, interaction design, UX design, conversation design, content design, or related experience.

REQUIRED SKILLS AND ABILITIES

• 5+ years of product design, interaction design, UX design, conversation design, content design, or related experience.

• Demonstrated experience designing conversational, AI-enabled, adaptive, or intelligent products that have been used in production.

• Strong interaction design capability across conversation, interface, information architecture, and complex service experiences.

• Strong content judgment and the ability to make sophisticated interactions clear, concise, and natural.

• Advanced fluency in Figma and experience contributing to scalable design systems.

• Demonstrated fluency using AI throughout the design process, including discovery, synthesis, exploration, prototyping, evaluation, and optimization.

• Experience using AI-native tools to analyze customer interactions, investigate agent performance, test hypotheses, and identify opportunities for improvement.

• Experience working with agent evaluation, simulation, experimentation, or observability tools to understand how intelligent experiences behave in production.

• Experience working in continuous discovery and delivery environments where evidence from live experiences informs what comes next.

• Comfort working directly with transcripts, behavioral data, analytics, research, and evaluation results.

• Strong partnership with product management and engineering, with experience jointly shaping product direction, interaction models, and outcomes.

• Ability to bring structure and design judgment to emerging problem spaces where established patterns may not yet exist.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

•
Experience spanning interaction design and content or conversation design.

•
Experience designing both customer-facing and colleague-facing AI experiences.

•
Understanding of agentic systems, including models, context, retrieval, tool use, memory, orchestration, guardrails, and evaluation.

•
Experience creating functional prototypes using AI-enabled development and prototyping tools.

•
Experience with AI-native conversation intelligence, agent evaluation, simulation, or optimization tools.

•
Experience designing voice and multimodal interactions.

•
Experience designing accessible conversational, adaptive, or voice experiences.

CORE CAPABILITIES

•
Agentic Interaction Design. Defines interaction models that connect intent, intelligence, interface, action, and outcome.

•
Design for Uncertainty. Designs explicitly for probabilistic systems, variable confidence, ambiguity, and exceptions.

•
Agency and Trust. Makes system capability, customer control, and consequential actions understandable and intentional.

•
AI-Enabled Experience Optimization. Uses AI to understand interaction patterns at scale, identify opportunities, and continuously improve agent behavior and experience quality.

•
Multimodal Design. Determines how conversation, voice, interface, and structured interaction work together as one experience.

•
Systems Thinking. Establishes reusable principles and patterns that scale across products and use cases.

•
Product Partnership. Shapes product direction alongside product management and engineering from problem definition through production.

•
AI Fluency. Understands the capabilities and constraints of intelligent systems and uses AI directly across design, prototyping, evaluation, and optimization.

•
Execution Discipline. Moves emerging concepts into production while maintaining experience quality and coherence.

TARGET EXPERIENCE

•
We are looking for a designer who has worked at the intersection of interaction design and intelligent systems.

•
You have designed and shipped conversational, AI-enabled, adaptive, or agentic experiences and learned from how they perform in the real world. You understand that agentic experience design extends beyond conversation. It requires designing the relationship between intent, context, intelligence, interface, action, control, and the service being delivered.

•
You are comfortable working in environments where the system is probabilistic, the interface may adapt, and the appropriate interaction cannot always be represented as a predetermined flow.

•
Experience with service journeys is particularly relevant. At Safelite, a digital interaction often initiates or influences something that ultimately happens in the physical world.

•
Relevant experience may come from conversational AI, customer engagement platforms, applied AI teams, marketplaces, on-demand services, travel and hospitality, home services, modern automotive experiences, or other organizations building intelligent digital products.

What You Will Get:

•
Competitive weekly pay and bonus opportunities.

•
Total job benefits valued at more than $10k*. This includes a 401(k) plan with company matching, medical coverage plans customized to suit your needs and a commitment to work/life balance through our paid time off (PTO) programs, company holidays and paid volunteer days.

•
Up to $5,250 in tuition reimbursement per year.

•

Our client is a fast-growing eCommerce company in the Patient Care space with a large presence in the Home Medical Equipment (HME) and Durable Medical Equipment (DME) niche. They are seeking a highly experienced professional to fill an immediate full-time remote Senior Product Designer/Industrial Designer opening.

As the Senior Product Designer/Industrial Designer, you will lead the design and development of next-generation patient care products - from concept through production - translating caregiver feedback, customer reviews, and competitive insights into profitable, manufacturable solutions with exceptional ergonomics, usability, and functional detail.

﻿This is a full-time, remote independent contractor position.

About the company:

The company is a purpose-driven provider of Patient Care products dedicated to enhancing the lives of patients and caregivers. With thousands of positive reviews and a passionate, diverse team from around the globe, the company prides itself on creating products that are not only well-designed but genuinely useful. Customer obsession is a guiding principle that shapes the company's strategy, culture, and decisions.

The company's mission is centered on improving well-being through meticulous attention to detail and continuous listening to customer feedback, ensuring that its solutions meet real caregiving needs. Its vision is to empower patients and caregivers with innovative products that improve quality of life. The company also values caring customer service, professional growth, work-life balance, and a supportive environment where team members can thrive and contribute to meaningful product impact.

This is a Full-Time | Fully Remote position reporting to the Project Manager.

Key Responsibilities:

• Lead the end-to-end design process from concept development to production-ready solutions, ensuring all designs go through rigorous DFM (Design for Manufacturing) and DFA (Design for Assembly) analysis.

• Translate internal product briefs, caregiver feedback, VOC data, and customer reviews into innovative, user-centered product concepts.

• Apply deep materials knowledge to select the most suitable materials that balance aesthetic with structural durability and cost-efficiency.

• Create advanced CAD models and detailed technical design and engineering documentation, utilizing FEA (Finite Element Analysis) and structural simulations to validate mechanical integrity and performance before prototyping.

• Design and validate mockups, prototypes, and functional test samples.

• Collaborate closely with engineers, sourcing partners, and marketing to balance creativity with cost targets, supplier capabilities, and timelines.

• Optimize design-to-prototype cycle times and improve design efficiency.

• Maintain high standards of manufacturability, functional performance, and customer satisfaction (targeting 4.5+ product ratings).

• Communicate effectively with international manufacturing partners, including Asian/China suppliers.

Expected Outcomes:

• Deliver 4–6 fully engineered, manufacturable product designs within the first 3 months.

• Develop final production-ready samples of 12–18 new SKUs by the end of 2026.

• Achieve 30% contribution margin in design cost modeling.

• Optimize and meet quarterly design-to-prototype cycle time targets within the first 6 months.

• Implement a structured, user-driven design process for top legacy products within 12 months.

• Establish and maintain a repeatable, scalable design documentation system.

Qualifications:

• 3+ years of experience in Industrial Design or Product Design.

• 2+ years designing mass-produced consumer, HME, or DME (patient care) products.

• Experience taking products from concept to mass production.

• Experience in mechanical design, prototyping, simulation, and testing.

• Experience working within manufacturing and supplier constraints.

• Experience communicating and collaborating with Asian/Chinese manufacturers.

• Experience designing products for marketplaces influenced by public customer reviews.

• Experience with mechanical CAD software, such as SolidWorks, Inventor, Onshape.

• Experience with cost modeling and margin-focused design decisions.

• Strong analytical skills with the ability to structure qualitative and quantitative insights into actionable design improvements.

• Deep understanding of ergonomics, usability, and user-centered design principles.

• Close attention to detail and commitment to excellence.

• Proactive problem-solver with a strong ownership mindset.

• Excellent cross-functional collaboration and communication skills.

• High adaptability and ability to thrive in a fast-scaling environment.

Attention to Detail – Nothing slips through the cracks.

title: Product Designer (Human-Centered)
description:
Company Overview

Voted #1 EHR by PC Mag, WRS Health delivers a fully integrated cloud based EMR and practice management solutions to its clients. We bring solutions to physicians by providing constant enhancement of our products and services including EHR, practice management, marketing, patient coordination and billing.

Job Overview

We are seeking a Human-Centered Design (HCD) Engineer to bridge the gap between user needs and technical execution. You will lead qualitative research, map user journeys, build interactive prototypes, and run usability tests to ensure our products are intuitive, accessible, and impactful for the physicians, clinical staff, billers, front-desk teams, and patients who rely on them every day. In a clinical setting, a confusing screen costs a provider time, adds to burnout, and can affect patient safety, so this role carries real weight. You will thrive here if you love sitting with users in their actual workflows, can turn messy observations into clear direction, and can defend design decisions with evidence.

Key Responsibilities

User Research

• Conduct contextual inquiries, interviews, field observations, and surveys with physicians, clinical staff, billers, and patients to uncover explicit and latent needs.

• Partner with account managers and support teams to surface usability pain points from client feedback and support tickets.

Synthesis & Strategy

• Translate research into personas, journey maps, service blueprints, and system workflows across clinical, operational, and billing processes.

• Present insights to product and executive leadership to shape roadmap priorities.

Ideation & Prototyping

• Facilitate cross-functional design workshops and build low- to high-fidelity wireframes and interactive prototypes in Figma, Sketch, or Adobe XD.

• Design AI-powered features (AI charting, AI agents) that keep clinicians in control and make AI output easy to review and correct.

Usability Testing

• Plan, moderate, and analyze formative and summative usability tests to iterate on designs before and during development.

• Evaluate safety-critical workflows such as medication management and e-prescribing, and support ONC Safety-Enhanced Design testing.

Collaboration & Governance

• Partner with product managers, business analysts, and engineers in Agile/Scrum teams to maintain design integrity from concept through release.

• Uphold accessibility standards (WCAG, Section 508) and HIPAA-safe research practices across all products.

Leadership

• Build and scale WRS Health's HCD practice, including research operations, templates, and standards.

• Mentor designers and researchers, and coach teammates on human-centered methods.

Qualifications

Required

• Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Human-Centered Design, Human-Factors Engineering, Interaction Design, Cognitive Psychology, or a related field.

• Experience: 3 to 6+ years of professional experience in HCD, UX design, or user research, including enterprise or regulated-industry experience.

• Technical Skills: Proficiency in prototyping software (Figma, Sketch, or Adobe XD), qualitative research methodologies, usability testing frameworks, and Agile/Scrum delivery flows.

• Accessibility: Working knowledge of Section 508 and WCAG standards and how to apply them in practice.

• Core Competencies: Strong empathy, verbal storytelling, analytical problem-solving, and the ability to defend design decisions with data.

• A portfolio or case studies demonstrating end-to-end research, synthesis, prototyping, and measurable impact.

Preferred

• Experience designing for EHR, practice management, revenue cycle, telehealth, or other health IT products.

• Familiarity with clinical workflows and terminology across ambulatory specialties.

• Knowledge of ONC Safety-Enhanced Design (user-centered design and summative testing) requirements, NISTIR 7804, or ISO 9241-210.

• Experience designing AI-assisted or automation features, including human-in-the-loop review patterns.

• Prior experience leading or mentoring designers/researchers, or building a design function from the ground up.

• Experience with remote research and unmoderated testing tools and product analytics platforms.

• Clinical background or prior work in a medical practice setting.

A Day in the Life

Your days move between the field, the whiteboard, and the prototype. You might start by joining the product team's stand-up to flag a research insight affecting an upcoming sprint, then sit in (virtually or on-site) with a specialty practice to watch how the front desk, medical assistants, and physicians actually work, noting the workarounds they've built and where the screens slow them down. Later, you could be synthesizing those observations into an updated journey map, facilitating a workshop with product managers, engineers, and billing specialists to sketch solutions, or moderating a usability test of a new AI charting feature to see how a clinician reviews and trusts AI-drafted notes. Before the day ends, you refine prototypes in Figma based on what you learned, check designs against accessibility standards, share prioritized recommendations with product leadership, and make time to coach the designers and researchers on your team.

Success Metrics

• Measurable usability gains: Improved task success rates, time-on-task, error rates, and System Usability Scale (SUS) scores for redesigned workflows, including fewer clicks and less documentation time for key clinical tasks.

• Research-driven roadmap: Consistent monthly contact with users across specialties, with a clear, visible share of roadmap items originating from or validated by HCD research.

• Fewer usability issues post-release: Decline in usability-related support tickets, rework, and post-launch design defects.

• Accessibility and certification compliance: New and updated features meet WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA and Section 508 standards at release, and ONC Safety-Enhanced Design documentation is completed on time.

• Adoption and satisfaction: Higher feature adoption (including AI features) and improved client satisfaction or NPS for redesigned areas.

Job Details

• Job Type: Full-time | Independent Contractor

• Location: Remote

• Hours: Must be available during standard US business hours (9:00 AM – 5:00 PM EST or 8:30 AM – 4:30 PM EST)

Compensation will be based on location, experience, and qualifications.

This job description outlines the general responsibilities of the role and is not exhaustive. Additional duties may be assigned as needed to support business operations.

WRS Health is an equal opportunity employer.

title: UX/UI Designer
description:
About Life Science Connect
Life Science Connect is a B2B media and data company serving the life sciences industry. We publish 15 industry websites and their email newsletters (including Bioprocess Online, Cell & Gene, Clinical Leader, Outsourced Pharma and Pharmaceutical Online), run sponsor-facing products such as Storefronts and supplier directories, and operate RFP Navigator, a platform for managing biopharma outsourcing RFPs. We are modernizing the user experience across all of it, and we are using AI to change how our content and data reach readers and clients.

The role
We're hiring our first dedicated UX/UI designer. You'll be a design partner to product, not only an executor of requirements: you'll help imagine and shape new experiences, products and interfaces for both our readers and our customers, then turn them into finished, buildable designs across web, email and SaaS. You'll work day-to-day with our Senior Product Manager, Audience & Data, alongside engineering, editorial and commercial teams.

The role starts as a 1099 contract as soon as possible, at about 22–28 hours a week. We plan to convert to a full-time position in Q1 2027. We're looking for someone who wants the full-time role. The contract start gets us working together sooner.

What you'll work on first

•
Website UX across 15 sites. For our move to a new CMS, we have core page templates and a design system in Figma, and the matching components are already built in our Storybook component library on Chromatic. You'll redesign, refine and extend them: a sponsored "Related Content" sidebar for article pages, sponsor Storefront microsite pages, and a searchable supplier directory with tiers and filters. Then you'll roll the changes out across all 15 site themes.

•
Email newsletter system. Design a modular email system and theme it into about 26 newsletter templates (editorial, sponsored and personalized "matched for you" sends). It has to render in Outlook, Gmail and Apple Mail, and work with mobile stacking, dark mode and images off.

•
RFP Navigator. A UX refresh of our B2B SaaS platform for two audiences: drug developers who issue RFPs and the CDMOs and CROs who answer them. This covers the marketing site, onboarding and the core RFP workflows.

Next on the roadmap: interactive AI content experiences (research content you can ask questions of), personalized on-site and reader-agent experiences, and self-service data products for clients.

What you'll do

• Partner with product to brainstorm and shape new experiences, products and interfaces for readers (the life science professionals who use our sites and newsletters) and customers (the sponsors and clients who buy our marketing, data and platform products).

• Turn PM requirements, briefs and rough prototypes into wireframes and high-fidelity Figma designs: desktop, tablet and mobile, with all states (empty, loading, error, logged-in vs anonymous).

• Present options and iterate with the PM, usually two or three review rounds per page type.

• Work within the existing design system (Figma plus our Storybook component library in Chromatic): reuse what's already built, and add new components back to the shared library.

• Spec designs for developers: layout, spacing, type, color tokens, interactions, responsive rules, content and data rules, accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) and analytics events.

• Answer developer questions and review built pages against the designs before release.

• Use AI tools to move faster, and help the team adopt them.

What you bring (required skills)

• About 5–7 years of professional UX/UI design experience.

• A portfolio that shows work in at least two of these three areas: B2B SaaS or web application UX, content or media websites, and email or newsletter design.

• Strong Figma skills, including working inside another team's design system.

• Responsive design and clean developer handoff.

• Practical knowledge of email design constraints: client rendering, mobile stacking, dark mode and image-off fallbacks.

• Working knowledge of accessibility (WCAG 2.x AA).

•
AI fluency: you already use AI tools in your design workflow and can show how.

• You're a self-starter. You take direction, work independently and communicate progress without being chased.

• You can present your thinking clearly to product, editorial and commercial stakeholders.

Nice to have

• Mobile app UX.

• HTML/CSS, especially for email. We have engineers to build, but it helps if you can carry a design closer to code or a working prototype.

• Life sciences, B2B publishing or media experience.

• Data products, dashboards, or AI and conversational interfaces.

• Designing against a coded component library (Storybook / Chromatic).

How we work

• Remote, with a weekly working session with the PM plus reviews as needed.

• Figma for design, specs and handoff, plus shared tools for tickets and feedback.

•
Life Science Connect owns all work product.

We do not offer visa sponsorship for this role.

title: UX/UI Designer, Design Systems Consultant (AI-Fluent)
description:
Please note, this posting is to highlight joining Right Side Up's talent collective specifically and is not representing an internal full-time role, or a current opportunity with a client.

Right Side Up is a collective of premium marketing talent, with all of the marketing chops, and none of the agency fluff. We're trusted by the most respected early-stage ventures, the fastest-growing tech companies, and well-established Fortune 500 teams to do one thing better: growth. We have over 1,400+ clients including Stitch Fix, Sephora, Yelp, Sun Basket, Crunchbase, DoorDash, Calm, and more.

About the Role

We're seeking freelance UX/UI Designers who specialize in design systems to help our clients modernize their systems for a world where humans and AI tools build side by side. Some companies call this a Design Engineer or Systems Designer; we're using UX/UI Designer, Design Systems here because it's the clearer, more searchable term for what this role actually is: a design role, not a software engineering one. This role sits at the intersection of design systems craft and AI fluency: someone who's equally comfortable untangling a token architecture in Figma and configuring the AI-tooling connections (MCP and similar) that let coding assistants read and respect that system instead of guessing at it. Contract projects typically range from ten to forty hours per week, depending on client needs and project scope, and often run as focused, timeboxed engagements rather than open-ended retainers.

Responsibilities

•
Audit existing design systems for structural gaps: tokens versus variables, component architecture, and missing or outdated documentation.

•
Resolve foundational issues (naming, token structure, variable setup) so a design system translates cleanly into documentation and code, without introducing breaking changes for engineering.

•
Build and maintain design system documentation, covering components, patterns, usage guidelines, and variant rules, in a structured format built for AI-fluent workflows and legible to both humans and AI tools.

•
Configure and maintain AI-tooling connections between design platforms (Figma, documentation platforms) and AI coding or design assistants (Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, Figma Make, GitHub Copilot, and similar), often via MCP-style integrations.

•
Extract undocumented institutional knowledge from designers and engineers and turn it into clear, actionable documentation.

•
Establish or refine governance models, contribution workflows, and success metrics so a design system stays healthy after the engagement ends.

•
Collaborate closely with design and engineering stakeholders, translating between the two without needing to write production code.

•
Stay current on evolving AI-assisted design and design-to-code workflows as the tooling landscape shifts.

Requirements

•
Strong experience in design systems, UX/UI design, or design engineering, with real depth at the foundational level (tokens, variables, component architecture), not just visual component work.

•
Genuine, hands-on fluency with AI-assisted design or coding tools, and enough technical comfort to configure AI-tooling connections rather than just use them.

•
Strong written communication skills. A lot of this work is turning tribal knowledge into documentation other people (and AI tools) can actually rely on.

•
Comfortable working independently on defined, timeboxed engagements with light day-to-day oversight.

•
Adaptable to different company environments, including regulated or compliance-sensitive ones where design-to-production handoffs stay manual by design.

Tools & Platforms

•
Figma, including Dev Mode, variables, and component architecture.

•
Design system documentation platforms: zeroheight preferred, with Supernova, Backlight, Frontify, or similar also valued.

•
AI-assisted design and coding tools: Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, Figma Make, GitHub Copilot, and other MCP-compatible platforms.

•
Familiarity with how design tokens map into code (CSS variables, JSON tokens, Style Dictionary-style pipelines) is a plus.

Why Right Side Up

Join a team that values expertise, flexibility, and meaningful work with some of the most innovative brands in the world.

Exciting opportunities are available now, apply today to join our network of experts!

title: Creative Technologist
description:

Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.



What you'll do

In one sentence: build the front-end surfaces and the AI-generation systems that let Lovable’s brand team produce at scale without losing its taste.

 - Build pipelines connecting image/video generation APIs, internal tooling, and the systems brand and marketing already use (Lovable, Design tools, CMS, the marketing site, Slack)

 - Build internal apps for the brand team - plausibly on Lovable itself, which is both a good dogfooding story and just the fastest way to do it

 - Own reliability and versioning for the AI-generation system so brand output doesn't silently drift in quality or style over time

 - Work closely with a Brand Designer who owns taste and direction - you're building the system that lets their judgment scale, not just executing tickets

 - Constantly evaluate new models, APIs, and generation tooling as the landscape moves, and rebuild pipelines when something better comes along



What we're looking for
